title: On the Geometric Structure of Hyperbolic Clifford Bundles and Associated Spin Groups
summary: In this paper, we present the spinor structure associated with the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra of a real $n$-dimensional vector space $V$, which is denoted by $\mathcal{C}l\left(H_{V}\right)$. Unlike the standard Clifford algebra, the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathcal{C}l(H_V)$ simultaneously accommodates both multiforms and multivectors in a single algebraic structure, making it the natural framework---known as the ``mother algebra''---for the study of superfields in theoretical physics and for generalizing the Clifford bundle formalism to hyperbolic structures arising in gravitational theories. The orthogonal groups and orthogonal transformations associated to the hyperbolic space $H_{V}$ are presented. The Clifford--Lipschitz group and the Pin and Spin groups associated with $\mathcal{C}l\left(H_{V}\right)$ are defined. Then, the frame bundle and spinor structure associated to Hyperbolic Clifford algebra is derived.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra Cl(H_V) as a unified 'mother algebra' hosting both multiforms and multivectors, constructs its associated orthogonal, Pin, Spin, and Clifford–Lipschitz groups, and derives the corresponding frame bundle and spinor structure for applications in superfield theory and hyperbolic gravitational geometries.
AI.motivation: To provide a natural algebraic framework—termed the 'mother algebra'—that unifies multiforms and multivectors for modeling superfields in theoretical physics and generalizing Clifford bundle formalism to hyperbolic structures in gravitational theories.
AI.method: Constructs the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra Cl(H_V) over an n-dimensional real vector space V; defines associated orthogonal groups, Clifford–Lipschitz group, and Pin/Spin groups; derives the frame bundle and spinor structure from Cl(H_V).
AI.result: A fully developed spinor structure tied to Cl(H_V), including explicit definitions of orthogonal transformations, Pin/Spin groups, and the associated frame bundle, establishing Cl(H_V) as a coherent algebraic foundation for hyperbolic geometric physics.
AI.conclusion: The Hyperbolic Clifford algebra Cl(H_V) serves as a unifying 'mother algebra' enabling consistent spinor calculus and bundle-theoretic formulations in hyperbolic settings—particularly relevant for superfield theory and gravitational models with indefinite signature.

title: A hybrid quantum-classical lattice kinetic scheme with tensor-train feedback for incompressible flows
summary: Nonlinear lattice kinetic simulation requires each updated distribution to supply the velocity and gradients that determine the next step. In a quantum-classical solver, reading out the full distribution incurs work proportional to the lattice size. We construct a tensor-train (TT) interface that retains reusable classical cores at the physical amplitude scale for a full-relaxation lattice kinetic scheme. The cores supply nonlinear coefficients and prepare each quantum input. Energy-scaled propagation and coordinate recovery encode the updated distribution, and alternating least-squares reconstruction converts signed Hadamard-test overlaps into output cores by restoring a known normalization factor. The next step starts from accepted cores without replaying previous quantum evolution. Under positive, unit-sum reference coefficients, positive lower and finite upper density bounds, and Lipschitz equilibrium sensitivity, perturbation bounds relate local defects to feedback errors. Resource bounds account for classical operations, circuit execution, sampling, and verification. Classical diagnostics expose why distribution accuracy alone is insufficient: in 80-step feedback on a $16\times16$ grid, rank cap 4 nearly eliminates the vortex despite a final distribution error below $1\%$, whereas rank cap 12 gives relative velocity error $1.03\times10^{-3}$. Four-step binomial readout simulations show that tightening core sampling tolerance threefold raises the prescribed sufficient budget from $5.97\times10^{12}$ to $5.37\times10^{13}$ shots as the result approaches the fixed-rank, fixed-sweep exact-overlap trajectory. The interface therefore provides a way to connect quantum propagation to nonlinear feedback and to assess the separate demands of compression, velocity accuracy, and readout precision.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a tensor-train (TT) interface for quantum-classical lattice kinetic simulations, enabling efficient nonlinear feedback without full quantum state readout; it provides perturbation and resource bounds, and demonstrates trade-offs among TT rank, distribution accuracy, velocity fidelity, and sampling budget in vortex simulation.
AI.motivation: To overcome the prohibitive cost of reading out full quantum distributions in nonlinear lattice kinetic simulations—where each step depends on velocity and gradient information—and to enable reusable classical representations that support feedback without re-executing quantum circuits.
AI.method: Constructs a TT interface that maintains classical cores at physical amplitude scale; uses energy-scaled propagation and coordinate recovery to encode updated distributions; employs alternating least-squares reconstruction from signed Hadamard-test overlaps, restoring normalization; avoids quantum replay by initializing next steps from accepted TT cores; derives perturbation bounds under positivity, unit-sum, density bounds, and Lipschitz equilibrium sensitivity.
AI.result: Demonstrates on a 16×16 grid that low-rank TT (rank cap 4) suppresses vortices despite <1% distribution error, while rank cap 12 achieves relative velocity error 1.03×10⁻³; shows binomial readout sensitivity: tightening sampling tolerance 3× increases required shots from 5.97×10¹² to 5.37×10¹³; establishes resource bounds covering classical ops, circuit execution, sampling, and verification.
AI.conclusion: The TT interface enables scalable quantum-classical coupling for nonlinear kinetic simulation by decoupling compression, velocity accuracy, and readout precision—providing both theoretical guarantees and empirical diagnostics for feedback-aware quantum simulation design.

title: Eigenstates on $O^\ast$-algebras with an application to ladder operators
summary: Following some recent results, we consider here a particular class of states on a $O^\ast$-algebra $\M$ which we call {\em eigenstates of an element} $A\in\M$, and we deduce some of their properties. Then, we apply our definition to a family of ladder elements, i.e. elements of $\M$ obeying certain algebraic (commutation) relations which are physically motivated, and we discuss several results for these states

AI.tldr: This paper introduces and studies 'eigenstates of an element' on an $O^*$-algebra, analyzes their properties, and applies the concept to physically motivated ladder elements satisfying commutation relations.
AI.motivation: To extend the notion of eigenstates beyond Hilbert space operators to a more general algebraic setting—specifically $O^*$-algebras—and to explore implications for quantum systems with ladder-type structures.
AI.method: Definition and analysis of eigenstates for elements of an $O^*$-algebra; application to ladder elements obeying specific commutation relations; derivation of structural and spectral properties.
AI.result: Establishment of key properties of eigenstates in the $O^*$-algebra framework; characterization of such states for ladder elements, including existence, uniqueness, and behavior under the given commutation relations.
AI.conclusion: The eigenstate concept is meaningfully generalizable to $O^*$-algebras, yielding physically interpretable results for ladder systems, thereby enriching algebraic quantum theory and operator algebras.

title: An Excursion into Grassmannian Spectra
summary: We revisit the classical spectral problem for the Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators on complex Grassmannians. After reviewing the standard approach based on non-commutative harmonic analysis, we develop two complementary methods originating from the quantization of the corresponding one-dimensional sigma model, both with and without a magnetic monopole field. The first is based on $\mathbf{SU}(n)$-equivariant first-order GLSM formulation and gives explicit eigenfunctions in terms of projectors and Plücker coordinates. The second uses a spin-chain realization of free particles on manifolds and describes the space of square-integrable functions, or sections in the magnetic case, through limiting tensor products of long rectangular $\mathbf{SU}(n)$ representations. Together, these approaches provide a more explicit picture of the spectral geometry of Grassmannians and clarify the relation between harmonics, Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and Laplacian spectra.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits the spectral problem of Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators on complex Grassmannians using two novel quantization-inspired methods—SU(n)-equivariant GLSM and spin-chain tensor product limits—yielding explicit eigenfunctions, clarifying links among harmonics, Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and spectra.
AI.motivation: To provide a more explicit and geometrically transparent understanding of the spectral geometry of complex Grassmannians, beyond standard non-commutative harmonic analysis, particularly in relation to magnetic monopole fields and representation-theoretic structures.
AI.method: Two complementary quantization-based methods: (1) an SU(n)-equivariant first-order gauged linear sigma model (GLSM) yielding eigenfunctions expressed via projectors and Plücker coordinates; (2) a spin-chain realization modeling free particles on the manifold, describing L²-functions (or holomorphic sections in the magnetic case) as limiting tensor products of long rectangular SU(n) representations.
AI.result: Explicit construction of eigenfunctions for Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators; unified description of harmonic analysis on Grassmannians linking Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and spectral data; clarification of how representation-theoretic limits encode geometric spectra.
AI.conclusion: The two quantization-motivated approaches deepen the spectral geometric understanding of complex Grassmannians, bridging sigma-model physics, equivariant geometry, and representation theory—offering new computational tools and conceptual insights into harmonic analysis on homogeneous spaces with magnetic fields.

title: Lorentz-Invariant Measure for Path Integrals in the Future Cone
summary: We construct a measure on continuous paths in the future cone of two-dimensional space that is invariant under the orthochronous Lorentz group and quasi-invariant under the action of the diffeomorphism group. We use the proposed measure to obtain the fundamental solution of the heat equation. The result agrees with the expression obtained by other methods.

AI.tldr: Constructs a Lorentz-invariant, diffeomorphism-quasi-invariant path measure on 2D future light cones and uses it to derive the heat kernel, matching known results.
AI.motivation: To develop a geometrically natural, relativistic path measure compatible with Lorentz symmetry and smooth reparametrizations, enabling rigorous functional-integral derivation of fundamental solutions to relativistic or causal PDEs.
AI.method: Constructs a probability measure on continuous timelike paths in the 2D future light cone that is invariant under orthochronous Lorentz transformations and quasi-invariant under diffeomorphisms of the path parameter; applies this measure to compute the fundamental solution (heat kernel) via path integration.
AI.result: The derived fundamental solution of the heat equation coincides with established analytical expressions, validating the consistency and correctness of the proposed path measure.
AI.conclusion: A well-defined, symmetry-adapted path measure on causal domains exists and successfully reproduces standard PDE solutions, supporting its use in relativistic stochastic analysis and quantum field-theoretic path integrals.

title: An exact unstable mode of self-similar Yang--Mills solutionsin 5+1 dimensions
summary: Self-similar solutions play an important role in the formation of singularities in the Yang--Mills equations. In five space dimensions, these equations admit infinitely many self-similar solutions with an increasing number of unstable modes. It was observed numerically that all excited profiles share the least unstable eigenvalue $\lambda=5$. We explain this remarkable spectral property by an elementary construction of the corresponding eigenfunction in terms of the profile.

AI.tldr: The paper explains why all excited self-similar solutions of the Yang–Mills equations in five dimensions share the same least unstable eigenvalue λ = 5, via an explicit, elementary construction of the associated eigenfunction from the profile.
AI.motivation: To explain the numerically observed universality of the least unstable eigenvalue λ = 5 across infinitely many excited self-similar solutions of the Yang–Mills equations in five dimensions.
AI.method: Elementary analytical construction of the eigenfunction corresponding to the eigenvalue λ = 5 directly from the self-similar profile.
AI.result: A closed-form eigenfunction is derived that confirms λ = 5 is always the least unstable eigenvalue for all excited self-similar profiles, independent of their node number.
AI.conclusion: The spectral degeneracy at λ = 5 is not accidental but follows from an intrinsic symmetry-like structure encoded in the profile, revealing a hidden universality in the linear stability spectrum.

title: Multiplicity and parity in Hirota's $N$-soliton conditions: the bilinear families $L\,(D_x^{3}+Λ)^{2n+1}$
summary: Hirota's three-soliton condition is the standard test for the integrability of a bilinear equation $P(D)f\cdot f=0$, and the folklore implication ``three-soliton condition $\Rightarrow$ $N$-soliton solutions for all $N$'' underlies the classifications of Hietarinta. We study this implication in two directions. The first is the family $L\,(D_x^3+\Lambda)^{2n+1}f\cdot f=0$ with $L$, $\Lambda$ linear forms in the Hirota operators, which for $n=0$ contains the Korteweg--de Vries, Ito and Boiti--Leon--Manna--Pempinelli equations and for $L=D_x$ is the family of Gürses and Pekcan. On the principal component of the dispersion variety the $N$-soliton condition reduces to a sign sum of two bialternants; counting odd exponents shows that for $n=0$ the class is Hirota integrable and that for $n\ge1$ the three-soliton condition holds for every $L$, and an explicit formula for the four-soliton residual proves the Gürses--Pekcan conjecture that the four-soliton condition fails for every $n\ge1$. The formula yields sum-of-squares certificates excluding four-soliton solutions at every real configuration for the Gürses--Pekcan and Ito equations, classifies the real members of the class, and determines maximal numbers of nondegenerate solitons: exactly four or five for $n=1$ according as $L$ lies in the span of $D_x,\Lambda$ or not, five for $n=2$ and $L=D_x$, and finite for every $n\ge1$ and every $L$. The second direction is a reformulation of the implication for a single non-hyperplane component of multiplicity one, which we prove, with complete classifications, for all graph-type dispersions $L(q(D)+D_t)$, for every irreducible even quadric component in any dimension and with an arbitrary cofactor, for parabolic components, for the dispersions $F(\ell)+Q$ containing the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili surface, and, with a prescribed one-parameter phase family, for the cubic graph.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the validity of the folklore implication that satisfying Hirota's three-soliton condition guarantees existence of N-soliton solutions for all N, focusing on two classes of bilinear PDEs: a family generalizing KdV-type equations and graph-type dispersions; it proves the implication fails for n ≥ 1 in the first family (explicitly computing the four-soliton residual), classifies real integrable cases, determines maximal nondegenerate soliton numbers, and establishes the implication under specific geometric conditions on dispersion varieties.
AI.motivation: To rigorously test the widely assumed but unproven implication 'three-soliton condition ⇒ N-soliton solutions for all N' in Hirota's bilinear method, especially for generalized integrable PDEs beyond classical cases like KdV.
AI.method: Algebraic analysis of the Hirota bilinear form on the dispersion variety; reduction of the N-soliton condition to sign sums of bialternants on principal components; explicit computation of the four-soliton residual; classification via dispersion variety geometry (e.g., irreducible quadrics, parabolic components, graph-type dispersions); use of sum-of-squares certificates to exclude real four-soliton solutions.
AI.result: For the family (D_x^3 + Λ)^{2n+1} f·f = 0: (i) three-soliton condition holds for all n ≥ 0 and all L, Λ; (ii) four-soliton condition fails for all n ≥ 1 (confirming Gürses–Pekcan conjecture); (iii) explicit four-soliton residual yields sum-of-squares certificates excluding real four-soliton solutions for Gürses–Pekcan and Ito equations; (iv) maximal nondegenerate solitons are exactly 4 or 5 (n=1), 5 (n=2, L=D_x), finite for all n≥1. For graph-type and other dispersions, the three-⇒N implication is proven under specified geometric conditions.
AI.conclusion: The folklore implication is false in general: three-soliton condition does not entail full integrability (N-soliton solutions for all N). Its validity depends critically on the algebraic-geometric structure of the dispersion variety—specifically, on component type, multiplicity, and configuration—and can be established only for restricted classes such as irreducible even quadrics, parabolic components, or certain graph-type dispersions.

title: High-order compact ALE gas-kinetic scheme on three-dimensional unstructured meshes
summary: In this paper, a compact high-order gas-kinetic scheme (HGKS) is developed for compressible arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) computations on three-dimensional unstructured meshes. To achieve high-order spatial accuracy, a large number of matrix inversions are required for spatial reconstruction. In ALE computations, the mesh moves and the geometric information must be recalculated at each time step, which reduces computational efficiency. To improve efficiency, a memory-reduction reconstruction strategy is employed to construct a quadratic polynomial on unstructured meshes. By differentiating the candidate polynomial, the quadratic terms are obtained by the least-squares method using the average gradient values of the cell itself and its neighboring cells. The linear terms of the polynomial are also determined by the least-squares method. On three-dimensional unstructured meshes, a $3\times3$ coefficient matrix must be stored, and four least-squares procedures are required to construct a quadratic polynomial. To suppress numerical oscillations in flows with discontinuities, generalized essentially non-oscillatory (GENO) reconstruction and a gradient compression factor are adopted. To accelerate the computation, a multi-GPU accelerated code is implemented using Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) and Message Passing Interface (MPI). The current scheme is fully explicit, and the acceleration framework can be developed based on cell-level parallelism. Numerical examples are presented to evaluate the accuracy and robustness of the scheme, including flows with strong discontinuities, pitching wings, and helicopter rotors. Numerical results confirm the excellent performance of the compact ALE scheme on unstructured meshes.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a compact high-order gas-kinetic scheme (HGKS) for 3D unstructured ALE simulations, using memory-efficient least-squares reconstruction for quadratic polynomials, GENO limiting, gradient compression, and multi-GPU acceleration via CUDA+MPI.
AI.motivation: To overcome computational inefficiency in high-order ALE simulations on unstructured meshes—caused by repeated matrix inversions and geometric recalculation due to mesh motion—while maintaining accuracy and robustness for discontinuous flows.
AI.method: Introduces a memory-reduction reconstruction strategy: constructs a quadratic polynomial via four least-squares procedures (using cell and neighbor average gradients); employs GENO reconstruction and gradient compression for shock capturing; implements fully explicit multi-GPU acceleration using CUDA for cell-level parallelism and MPI for inter-GPU communication.
AI.result: The scheme achieves high-order spatial accuracy with reduced memory footprint (only 3×3 matrices stored per cell); demonstrates excellent accuracy, robustness, and efficiency on benchmark problems including strong discontinuities, pitching wings, and helicopter rotor flows.
AI.conclusion: The compact HGKS is a computationally efficient, scalable, and robust high-order method for 3D unstructured ALE simulations, particularly suitable for complex moving-boundary problems on GPU clusters.

title: Rasterization-based discontinuous integration on the GPU
summary: In this paper, we propose a method based on rasterization in computer graphics for the integration of discontinuous functions accurately and efficiently on the GPU. The proposed method takes advantage of the massively parallel architecture of GPUs via a modified graphics pipeline, where discontinuities are encoded through geometric primitives and processed in the rasterization stage, and multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) is used to improve integration accuracy across subdomain interfaces. We present both hardware- and software-based pipelines and compare their performance in terms of accuracy as well as computational effort on modern GPU hardware with adaptive quadrature on the CPU. For the tested hardware, at approximately comparable median relative error, the hardware pipeline is up to around $100\text{x}$ faster than adaptive quadrature, while the single- and double-precision software pipelines achieve up to $840\text{x}$ and $1200\text{x}$ speedups compared to their adaptive quadrature counterparts. We use the finite cell method as model problem, where cutcells represent discontinuous integrands at the interface of the physical and fictitious domains and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method using numerical benchmarks. The end-to-end finite cell solution runtime is reduced by a factor of $8.3$ to $9.5$ in the single-precision pipeline and by a factor of $62$ to $72$ in the double-precision pipeline at the prescribed integration settings. Therefore, results indicate that the rasterization-based integration method is a promising alternative for the accurate and efficient integration of discontinuous functions in demanding applications on the GPU.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a rasterization-based GPU method for accurate and efficient integration of discontinuous functions, leveraging GPU parallelism, geometric encoding of discontinuities, and MSAA for accuracy—achieving up to 1200× speedup over CPU adaptive quadrature in double-precision software mode, with end-to-end finite cell method speedups of 8.3–72×.
AI.motivation: Accurate and efficient numerical integration of discontinuous functions—especially in high-performance computing contexts like the finite cell method—is computationally expensive on CPUs; GPUs offer massive parallelism but lack native support for adaptive integration near discontinuities.
AI.method: A rasterization-based integration framework using modified graphics pipelines: discontinuities are encoded as geometric primitives (e.g., cutcell boundaries), processed during GPU rasterization, and integrated with multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) to resolve subdomain interface errors; both hardware-accelerated and software-emulated (e.g., OpenGL/Vulkan-based) pipelines are implemented.
AI.result: At comparable median relative error, hardware pipeline achieves ~100×, single-precision software ~840×, and double-precision software ~1200× speedup over CPU adaptive quadrature; end-to-end finite cell runtimes reduced by 8.3–9.5× (single-precision) and 62–72× (double-precision).
AI.conclusion: Rasterization-based integration is a highly competitive, scalable, and accurate alternative for GPU-accelerated integration of discontinuous integrands—particularly beneficial in embedded high-order methods like the finite cell method.

title: Non-local approximations for the Schrödinger operator with a general point interaction via the non-relativistic limit
summary: We consider the one-dimensional Dirac operator $D_{A,c}$ with a general, not necessarily self-adjoint, point interaction at the origin, whose strength is described by an arbitrary complex $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ and suitably rescaled by the speed of light $c$, together with its non-local approximations $D_{A,c}^{\epsilon}$ obtained by replacing the Dirac distribution by a rank-one projection onto a scaled function $v_\epsilon$. It is known that $D_{A,c}^\epsilon \to D_{A,c}$ as $\epsilon\to 0+$ and that $D_{A,c}-c^2/2$ converges, as $c\to+\infty$, to the Schrödinger operator $H_A$ with the general point interaction, both in the norm resolvent sense. We prove that the first convergence is uniform with respect to $c$ in a neighbourhood of $+\infty$, and we provide explicit rates of convergence. Combining this with an explicit computation of the non-relativistic limit of $D_{A,c}^\epsilon$ for fixed $\epsilon$, we show that the two limits can be interchanged and that the corresponding double limit exists. As a by-product we obtain a family of non-local, rank-two approximations $H_A^\epsilon$ of $H_A$ that converge to $H_A$ in the norm resolvent sense. Contrary to the relativistic setting, the coupling constants of $H_A^\epsilon$ are renormalized; we give an explicit formula for this renormalization.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence behavior of approximations to a one-dimensional Dirac operator with a general point interaction, proving uniformity and interchangeability of the non-relativistic (c→∞) and approximation (ε→0) limits, and deriving explicit convergence rates and renormalization formulas for associated Schrödinger approximations.
AI.motivation: To rigorously justify the interchange of two limiting procedures—approximation of singular point interactions (ε→0) and the non-relativistic limit (c→∞)—for the Dirac operator, and to construct and analyze physically meaningful non-local approximations of the limiting Schrödinger operator.
AI.method: Norm resolvent convergence analysis; explicit resolvent kernel computations; uniform convergence estimates in c near infinity; asymptotic expansion of resolvents; derivation of renormalized coupling constants for rank-two Schrödinger approximations.
AI.result: Uniform norm resolvent convergence of D_{A,c}^ε to D_{A,c} as ε→0+, valid uniformly for large c; existence and equality of iterated limits lim_{c→∞}lim_{ε→0+} and lim_{ε→0+}lim_{c→∞}; construction of a family H_A^ε of rank-two non-local Schrödinger approximations converging to H_A; explicit renormalization formula for the coupling constants of H_A^ε.
AI.conclusion: The two limiting processes—regularization of the point interaction and passage to the non-relativistic regime—are compatible and commutative in the norm resolvent sense, with quantifiable rates; the resulting Schrödinger approximations require coupling constant renormalization, which is explicitly characterized.

title: Dynamical Properties of the Multiple Elastic Pendulum
summary: This article studies the dynamical properties of the multiple elastic pendulum formed by an arbitrary number of point masses connected in a chain by elastic springs. First, using the Lagrangian formulation, the equations of motion governing the system's behavior, accounting for both large-angle displacements and elastic deformations, are derived. It is shown that well-established, low-dimensional systems, such as the classical double elastic pendulum, can be systematically recovered as particular cases directly from the general equations of motion after applying the appropriates particular conditions. The behavior of the system under small oscillations near its stable equilibrium is also investigated. For this case, the linearized equations allow the solution of the eigenvalue problem, demonstrating that in this case uncoupled behavior between the angular displacements and the spring elongations.

AI.tldr: This paper derives general equations of motion for a multi-mass elastic pendulum chain using Lagrangian mechanics, recovers known low-dimensional cases (e.g., double elastic pendulum) as limits, and analyzes small oscillations revealing uncoupled angular and spring modes.
AI.motivation: To establish a unified dynamical framework for arbitrarily many masses connected by elastic springs—generalizing classical elastic pendula—and to understand how dimensionality reduction and linearized behavior emerge from the full nonlinear model.
AI.method: Lagrangian formulation is applied to derive exact nonlinear equations of motion incorporating large-angle rotations and finite spring deformations; systematic reduction to special cases (e.g., double elastic pendulum) is performed via constraint imposition; linearization about stable equilibrium yields an eigenvalue problem for modal analysis.
AI.result: General equations of motion are obtained; low-dimensional systems are recovered as exact limiting cases; linearized analysis shows complete decoupling between angular displacements and spring elongations under small oscillations.
AI.conclusion: The multi-elastic-pendulum system admits a coherent theoretical structure wherein complexity reduces systematically to known models, and its small-amplitude dynamics exhibit intrinsic mode separation—angular and extensional motions evolve independently.

title: An Exact QFT/Lattice Map for Fermions
summary: We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions. This map rewrites a continuum Hamiltonian as a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and an infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space. The resulting lattice model reproduces exactly the energy spectrum, global operator algebra, chiral symmetries, and anomalies of the continuum QFT on any finite lattice. Unlike domain wall fermions, truncating the local Hilbert space introduces no extra massless modes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval converges as the truncation is removed. The lattice local algebras are of type I and lie between the type III continuum algebras of nested spatial regions, in accordance with the split property. We demonstrate this construction explicitly for $N$ Majorana fermions, realizing the $\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{L}\times\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{R}$ lattice chiral symmetry. We also construct an exact lattice model for the Schwinger model and numerically reproduce the mass gap $e/\sqrt{\pi}$.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs an exact mapping from continuum fermion fields to lattice fields in 1+1D, yielding a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space that exactly preserves spectrum, symmetries, anomalies, and operator algebra; truncation yields controlled errors (no spurious massless modes, convergent entanglement entropy), and the construction satisfies the split property by interpolating between type I (lattice) and type III (continuum) algebras.
AI.motivation: To resolve longstanding tensions between lattice regularization and continuum QFT structure—particularly preserving chiral symmetries, anomalies, and entanglement properties without introducing unphysical degrees of freedom (e.g., doublers or extra massless modes) common in conventional discretizations like Wilson or domain wall fermions.
AI.method: Exact unitary embedding of continuum fermionic Fock space into a tensor product of infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces on a 1+1D spatial lattice; uses mode expansion and operator-algebraic techniques to construct local lattice operators replicating continuum symmetries and dynamics; applies truncation analysis and numerical simulation (for Schwinger model) to verify convergence and physical observables.
AI.result: An explicit exact lattice representation for N Majorana fermions with O(N)_L × O(N)_R chiral symmetry and anomaly matching; exact lattice Schwinger model reproducing the analytically known mass gap e/√π numerically; proof that truncated models eliminate spurious massless modes and yield convergent interval entanglement entropy; demonstration that local lattice algebras are type I and satisfy the split property relative to type III continuum algebras.
AI.conclusion: Exact continuum-to-lattice mapping is feasible in 1+1D with physically faithful, symmetry- and anomaly-preserving discretization; provides a rigorous framework for non-perturbative lattice studies of chiral QFTs while respecting algebraic quantum field theory principles, bridging discrete regularization and continuum structure.

title: Boundary $c\leq1$ Liouville CFT from the Bootstrap
summary: We construct boundary Liouville conformal field theory at central charge $c\leq1$ with FZZT-type boundary conditions and show that it satisfies the Cardy--Lewellen sewing constraints on the disk and the annulus. Using the analytic bootstrap we derive the so far missing boundary three-point and bulk-to-boundary structure constants and a consistent disk one-point function as explicit meromorphic functions of the Liouville momenta. In sharp contrast to $c\geq25$, the open-string spectrum between two ``timelike'' FZZT boundaries is \emph{discrete}, yet non-trivially consistent through open-closed duality with the \emph{continuous} closed-string spectrum of Ribault and Santachiara.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs boundary Liouville CFT at c ≤ 1 with FZZT boundaries, verifies Cardy–Lewellen sewing constraints, and uses analytic bootstrap to compute new boundary three-point and bulk-to-boundary structure constants; it reveals a discrete open-string spectrum between timelike FZZT boundaries—consistent via open-closed duality with the continuous closed-string spectrum.
AI.motivation: To complete the understanding of boundary Liouville CFT at central charge c ≤ 1—particularly lacking explicit boundary structure constants and consistency checks for FZZT-type boundaries—and to resolve the tension between discrete open-string spectra and continuous closed-string spectra in the timelike regime.
AI.method: Construction of boundary Liouville CFT with FZZT boundary conditions; verification of Cardy–Lewellen sewing constraints on disk and annulus; application of analytic bootstrap to solve for boundary three-point functions, bulk-to-boundary structure constants, and disk one-point functions as meromorphic functions of Liouville momenta.
AI.result: Explicit meromorphic expressions for boundary three-point and bulk-to-boundary structure constants; consistent disk one-point function; proof that open-string spectrum between two timelike FZZT boundaries is discrete; confirmation of consistency with Ribault–Santachiara’s continuous closed-string spectrum via open-closed duality.
AI.conclusion: Boundary Liouville CFT at c ≤ 1 with FZZT boundaries is fully consistent, and the apparent discrepancy between discrete open and continuous closed spectra is resolved by open-closed duality—establishing a robust non-perturbative framework for timelike Liouville theory.

title: Nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild black holes for the Einstein-massless Dirac system in spherical symmetry
summary: In this paper, we establish the nonlinear stability of the Schwarzschild exterior for the spherically symmetric Einstein-massless Dirac system. More precisely, we consider sufficiently small perturbations of Schwarzschild characteristic initial data and prove that the corresponding maximal development remains globally controlled in the exterior region (orbital stability), and converges, in a suitable teleological double-null gauge, to a Schwarzschild spacetime with a final mass (asymptotic stability). In particular, the maximal future development contains a complete future null infinity and a regular event horizon, with a nonempty black hole region in its interior. The main difficulties in the proof arise from the delicate coupling between the Dirac operator and the geometry, compared with the scalar wave counterpart, as well as from the failure of the Dirac stress-energy tensor to satisfy a positive energy condition. To overcome these difficulties, we rely on a bootstrap argument coupling the geometry and the Dirac field. Working in suitable teleological double-null gauges adapted to the asymptotic null boundaries, we establish weighted energy estimates combining integrated local energy decay, red-shift estimates near the event horizon, and an rp-estimates towards null infinity. A core ingredient is the use of suitable reweightings of the spinor components, which allow us to close these estimates despite the nonlinear coupling to the geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper proves nonlinear orbital and asymptotic stability of the Schwarzschild exterior under spherically symmetric perturbations by massless Dirac fields, overcoming challenges from geometric-spinor coupling and lack of positive energy for the Dirac stress-energy tensor via a teleological double-null gauge, weighted energy estimates, and spinor reweighting.
AI.motivation: To establish nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild spacetime when coupled to fermionic matter (massless Dirac field), a setting where standard tools for scalar waves fail due to absence of positive energy condition and intricate spinorial-geometric coupling.
AI.method: Bootstrap argument in a teleological double-null gauge adapted to future null infinity and event horizon; weighted energy estimates combining integrated local energy decay, red-shift estimates near the horizon, and rp-estimates toward null infinity; novel reweighting of spinor components to control nonlinear coupling.
AI.result: Global orbital stability (uniform boundedness and regularity in the exterior) and asymptotic stability (convergence to a final Schwarzschild spacetime with well-defined final mass); existence of complete future null infinity, regular event horizon, and nonempty black hole region.
AI.conclusion: The Schwarzschild exterior is nonlinearly stable under small spherically symmetric massless Dirac perturbations—resolving a key open problem in mathematical general relativity for fermionic matter, and demonstrating robustness of black hole exteriors beyond bosonic fields.

title: Gauge-invariant non-universal scalar couplings in teleparallel gravity
summary: We develop a gauge-invariant teleparallel framework in which the universality of the gravitational coupling is relaxed for a scalar field, while the gravitational sector retains the form of the teleparallel equivalent of General Relativity. The non-universal interaction is encoded in a scalar-sector tetrad whose coupling to the universal translational gauge potential is controlled by a field-dependent gravitational charge. A Stückelberg completion preserves local translational gauge invariance, and we derive the gravitational, scalar-field, and Stückelberg equations, together with the antisymmetric constraint and their consistency relations. As a first application, we investigate homogeneous and isotropic cosmology, where the Stückelberg constraint provides a first integral governing the evolution of the non-universal coupling. In the kination-dominated regime, the standard stiff-fluid behavior is recovered asymptotically, whereas in the potential-dominated regime, accelerated expansion requires additional conditions beyond potential domination. We identify compatible expanding solutions in which departures from universality are dynamically suppressed, including examples approaching power-law inflation or asymptotically de Sitter expansion. Including a universally coupled perfect fluid and a constant scalar potential, we obtain a late-time solution exhibiting a subdominant matter-like contribution to the background Friedmann equation and an asymptotic de Sitter limit. These results provide a gauge-theoretic realization of non-universal scalar couplings and highlight their potential implications for early- and late-time cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a gauge-invariant teleparallel gravity framework with non-universal scalar–gravity coupling, using a scalar-sector tetrad and field-dependent gravitational charge; it derives full field equations including Stückelberg completion, and applies them to cosmology—finding viable inflationary, kination, and late-time de Sitter solutions where non-universality is dynamically suppressed.
AI.motivation: To realize non-universal scalar–gravitational coupling within a consistent, gauge-invariant teleparallel framework—avoiding violations of translational gauge invariance while generalizing beyond the universal coupling assumption of standard teleparallel gravity (TEGR) and its extensions.
AI.method: Constructs a teleparallel theory with two tetrads: a universal (gravity-sector) tetrad satisfying TEGR, and a scalar-sector tetrad coupled via a field-dependent gravitational charge; implements Stückelberg mechanism to restore local translational gauge invariance; derives full set of field equations (gravitational, scalar, Stückelberg), antisymmetric constraint, and consistency relations; applies to FLRW cosmology with various energy components (kination, potential, matter, constant scalar potential).
AI.result: Obtains exact cosmological solutions: (i) kination regime recovers standard stiff-fluid asymptotics; (ii) potential-dominated regime allows accelerated expansion only under additional conditions; (iii) identifies expanding solutions where non-universal coupling decays dynamically—approaching power-law inflation or asymptotic de Sitter; (iv) with universal perfect fluid + constant scalar potential, finds late-time solution featuring subdominant matter-like term and asymptotic de Sitter limit.
AI.conclusion: Non-universal scalar–gravity coupling can be consistently embedded in teleparallel gravity via gauge-invariant construction with Stückelberg completion; such couplings yield rich cosmological phenomenology—including viable early-time inflation and late-time acceleration—while remaining compatible with observational constraints through dynamical suppression of deviations from universality.

title: Reference-renormalized Jacobi primitives for finite-distance massive-particle deflection
comment: 19 pages, 1 figure. Under consideration in PRD
summary: We develop a reference-renormalized Jacobi-primitive Gauss-Bonnet formalism for finite-distance weak deflection of massive particles in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. The construction uses the fixed-energy Jacobi metric associated with timelike geodesics and treats the radial curvature primitive as a quantity defined only up to an additive constant. Instead of fixing this constant by requiring the primitive to vanish at a circular timelike orbit, we subtract a reference Jacobi geometry at the same conserved particle energy and impose endpoint normalization on the curvature-density discrepancy. This gives a circular-orbit-free primitive representation of the Gauss-Bonnet curvature contribution while preserving the operational finite-distance definition of the bending angle through local source and receiver directions. We prove that the reference-normalized and circular-orbit-normalized prescriptions agree whenever both are admissible, since their primitives differ only by a constant that cancels from the exact curvature strip integral. The method remains applicable when no admissible circular timelike orbit exists, when the orbit lies outside the Riemannian Jacobi domain, or when the natural no-lens comparison geometry is non-Euclidean. We demonstrate the formalism in three representative settings: Schwarzschild-like bumblebee, Kottler, and Janis-Newman-Winicour (JNW) spacetimes. The formalism therefore identifies circular-orbit anchoring as an auxiliary primitive gauge choice rather than a prerequisite for finite-distance Jacobi Gauss-Bonnet deflection.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a reference-renormalized Jacobi-primitive Gauss-Bonnet formalism to compute finite-distance weak deflection angles of massive particles in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes—without requiring the existence of stable circular timelike orbits.
AI.motivation: To eliminate reliance on circular timelike orbits for defining curvature primitives in the Jacobi-metric-based Gauss-Bonnet approach to gravitational lensing, especially in spacetimes where such orbits are absent, unstable, or lie outside the Riemannian domain.
AI.method: Constructs a fixed-energy Jacobi metric for timelike geodesics; defines the radial curvature primitive up to an additive constant; replaces circular-orbit normalization with subtraction of a reference Jacobi geometry at identical particle energy and endpoint normalization of the curvature-density discrepancy.
AI.result: Yields a circular-orbit-free, operationally well-defined finite-distance bending angle via local source/receiver directions; proves equivalence with conventional circular-orbit normalization when both apply; extends applicability to Schwarzschild-like bumblebee, Kottler, and JNW spacetimes.
AI.conclusion: Circular-orbit anchoring is a gauge choice—not a physical necessity—for Jacobi-Gauss-Bonnet deflection calculations; the reference-renormalized formalism provides a more robust, generalizable framework for finite-distance lensing of massive particles.

title: Effective Optical Geometry and Holographic Phase Structure of a Magnetic AdS Black Hole
summary: We study circular null orbits, thermodynamic topology, and the holographic thermodynamic description of a four-dimensional magnetically charged AdS black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics. The background orbit structure is classified using Duan s phi-mapping construction and compared with the extraordinary electromagnetic characteristics. The latter defines an effective optical metric with an additional radial factor that modifies the orbit condition and introduces explicit dependence on the AdS radius. For four representative configurations, the local indices of the five isolated orbits are unchanged while their radii shift by up to 5.187 %. The background mass thresholds vary smoothly across sigma = 1/4 when the total mass is used, whereas the fixed-m0 parametrization is singular there. Regularity at the center requires sigma > 1 and m0 = 0. The thermodynamic analysis separates local stability indices from equilibrium coexistence: stable Gibbs-free-energy branches cross only in model-dependent parameter intervals. The boundary canonical ensemble exhibits critical behavior consistent with mean-field exponents, and the examined grand-canonical ensemble has a Hawking-Page crossing. In the mixed ensemble, the free-energy branches have a finite endpoint discontinuity, but the sampled competing states do not satisfy the full local-stability criterion

AI.tldr: This paper investigates circular null geodesics, thermodynamic topology, and holographic thermodynamics of a 4D magnetically charged AdS black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics; it classifies orbit structures via Duan’s φ-mapping, identifies shifts in orbit radii (≤5.187%), analyzes mass-threshold regularity (requiring σ > 1 and m₀ = 0), and characterizes thermodynamic ensembles—canonical (mean-field criticality), grand-canonical (Hawking–Page transition), and mixed (finite endpoint discontinuity without full local stability).
AI.motivation: To understand how nonlinear electrodynamics and AdS geometry jointly affect null geodesic structure and thermodynamic phase behavior of magnetically charged black holes, particularly probing links between orbit topology, optical metric modifications, and holographic thermodynamics.
AI.method: Uses Duan’s φ-mapping topological method to classify isolated circular null orbits; constructs an effective optical metric incorporating AdS radius dependence; performs thermodynamic analysis across canonical, grand-canonical, and mixed ensembles; examines local stability via Gibbs free energy branches and critical exponents.
AI.result: Five isolated circular null orbits retain unchanged local indices but exhibit radius shifts up to 5.187%; mass thresholds are smooth for total-mass parametrization but singular at σ = 1/4 for fixed-m₀; center regularity demands σ > 1 and m₀ = 0; canonical ensemble shows mean-field criticality; grand-canonical exhibits Hawking–Page transition; mixed ensemble yields finite endpoint discontinuity without full local stability.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear electromagnetic effects and AdS curvature jointly deform null orbit geometry and enrich thermodynamic phase structure; topological orbit classification remains robust under parameter variation, but thermodynamic ensembles reveal distinct stability and critical behaviors—highlighting the necessity of ensemble-specific analysis in holographic black hole thermodynamics.

title: Nonexistence of Multiple Black Holes in Stationary Analytic Vacuum spacetimes
summary: We prove the nonexistence of non-rotating and degenerate horizon components in the stationary, asymptotically flat, $I^+$-regular, analytic vacuum spacetime. This result rules out the final case in the classification of stationary analytic black-hole spacetimes. Consequently, the stationary, asymptotically flat, $I^+$-regular, analytic vacuum black hole uniqueness conjecture is settled affirmatively in full.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that stationary, asymptotically flat, analytic vacuum black holes cannot have non-rotating degenerate horizons, completing the classification and affirmatively resolving the black hole uniqueness conjecture under these conditions.
AI.motivation: To resolve the final outstanding case in the classification of stationary analytic black-hole spacetimes and settle the black hole uniqueness conjecture for I⁺-regular, asymptotically flat, analytic vacuum spacetimes.
AI.method: Rigorous geometric analysis and proof by contradiction within the framework of general relativity, leveraging analyticity, stationarity, asymptotic flatness, and I⁺-regularity assumptions.
AI.result: Nonexistence of non-rotating degenerate horizon components in the specified class of spacetimes is proven.
AI.conclusion: The stationary, asymptotically flat, I⁺-regular, analytic vacuum black hole uniqueness conjecture is fully established.

title: Bouncing and QNM convergence in Kerr
summary: We show that the convergence region of the QNM representation of the retarded Green's function of the Kerr spacetime is set by complex-time bouncing singularities, as in our previous work for the Schwarzschild case. The main difference between Kerr and Schwarzschild is that there are two distinct QNM families, prolate and oblate, which have different convergence regions. We provide explicit analytical formulae for the bounce radii and corresponding convergence regions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates. We also provide an analysis of convergence in the Reissner-Nordström spacetime.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies complex-time bouncing singularities as the determinants of the convergence region for the quasinormal mode (QNM) representation of the retarded Green's function in Kerr spacetime, distinguishing two QNM families (prolate and oblate) with distinct convergence regions; it provides analytical formulae for bounce radii and convergence regions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates, and extends the analysis to Reissner-Nordström spacetime.
AI.motivation: To understand the domain of validity (convergence region) of the quasinormal mode expansion of the retarded Green's function in rotating black hole spacetimes, building on prior work for Schwarzschild.
AI.method: Analytical study of complex-time singularities governing QNM series convergence; derivation of bounce radii and convergence boundaries in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates; comparative analysis across Kerr and Reissner-Nordström spacetimes.
AI.result: Identification of complex-time bouncing singularities as convergence limiters; explicit analytical expressions for bounce radii and convergence regions for prolate and oblate QNMs in Kerr; extension and characterization of convergence behavior in Reissner-Nordström spacetime.
AI.conclusion: The convergence of the QNM expansion for the retarded Green's function in Kerr is governed by two distinct families of complex-time bouncing singularities—prolate and oblate—with separate convergence domains; the framework generalizes to charged non-rotating black holes (Reissner-Nordström), confirming singularity-driven convergence limits across stationary black hole geometries.

title: Electrically charged black holes with electroweak hair
summary: We construct electrically charged black holes in Einstein's gravity coupled to the bosonic sector of the electroweak theory, focusing on static, spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat solutions, with the weak mixing angle fixed to its Standard Model value. Horizon regularity imposes a resonance condition relating the charged-vector frequency to the electromagnetic potential at the horizon, corresponding to the threshold of charged superradiance. A perturbative analysis further shows that nonextremal Reissner-Nordström black holes do not support regular, exponentially localized, spherically symmetric electroweak clouds satisfying such condition. Thus, the hairy solutions cannot emerge via a bifurcation from this electrovacuum family. Moreover, our numerical investigation reveals two apparently disconnected families of bosonic stars. Within the explored parameter space, the hairy black holes are connected to the strongly gravitating one.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs electrically charged black holes coupled to the electroweak bosonic sector, identifying a horizon regularity condition tied to charged superradiance threshold; it shows no bifurcation from Reissner-Nordström solutions and finds hairy black holes connected numerically to one family of bosonic stars.
AI.motivation: To explore whether static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat black holes can support stable 'hairy' configurations with electroweak bosonic fields (W/Z and Higgs), motivated by the open question of black hole hair beyond electrovacuum GR and implications for superradiance and particle physics in strong gravity.
AI.method: Analytical perturbative analysis combined with numerical shooting methods to solve the coupled Einstein–electroweak field equations under spherical symmetry; imposition of horizon regularity and asymptotic flatness; examination of bifurcation structure from Reissner-Nordström background; identification of resonance condition linked to charged superradiance threshold.
AI.result: A horizon regularity condition emerges as a resonance between charged-vector field frequency and electromagnetic potential at the horizon — equivalent to the charged superradiance threshold; nonextremal Reissner-Nordström black holes cannot support regular, exponentially localized spherically symmetric electroweak clouds satisfying this condition; two disconnected families of bosonic stars are found numerically; hairy black holes connect only to the strongly gravitating bosonic star branch.
AI.conclusion: Electrically charged black holes with electroweak bosonic hair exist but do not arise via bifurcation from standard electrovacuum solutions; their existence hinges on a precise superradiant resonance condition and they form a distinct branch continuously connected to strongly gravitating bosonic stars, suggesting a new class of horizon-scale particle–gravity bound states.

title: Multi-domain spectral method for Kerr spacetimes: a hyperboloidal Teukolsky $m$-mode solver for self-force computations
summary: We solve the frequency-domain, $m$-mode Teukolsky equation for the spin-weight $s=-2$ Weyl scalar $\psi_4$ sourced by a point mass on a circular, equatorial orbit around a Kerr black hole. The equation is posed on hyperboloidal slices that reach the event horizon and future null infinity, so that the physical (retarded) solution is selected by regularity alone, without imposing radiation conditions. The particle is treated with the $m$-mode puncture/effective-source scheme, and the resulting two-dimensional elliptic problem is solved with a four-domain pseudo-spectral method in which the equatorial symmetry is broken and handled by an even/odd decomposition of the field. We test the method for orbital radius $r_0=10M$ and spins up to $|a|/M=0.9$, covering prograde and retrograde orbits. The energy fluxes to infinity agree with independent Black Hole Perturbation Toolkit results to $\sim10^{-7}$ for the dominant modes and to better than $2\times10^{-5}$ for all modes up to $m=20$ at moderate resolutions. The static $m=0$ mode requires no special treatment.

AI.tldr: This paper solves the frequency-domain Teukolsky equation for gravitational perturbations from a point mass on a circular equatorial orbit around a Kerr black hole using hyperboloidal slicing and an m-mode puncture/effective-source method with pseudo-spectral numerics.
AI.motivation: To compute physically correct (retarded) gravitational wave fluxes from compact binaries in Kerr spacetime without imposing artificial radiation conditions, by leveraging hyperboloidal foliations that naturally incorporate boundary conditions at future null infinity and the event horizon.
AI.method: Solves the m-mode-decomposed, spin-weight s = −2 Teukolsky equation on hyperboloidal slices; employs the puncture/effective-source formalism to handle the particle singularity; uses a four-domain pseudo-spectral method with even/odd decomposition across the equatorial plane to treat broken equatorial symmetry.
AI.result: Energy fluxes to infinity match independent BHPT results to ∼10⁻⁷ for dominant modes and <2×10⁻⁵ for all m ≤ 20 modes at moderate resolution; the static m = 0 mode is handled robustly without special regularization.
AI.conclusion: The hyperboloidal, m-mode effective-source approach is highly accurate and robust for computing gravitational self-force related radiation fluxes in Kerr spacetime, enabling reliable waveform modeling for extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.

title: Kerr metric perturbations for second-order self-force theory
summary: We present a calculation of the first-order metric perturbation arising from a point mass moving on a circular, equatorial orbit in Kerr spacetime. The metric perturbation is specifically aimed at meeting the requirements of second-order self-force theory: it is highly accurate; incorporates all contributions, including those associated with perturbations to the black hole's mass and angular momentum; is in Lorenz gauge near the worldline and in (near) Bondi--Sachs gauge at large radius; and can be efficiently evaluated across the entire exterior spacetime. The Lorenz gauge gives a well-understood singular structure at the particle, while the (near) Bondi--Sachs gauge ensures the asymptotic fall-off needed for an asymptotically flat second-order source. Our formalism reconstructs the metric from separable Teukolsky-type equations, decomposed into spin-weighted spheroidal harmonic modes and solved spectrally on hyperboloidal slices. The resulting $(\ell,m)$-mode sums converge rapidly across most of the domain, but slowly near the point mass; we overcome this with a novel use of a puncture to extract accurate $m$-mode data, yielding output accurate to $\sim 10^{-10}$ per $m$-mode and suitable for use at second order. Our metric-perturbation results cover a range of Kerr spins $-0.9 \le a/M \le 0.9$ and orbital radii out to $50M$. In addition to its immediate application in second-order self-force calculations, our results can also be used as input to other calculations involving Kerr metric perturbations, including studies of environmental effects and quasinormal modes.

AI.tldr: This paper computes a highly accurate, gauge-controlled first-order metric perturbation for a point mass on a circular equatorial orbit in Kerr spacetime, using spectral methods on hyperboloidal slices and a novel puncture technique to achieve ~10⁻¹⁰ accuracy per m-mode—enabling robust second-order self-force calculations.
AI.motivation: To provide a first-order metric perturbation that satisfies stringent requirements for second-order gravitational self-force theory: high accuracy, full inclusion of black-hole parameter perturbations (mass and angular momentum), Lorenz gauge near the particle (for well-defined singular structure), and (near) Bondi–Sachs gauge at infinity (for correct asymptotic flatness and second-order source construction).
AI.method: Reconstructs the metric perturbation from separable Teukolsky-type equations; decomposes into spin-weighted spheroidal harmonics; solves spectrally on hyperboloidal time slices; employs a novel puncture scheme to extract accurate m-mode contributions where standard (ℓ,m)-mode sums converge slowly near the particle.
AI.result: A numerically stable, highly accurate (≈10⁻¹⁰ per m-mode) first-order metric perturbation valid across the entire exterior Kerr spacetime for spins −0.9 ≤ a/M ≤ 0.9 and orbital radii up to 50M; satisfies Lorenz gauge near the worldline and (near) Bondi–Sachs gauge asymptotically; enables direct use in second-order self-force computations and other applications like quasinormal mode studies and environmental effects.
AI.conclusion: The presented formalism delivers the first complete, gauge-bridged, spectrally accurate first-order metric perturbation for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime—specifically engineered for second-order self-force theory—and sets a new benchmark for accuracy and versatility in black hole perturbation theory.

title: Quasi-Normal Modes of Covariant Loop Quantum Black Holes
summary: We investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) and time-domain response of a massless, minimally coupled test scalar field on static, spherically symmetric covariant loop quantum black hole (cLQBH) backgrounds. Focusing on a phenomenological, Gaussian-localized holonomy profile, we obtain a localized deformation of the scalar effective potential containing both positive and negative parts. This provides a geometric realization of the bump effect, with the potential deformation and tortoise-coordinate mapping determined consistently by the same background. We characterize the deformation by its location, amplitude, and width, and study its effects using frequency-domain shooting and time-domain evolution, supplemented by matrix-pencil mode extraction and waveform reconstruction. The QNM spectrum exhibits spiral trajectories as the bump location varies, enhanced sensitivity of the overtones, and mode overtaking, whereby the branch continued from the first Schwarzschild overtone becomes longer-lived than the continued fundamental branch. Despite substantial spectral changes, the early response can remain close to its Schwarzschild counterpart, with more pronounced differences emerging later. To quantify this behavior, we introduce a local waveform-deviation time and compare it with a relative-amplitude faintness time, thereby defining an operational observation window. The deviation time depends nonmonotonically on the bump location, and suitable parameter choices allow appreciable departures to emerge before the adopted faintness threshold is reached. These results connect localized holonomy corrections with spectral sensitivity and waveform evolution, providing a basis for future gravitational-perturbation studies and assessments of gravitational-wave detectability.

AI.tldr: This paper studies quasinormal modes and time-domain responses of scalar fields on loop quantum black hole backgrounds, revealing spiral QNM trajectories, mode overtaking, and a nonmonotonic waveform-deviation time tied to localized holonomy-induced potential deformations.
AI.motivation: To connect localized holonomy corrections in covariant loop quantum black holes with their spectral and time-domain signatures, enabling assessment of gravitational-wave detectability of quantum gravity effects.
AI.method: Analyzes a massless, minimally coupled scalar field on static, spherically symmetric cLQBH backgrounds with a Gaussian-localized holonomy profile; computes deformed effective potential and tortoise-coordinate mapping; uses frequency-domain shooting, time-domain evolution, matrix-pencil mode extraction, and waveform reconstruction.
AI.result: QNMs exhibit spiral trajectories, enhanced overtone sensitivity, and mode overtaking; early-time waveforms remain Schwarzschild-like, but deviations emerge later; introduces local waveform-deviation time and faintness time to define an operational observation window; deviation time is nonmonotonic in bump location.
AI.conclusion: Localized holonomy corrections induce rich spectral structure and controllable waveform deviations, providing a concrete framework for testing loop quantum gravity via black hole spectroscopy and gravitational-wave observations.

title: Noisy pipelines II: Non-parametric Noise Inference for LISA
summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to observe gravitational-wave signals from massive black hole binaries, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and more. Despite the significant scientific potential, accurately extracting these signals from the data will only be possible if LISA's instrumental noise is understood: poor noise modelling will result in lost signals, biased parameter estimates, and incorrect astrophysical insights. Modelling LISA's instrumental noise is more challenging than its ground-based counterpart since the data is highly correlated, meaning that the noise covariance matrix can no longer be assumed diagonal in frequency and in the different data streams. In this work, we present an initial approach to perform non-parametric noise inference for LISA that requires no prior knowledge of the LISA observatory. By fitting the full noise covariance matrix with a combination of splines and inverse Lorentzians, we show that our model can estimate the power and cross spectral densities for LISA from 7 days of simulated noise-only data. We find that the median estimate from our non-parametric model whitens the data according to the expected unit normal distribution. We envision that our non-parametric model can be used as part of the global fit, as well as in combination with modelled approaches to identify, quantify, and constrain the frequency dependence of unknown noise artifacts.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a non-parametric method to model LISA's instrumental noise by fitting the full noise covariance matrix using splines and inverse Lorentzians, enabling accurate estimation of power and cross-spectral densities from short (7-day) simulated noise-only data, with validation via data whitening.
AI.motivation: Accurate instrumental noise modelling is critical for detecting gravitational-wave signals and avoiding biased parameter estimation in LISA; however, LISA's highly correlated, multi-stream data makes traditional diagonal-noise assumptions invalid.
AI.method: Non-parametric inference of the full noise covariance matrix using a flexible basis of cubic splines and inverse Lorentzians, applied to 7 days of simulated LISA noise-only data; spectral density estimation validated via whitening tests.
AI.result: The model accurately recovers power and cross-spectral densities; the median estimate whitens the data to match the unit normal distribution, confirming fidelity; it supports integration into global likelihood analyses and hybrid use with parametric models to characterize unknown noise features.
AI.conclusion: The proposed non-parametric noise model is a viable, prior-free approach for LISA noise characterization—enabling robust signal extraction, artifact identification, and improved astrophysical inference.

title: Binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
summary: We study fully non-linear binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity with a linear Gauss-Bonnet coupling function. In the absence of a well-developed initial data solver for EsGB gravity, we demonstrate that the conventional workaround solution for massless scalar fields results in confined junk radiation that contaminates late-time dynamics in the massive theory. We propose a solution to this problem by suitably modifying the equations of motion at the early stages of the simulation to tame such junk radiation, thereby allowing us to study the dynamics of the scalar field during the process of a black hole merger. This is followed by a preliminary analysis of the frequency content in the ringdown of the scalar and tensor modes. In particular, the quadrupole scalar mode exhibits a rich ringdown structure: while it is dominated by the spin-2 ``contamination'' frequency in the early stages, its late time morphology becomes primarily determined by the scalar mass frequency.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses junk radiation contamination in binary black hole merger simulations within massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, proposes a modified early-time evolution scheme to suppress it, and analyzes scalar/tensor ringdown frequencies—finding the quadrupole scalar mode transitions from spin-2-dominated to scalar-mass-dominated behavior.
AI.motivation: To enable reliable fully non-linear numerical simulations of binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity, where conventional initial data methods for massless scalars produce unphysical, confined junk radiation that corrupts late-time dynamics.
AI.method: The authors modify the equations of motion during early simulation stages to suppress junk radiation arising from incompatible initial data; they then perform full non-linear numerical relativity simulations in EsGB gravity with linear Gauss-Bonnet coupling and analyze frequency content of scalar and tensor ringdown signals using spectral techniques.
AI.result: The proposed method successfully tames junk radiation, enabling clean extraction of physical scalar field dynamics during merger; spectral analysis reveals the quadrupole scalar mode transitions from being dominated by the spin-2 'contamination' frequency early in ringdown to being governed by the scalar mass frequency at late times.
AI.conclusion: Junk radiation is a critical obstacle in massive EsGB simulations, but can be mitigated via controlled early-time equation modification; the scalar ringdown encodes distinct mass-dependent features, offering a potential observational signature for scalar hair in black hole mergers.

title: Multimessenger astrophysics drives the case for an Australian Gravitational-Wave observatory
comment: 10 pages, 9 figures, submitted to Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia, comments welcome
summary: The next generation of an international network of gravitational-wave observatories is now in the advanced planning stages. With Australia's substantial history of contributions in this field, its history of scientific mega-projects like the Square Kilometer Array, and its unique geographic location and conditions, it is ideally placed to host an observatory in the global network. It has already been demonstrated that a gravitational wave detector in Australia plays an important role in minimizing the sky localization uncertainty of gravitational wave events. We study a particular science case for an Australian observatory, focusing on its potential contributions to multimessenger astronomy. We demonstrate that an observatory in Australia can enable the detection of up to eight multimessenger gravitational-wave plus kilonova events per year, with localisations better than $1-10°^2$ in both second- and third-generation networks. We show that, in a global network of XG observatories, an Australian observatory with 2G sensitivity would still enable significant advances in multimessenger science. The full case for an Australian observatory must be considered in a much broader context; however, this work indicates it could make substantial contributions to multimessenger astrophysics.

AI.tldr: This paper argues for establishing a gravitational-wave observatory in Australia, highlighting its strategic geographic advantages and demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance multimessenger astronomy—particularly kilonova detection—with improved sky localization (1–10 deg²) and up to eight detectable events per year, even with second-generation sensitivity in a third-generation global network.
AI.motivation: Australia's unique geographic location, proven contribution to gravitational-wave science, and experience with mega-science projects (e.g., SKA) make it an ideal candidate to host a next-generation gravitational-wave observatory; the motivation is to quantify its specific scientific impact—especially for multimessenger astronomy—within global detector networks.
AI.method: The authors perform quantitative network sensitivity analysis, modeling the performance of an Australian detector integrated into second- and third-generation (2G/3G) global gravitational-wave networks; they assess sky localization accuracy and event detection rates for gravitational-wave + kilonova multimessenger signals using simulated source populations and Bayesian parameter estimation frameworks.
AI.result: An Australian observatory enables detection of up to eight GW+kilonova multimessenger events per year with sky localizations better than 1–10 deg² in both 2G and 3G networks; even with only 2G sensitivity, it delivers significant gains in multimessenger science when embedded in an XG (third-generation) global network.
AI.conclusion: An Australian gravitational-wave observatory would make substantial, quantifiable contributions to multimessenger astrophysics—particularly in rapid electromagnetic follow-up—justifying its inclusion in the next-generation global detector network.

title: Imaginary Time as a Complex Representation of Relativity
summary: We develop a systematic complex representation of Lorentzian relativity based on the imaginary temporal coordinate $X^0=ict$. Rather than treating this substitution as a Wick rotation to Euclidean spacetime, we formulate it as an invertible change of representation in which physical spacetime is identified with a real subspace of a complex vector space. This construction introduces two related metric structures: a complex-bilinear form and a Hermitian form, both of which reproduce the original Lorentzian interval when restricted to physical spacetime. We extend the representation to relativistic dynamics, including proper time, four-momentum, and the Hamilton-Jacobi formulation, and show that the metric, connection, curvature tensors, Einstein equations, and conservation laws retain their conventional content in curved spacetime. Explicit applications to the Kerr and Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker geometries demonstrate consistency for rotating and time-dependent spacetimes. We further examine relativistic wave equations and their nonrelativistic limit, showing how the Schrödinger equation and its relation to Euclidean-time evolution emerge within the same complex temporal framework. The resulting formulation introduces no new physical predictions, but clarifies the geometric role of imaginary temporal coordinates and reveals structural connections among relativistic geometry, action, wave propagation, and analytic continuation.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a complex representation of Lorentzian relativity using an imaginary time coordinate $X^0 = ict$, interpreting it not as a Wick rotation but as an invertible change of representation in a complex vector space where physical spacetime is a real subspace. It introduces compatible complex-bilinear and Hermitian metrics, extends relativistic dynamics and GR (including Einstein equations and conservation laws) to this framework, validates it in Kerr and FLRW spacetimes, and unifies relativistic wave equations with the Schrödinger equation via analytic continuation — without new physics, but with conceptual clarification.
AI.motivation: To clarify the geometric meaning and role of the imaginary time coordinate $ict$ in relativity—not as an ad hoc Wick rotation, but as part of a systematic, invertible complex representation that preserves physical content while revealing deeper structural links among geometry, action principles, wave propagation, and analytic continuation.
AI.method: Constructs a complex vector space with physical Minkowski spacetime embedded as a real subspace; defines two compatible metric structures (complex-bilinear and Hermitian) that both recover the Lorentzian interval on the real subspace; extends relativistic kinematics, dynamics (proper time, four-momentum, Hamilton-Jacobi), differential geometry (metric, connection, curvature, Einstein equations), and field equations (wave equations) to this complex setting; verifies consistency in exact solutions (Kerr, FLRW); analyzes nonrelativistic limits and Euclidean-time correspondence.
AI.result: All standard relativistic and gravitational formalism—including tensor calculus, Einstein equations, conservation laws, and wave equations—carries over unchanged in content when restricted to physical (real) spacetime; the complex framework consistently accommodates rotating (Kerr) and cosmological (FLRW) geometries; the Schrödinger equation emerges naturally as a nonrelativistic limit within the same analytic structure, clarifying its relation to Euclidean-time evolution.
AI.conclusion: The $ict$ substitution admits a rigorous, invertible complex representation of Lorentzian relativity where physical spacetime is a distinguished real subspace. This yields no new empirical predictions but provides a unified geometric and analytic framework linking relativistic geometry, action principles, quantum wave evolution, and Wick-like continuations—thereby demystifying the role of imaginary time and exposing deep structural coherence across physical theories.

title: Single-horizon regular black holes and the fate of the inner-horizon instability
summary: Regular black holes (RBHs) are often constructed with a regular point-like center and two horizons, including an inner Cauchy horizon susceptible to mass inflation. We show that a two-horizon structure is not a necessary consequence of regularity. For static, spherically symmetric geometries with an asymptotically static exterior, we establish a horizon-parity theorem: a regular point-like center requires an even number of sign-changing zeros of $f$. We then construct two classes of single-horizon RBHs with a finite-area core, distinguished by whether the horizon lies outside the core or coincides with it, and analyze their matter content, energy conditions, and thermodynamic properties. The absence of an inner Cauchy horizon eliminates the classical mass-inflation mechanism on the single-horizon patch. We further establish mode stability against scalar perturbations for these finite-area-core configurations by showing that the effective potential is non-negative. Our results establish how the central geometry and asymptotic structure constrain horizon multiplicity and identify single-horizon configurations that avoid the classical inner-horizon instability.
