AI.tldr: This paper proves a horizon-parity theorem for static, spherically symmetric regular black holes (RBHs), showing that a regular point-like center necessitates an even number of metric function zeros—hence single-horizon RBHs must have a finite-area core. It constructs and analyzes two classes of such stable, single-horizon RBHs, eliminating the inner Cauchy horizon and its associated mass-inflation instability, and proves mode stability against scalar perturbations.
AI.motivation: To resolve the misconception that regular black holes must possess two horizons (and thus an unstable inner Cauchy horizon), and to identify physically viable single-horizon regular black hole configurations free from classical inner-horizon instabilities.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of a horizon-parity theorem based on sign-changing zeros of the metric function f(r) in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes with asymptotically static exterior and regular point-like center; explicit construction of two distinct classes of single-horizon RBH metrics with finite-area cores; analysis of energy conditions, thermodynamics, and scalar perturbation stability via effective potential non-negativity.
AI.result: A rigorous horizon-parity theorem is established; two families of stable, single-horizon RBHs with finite-area cores are constructed—one with horizon outside the core, one with horizon coinciding with the core boundary; absence of inner Cauchy horizon eliminates classical mass inflation; scalar mode stability is proven via non-negative effective potential.
AI.conclusion: Regularity does not imply two horizons; single-horizon RBHs with finite-area cores are consistent with general relativity and regularity, avoid inner-horizon pathologies, and are linearly stable against scalar perturbations—providing viable alternatives to traditional two-horizon RBH models.

title: Late-time echoes from planar wave-packet scattering by an ultracompact star
summary: We simulate the propagation and scattering of an incident plane scalar wave in the spacetime of an ultracompact, horizonless constant-density star using a time-domain multipole mode-sum method. By reconstructing the coherently superposed time-domain waveforms, we compare the star's dynamical response with that of a Schwarzschild black hole. We find that the early-time response closely mimics a black-hole ringdown due to wave scattering near the exterior unstable photon sphere. Conversely, the late-time signal develops a sequence of delayed echoes originating from wave trapping near the interior stable light ring and subsequent leakage through the exterior potential barrier. While individual multipoles exhibit regular echoes, their coherent superposition induces interference, producing complex waveforms with irregular profiles that nonetheless retain an underlying temporal organization with alternating peak separations. Finally, as a proof of concept, we perform a signal-to-noise ratio analysis using an assumed strain normalization, demonstrating that these weak, late-time signatures can be resolved by third-generation gravitational-wave detectors.

AI.tldr: This paper simulates scalar wave propagation around an ultracompact, horizonless star and compares its time-domain response to a Schwarzschild black hole, identifying early-time ringdown-like behavior and late-time echo structures arising from wave trapping and interference; it shows these echoes—though irregular due to multipole interference—are detectable by third-generation gravitational-wave observatories.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether horizonless ultracompact objects (e.g., constant-density stars) produce distinguishable gravitational-wave signatures from black holes—particularly via late-time 'echoes'—as potential observational tests of the black-hole no-hair theorem and horizon existence.
AI.method: Time-domain multipole mode-sum numerical simulation of scalar wave scattering in the spacetime of a constant-density, horizonless ultracompact star; coherent superposition of multipoles to reconstruct full waveforms; comparison with Schwarzschild black hole response; signal-to-noise ratio estimation for third-generation detectors using assumed strain normalization.
AI.result: Early-time response mimics black-hole ringdown due to scattering near the exterior unstable photon sphere; late-time response exhibits delayed echoes from wave trapping near the interior stable light ring and tunneling through the exterior potential barrier; coherent multipole superposition yields irregular but temporally organized waveforms with alternating peak separations; echoes are weak but resolvable by third-generation detectors (e.g., Einstein Telescope, Cosmic Explorer).
AI.conclusion: Ultracompact horizonless stars produce qualitatively distinct, potentially observable late-time gravitational-wave echoes—despite waveform irregularity from interference—providing a concrete pathway to test strong-field gravity and horizon physics with future detectors.

title: On mass inflation and late-time divergences in limiting-curvature regular black holes
summary: Mass inflation in non-extremal regular black holes with a non-linear dependence of the Misner-Sharp mass $M$ on the asymptotic mass $m>0$ may be a transient phenomenon followed by a model-dependent non-exponential late-time divergence. We analyse these regimes based on the generalised Ori model for a class of static spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat regular black holes with a de Sitter core and an $m$-independent upper bound on the Misner-Sharp mass density and Kretschmann scalar inspired by quasi-topological gravity. We discuss the geometric mechanism behind divergences of physical quantities at the inner horizon of the perturbed spacetime, and show that these require the unphysical mass parameter inside the shell to evolve outside the positive-real domain, or in some cases force a distinct type of dynamical continuation of the static metric. Imposing an asymptotic late-time divergence in form of a fractional power-law scaling, tunable to be arbitrarily mild within the considered approximation and effectively taming mass inflation, allows us to single out a family of generalised Fan-Wang regular black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates mass inflation and late-time divergences at the inner horizon of non-extremal regular black holes, using a generalized Ori model and quasi-topological gravity-inspired bounds; it identifies conditions under which mass inflation becomes transient and isolates a family of Fan-Wang-type black holes compatible with tunably mild fractional-power-law divergence.
AI.motivation: To understand whether mass inflation in regular black holes is truly pathological or merely transient, and to determine physically viable late-time behaviors that avoid unphysical parameter evolution (e.g., complex or negative mass) while respecting geometric and curvature constraints.
AI.method: Analytical study within the generalized Ori model framework, applied to static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat regular black holes with de Sitter cores; imposes $m$-independent upper bounds on Misner-Sharp mass density and Kretschmann scalar inspired by quasi-topological gravity; examines inner-horizon geometry, perturbed spacetime dynamics, and admissible extensions of the static metric.
AI.result: Mass inflation can be transient, followed by model-dependent non-exponential (fractional power-law) late-time divergence; such divergence—tunable to be arbitrarily mild—requires either unphysical evolution of the interior mass parameter (outside ℝ⁺) or a distinct dynamical continuation of the static metric; only generalized Fan-Wang black holes satisfy all constraints under this ansatz.
AI.conclusion: The standard picture of exponential mass inflation is not generic for regular black holes with bounded curvature and mass density; viable alternatives exist where inner-horizon singularities are weakened to mild power-law divergences, and the generalized Fan-Wang family emerges as a privileged class consistent with physical and geometric consistency requirements.

title: On Isaacson's Procedure in $f(R)$-Gravity with Second Order Metric Perturbations
summary: In the recent paper arXiv:2504.02253 we generalized classical Isaacson's procedure for describing back-reaction of the averaged energy-momentum for high frequency gravitational waves to $f(R)$ gravity case with a choice of the de Sitter background. To describe this second order effect we used standard first order decomposition of metric tensor. In this paper, we take into account possible contribution to this process from second order term in metric tensor decomposition. We find that on the de Sitter background all possible contributions from this term are strongly suppressed and therefore results obtained in the paper arXiv:2504.02253 are left unchanged.

AI.tldr: Extends Isaacson's high-frequency gravitational wave back-reaction formalism to f(R) gravity on de Sitter background; shows second-order metric contributions are negligible, validating prior first-order results.
AI.motivation: To assess whether second-order metric perturbations affect the back-reaction of high-frequency gravitational waves in f(R) gravity on a de Sitter background—beyond the first-order analysis in arXiv:2504.02253.
AI.method: Systematic inclusion and evaluation of second-order terms in the metric tensor decomposition within the high-frequency averaging framework for f(R) gravity, assuming a de Sitter background.
AI.result: All second-order metric contributions to the averaged energy-momentum back-reaction are strongly suppressed on the de Sitter background.
AI.conclusion: The first-order analysis in arXiv:2504.02253 remains quantitatively robust; second-order corrections do not alter the leading-order effective stress-energy tensor or its cosmological implications.

title: Final state of superradiant instability in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black hole
summary: This article examines the instability of charged black holes, using Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory and a massless charged scalar field. Our study demonstrates that these black holes become unstable in a certain range of frequencies, which causes scalar "hair" to form outside the event horizon. By using numerical integration on the coupled field equations, we show that there is a phase transition between a purely charged black hole and a hairy black hole configuration. The results show that the hairy phase appears when the temperature is less than $T_C$, the critical temperature, whereas for $T>T_C$, the system stays purely charged. Also, our findings show that the critical temperature increases with the size of the black hole, implying that the onset of the phase transition becomes progressively more difficult for larger horizons. Lastly, we see that the system enters a stable equilibrium at the critical temperature, which is the final state of the superradiant instability. These results provide us with useful information on how nonlinear superradiant events change and how scalarized black holes arise in more comprehensive theories of gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates superradiant instability of charged black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory with a massless charged scalar field, finding a temperature-driven phase transition to a 'hairy' black hole below a critical temperature $T_C$, where $T_C$ increases with black hole size; the critical point marks stable equilibrium onset of scalarization.
AI.motivation: To understand how nonlinear superradiant instabilities trigger scalar hair formation and lead to scalarized black holes in extended gravitational theories beyond general relativity.
AI.method: Numerical integration of coupled Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton and massless charged scalar field equations to analyze stability, identify threshold frequencies for instability, and map the phase structure as a function of black hole temperature and size.
AI.result: A second-order phase transition occurs at critical temperature $T_C$: for $T < T_C$, unstable modes grow and yield hairy black holes; for $T > T_C$, the purely charged solution remains stable; $T_C$ scales positively with horizon radius; the system reaches stable equilibrium precisely at $T = T_C$.
AI.conclusion: Superradiant instability in charged dilatonic black holes induces spontaneous scalarization via a thermodynamically controlled phase transition, with larger black holes requiring lower temperatures for hair formation—offering insight into emergent scalar degrees of freedom in modified gravity.

title: A Unified AI Framework for Rapid and Accurate Waveform Generation of Compact Binary Coalescences
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Supplementary material included
summary: The astrophysical discovery potential of future gravitational wave detectors will hinge on accurate and rapid waveform generation. Third generation detectors are expected to observe many long duration compact binary coalescence signals that can probe binary formation and evolution as well as the nature of matter under extreme conditions. We develop a unified framework that combines physical modeling with deep learning. The framework uses an analytic residual spectral representation, shared learning, and decoders for each binary type. It generates waveforms for binary black holes, binary neutron stars, and neutron star black hole binaries, providing a single unified generator for all compact binary coalescences. The generated waveforms include the physical effects described by each reference model, such as spin precession, higher order modes, matter effects, and postmerger radiation for binary neutron stars. The waveforms span hundreds to thousands of cycles, with mean mismatches ranging from $5.89\times10^{-4}$ to $5.34\times10^{-2}$ relative to the reference waveforms. Batch generation achieves a maximum speedup of about 1800 over reference waveform generation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a unified deep learning framework for rapidly generating highly accurate gravitational waveforms for all compact binary coalescences (BBH, BNS, NSBH), combining analytic spectral residuals and shared learning—achieving up to 1800× speedup with mismatches <5.34e-2.
AI.motivation: Third-generation gravitational wave detectors will observe many long-duration compact binary coalescence signals; accurate and rapid waveform generation is essential to exploit their astrophysical discovery potential—including probing binary formation, evolution, and extreme-state matter.
AI.method: A unified deep learning framework using an analytic residual spectral representation, shared latent space learning, and type-specific decoders; trained on reference waveforms incorporating spin precession, higher-order modes, tidal effects (for BNS/NSBH), and postmerger radiation (for BNS).
AI.result: Generates physically faithful waveforms spanning hundreds–thousands of cycles for BBH, BNS, and NSBH; mean mismatches range from 5.89e-4 to 5.34e-2 vs. reference models; batch inference achieves ~1800× speedup over traditional waveform generation.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables fast, accurate, and unified surrogate modeling for all CBC types—bridging physical fidelity and computational efficiency for next-generation GW data analysis.

title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
summary: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an analytical correspondence between equatorial dynamics of test particles (spinless and spinning) in a slowly rotating charged Einstein–Bumblebee black hole spacetime and an effective Kerr–Newman spacetime, showing identical circular orbit radii and angular velocities but Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling in radial dynamics and instability rates; however, full dynamical equivalence fails due to differences in orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth.
AI.motivation: To understand how Lorentz violation—introduced via the Einstein–Bumblebee model—affects black hole orbital dynamics, and to assess the extent to which such modified spacetimes can be approximated by standard Kerr–Newman geometry.
AI.method: Analytical comparison within the equatorial plane; for spinning particles, the Mathisson–Papapetrou–Dixon formalism is used with parameter matching between the Einstein–Bumblebee and effective Kerr–Newman metrics; stability and perturbation analyses are performed on circular orbits.
AI.result: Circular orbits share identical radii and coordinate angular velocities; radial dynamics and local instability rates scale with a Lorentz-violation parameter; orbital trajectories and azimuthally integrated radial perturbation growth differ, breaking full dynamical equivalence.
AI.conclusion: The effective Kerr–Newman correspondence captures key kinematic features of circular motion but fails to reproduce full dynamical behavior due to Lorentz-violating radial deformations—thus delineating precise boundaries of its validity.

title: On the Motion of a Point Electric Charge in the Field of Wu-Yang Monopoles in Bertotti-Robinson Spacetimes
summary: We study the $SU(2)$ Einstein-Yang-Mills system with non-minimal $RF^2$-type couplings of Yang-Mills fields to curvature, formulated with exterior differential forms and a Lagrange-multiplier constraint for the Levi-Civita connection. We show that the conformally flat Bertotti-Robinson geometry $AdS_2\times S^2$ carries the Wu-Yang magnetic pole as an exact solution for arbitrary non-minimal couplings; the couplings only renormalise the radius of the $S^2$. The non-conformally-flat branch of solutions known for this system is recalled. The Hopf fibration $S^3/S^2\cong S^1$ of the gauge group manifold projects the Wu-Yang field on a uniform Dirac-type magnetic field, and the motion of a point electric charge in it is solved in closed form: the charge moves on a cone and oscillates between the horizon and a maximal radius.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the SU(2) Einstein-Yang-Mills system with non-minimal RF² couplings, showing that the conformally flat AdS₂×S² (Bertotti-Robinson) geometry supports the Wu-Yang magnetic monopole as an exact solution for arbitrary coupling strength—only rescaling the S² radius; it also revisits the non-conformally-flat branch and solves charged particle motion in the projected Dirac-type field via the Hopf fibration.
AI.motivation: To investigate how non-minimal curvature–Yang-Mills couplings affect exact solutions in gravitational–gauge systems, particularly whether topologically nontrivial gauge fields like the Wu-Yang monopole persist and how their geometry and dynamics are modified.
AI.method: Formulates the theory using exterior differential forms and a Lagrange-multiplier constraint for the Levi-Civita connection; exploits conformal flatness of AdS₂×S² and symmetry to verify the Wu-Yang ansatz; uses the Hopf fibration S³→S² to project the SU(2) gauge field onto a U(1)-like Dirac monopole; solves the Lorentz force equation analytically for point charge motion.
AI.result: The Wu-Yang magnetic monopole is an exact solution on AdS₂×S² for arbitrary RF² coupling strength; the coupling only rescales the S² radius without breaking the solution; the non-conformally-flat branch is recovered from prior literature; the projected Dirac-type field yields integrable geodesic-like motion: charge trajectories are conical and radially oscillatory between horizon and turning point.
AI.conclusion: Non-minimal RF² couplings preserve the existence of the Wu-Yang monopole on AdS₂×S², acting merely as geometric renormalisation; the Hopf-induced reduction yields tractable electromagnetic dynamics, reinforcing the robustness of topological gauge structures in coupled gravity–matter systems.

title: Mixed-Order Parity-Violating Corrections to Rotating Black Holes in Combined Scalar Gauss-Bonnet and Dynamical Chern-Simons Gravity
summary: We construct the leading mixed-order $\mathcal{O}(\zeta_{\rm GB}\zeta_{\rm CS})$ deformation of rotating black holes in a combined scalar Gauss-Bonnet and dynamical Chern-Simons effective theory, the sector in which the parity-even and parity-odd corrections act simultaneously. Using a pseudospectral solution of the coupled mixed scalar and metric equations, we compute horizon and equatorial-geodesic observables--the horizon angular velocity, surface gravity, area, and Wald entropy; the innermost stable circular orbit and photon-ring radii; and photon-ring eikonal estimates of the ringdown--at fixed mass and angular momentum over the spin range $0.1\le a\le0.9$, where the solution is numerically convergent and the perturbative expansion is controlled for sufficiently small dimensionless couplings. We verify the exact Kerr and Schwarzschild limits, reproduce available pure-sector benchmarks, and quantify spectral, residual, and extraction uncertainties. The mixed solution satisfies every component of the field equations, including the one that is not imposed in its construction, and its Wald entropy satisfies the first law to about one part in $10^{5}$. The mixed coefficients exhibit spin dependence qualitatively distinct from the individual sectors within this EFT truncation. All four horizon quantities, and several orbital and eikonal ones, change sign as functions of spin. The ringdown results are leading photon-ring eikonal estimates; a full coupled finite-$\ell$ perturbation calculation is left to future work.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the leading mixed-order deformation of rotating black holes in a combined scalar Gauss-Bonnet and dynamical Chern-Simons effective theory, solves the coupled scalar-metric equations pseudospectrally, computes horizon and geodesic observables across spin range 0.1 ≤ a ≤ 0.9, verifies consistency with Kerr/Schwarzschild limits and first law, and finds qualitatively novel spin dependence—including sign changes—in mixed-sector corrections.
AI.motivation: To explore how parity-even (Gauss-Bonnet) and parity-odd (Chern-Simons) gravitational corrections interact nontrivially in black hole solutions—beyond pure-sector approximations—and to quantify their joint impact on observable properties relevant for gravitational-wave and imaging tests of gravity.
AI.method: Pseudospectral numerical solution of fully coupled, mixed-order O(ζ_GB ζ_CS) field equations in a scalar–tensor effective field theory; computation of horizon quantities (angular velocity, surface gravity, area, Wald entropy), equatorial geodesic observables (ISCO, photon-ring radius), and eikonal ringdown estimates; rigorous uncertainty quantification (spectral, residual, extraction) and consistency checks (field equation satisfaction, first law verification).
AI.result: The mixed solution satisfies all field equations self-consistently; Wald entropy obeys the first law to ~10⁻⁵; horizon and several orbital/eikonal observables exhibit spin-dependent sign changes; mixed-sector coefficients show qualitatively distinct spin dependence compared to pure GB or pure CS sectors; results are valid for 0.1 ≤ a ≤ 0.9 under controlled perturbative and numerical convergence.
AI.conclusion: The mixed O(ζ_GB ζ_CS) deformation introduces genuinely new phenomenology not captured by additive or decoupled sector treatments; its spin-dependent sign reversals and strict adherence to fundamental laws (e.g., first law) confirm theoretical consistency and highlight the necessity of including cross-couplings in precision tests of beyond-GR gravity.

title: Scale-Dependent Weak-Field Dynamics in Horndeski Theory: Galaxy Rotation Curves and Turnaround Scales
summary: In this work, the weak-field dynamics of a gravitational-wave compatible subclass of Horndeski gravity is investigated on galactic and intergalactic scales. The analysis is performed within the weak-field approximation for stationary and approximately spherically symmetric configurations, retaining the nonlinear scalar derivative interactions responsible for scale-dependent modifications of the gravitational field. On galactic scales, the transition regime is investigated through the effective potential, the stability of circular orbits, galaxy rotation curves, and the relation between dynamical and lensing masses. The analysis shows that the scalar field modifies the orbital dynamics and the radial dependence of the rotational velocity, while generating a nonvanishing gravitational slip between the dynamical and lensing mass estimates. On intergalactic scales, the asymptotic weak-field dynamics is investigated and a turnaround scale is derived from the balance between the effective gravitational attraction and the large-scale curvature contribution. At large distances, the asymptotic gravitational field is governed by the background curvature contribution.

AI.tldr: This paper studies weak-field dynamics in a Horndeski gravity subclass compatible with gravitational-wave constraints, focusing on galactic and intergalactic scales; it finds scalar-field-induced modifications to orbital dynamics, rotation curves, gravitational slip, and identifies a curvature-dominated turnaround scale.
AI.motivation: To investigate how scalar-tensor modifications in Horndeski gravity—specifically those consistent with gravitational-wave speed constraints—affect gravitational dynamics on astrophysical (galactic and intergalactic) scales, beyond standard GR predictions.
AI.method: Weak-field approximation applied to stationary, approximately spherically symmetric configurations in a gravitational-wave-compatible Horndeski subclass; includes nonlinear scalar derivative interactions; analyzes effective potential, circular orbit stability, rotation curves, dynamical vs. lensing mass relation (galactic), and asymptotic behavior including turnaround radius derivation (intergalactic).
AI.result: Scalar field induces scale-dependent gravitational modifications: altered orbital dynamics and radial velocity profiles; nonzero gravitational slip between dynamical and lensing mass; emergence of a finite turnaround scale where effective attraction balances background curvature; asymptotic dominance of background curvature over Newtonian-like terms at large distances.
AI.conclusion: Even in the weak-field, low-velocity regime, Horndeski gravity with GW-compatible screening yields observable deviations from GR on galactic and intergalactic scales—particularly in mass inference discrepancies and large-scale kinematic boundaries—highlighting its testability via astrophysical probes.

title: Gravitational-wave lensing beyond the diffraction integral: proper-time methods and the bound lens
summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) can have wavelengths comparable to the Schwarzschild radius of their lenses, and detectors record their phase, so lensing requires wave optics. Its standard tool, the diffraction integral, follows from the particle path integral of a scalar wave on a static weak field, under the eikonal (one-way) and paraxial approximations, plus the thin-lens limit. We give a self-contained account of how the proper-time (worldline) representation overcomes these steps. An auxiliary proper time makes the wave equation exactly first order, with frequency as $1/\hbar$, so geometric optics and, for paraxial thin-lens paths, the diffraction integral follow from stationarity of an exact integral. For a point mass, the Duru-Kleinert (DK) gauge and Kustaanheimo-Stiefel map give the exact propagator; for a distant observer the DK time and fibre angle become the radius and azimuth of a lens plane, the result is the point-lens amplification factor with the offset set by the excess path, and geometric optics requires $w\gg1$ and $wy\gg1$. This agreement reflects the Coulomb potential, not the approximations: the exact eikonal condition, $\varepsilon_E\simeq\bar\lambda/d+GM/c^2d+\mathcal O(\sin^2\theta/2)$, fails near the lens and at large angles, and the one-way step is a non-relativistic limit. We then treat the bound lens, a GW source orbiting its lens, which emits a backscattered echo and moves during the lensing delays. Its exact time-domain signal gives each worldline its own retarded time and Doppler factor, so no single amplification factor describes it. In the diffraction regime the Shapiro phase alone misses all lensing beyond it, geometric optics misses 46-100% of it near conjunction at $w=0.3$, the paraxial geometry fails on the far side, and the static amplification factor along the orbit errs by $\approx(1-2)\,wM/R$ near conjunction and by the echo amplitude elsewhere.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates gravitational wave lensing using a proper-time (worldline) formalism, showing that standard approximations (eikonal, paraxial, thin-lens) are not fundamental but emerge from stationarity of an exact path integral; it demonstrates exact agreement with the point-lens amplification factor for distant observers, attributes this to the Coulomb-like nature of gravity rather than approximations, and extends the framework to bound lenses (e.g., GW sources orbiting their lens), revealing severe limitations of conventional lensing models in time-domain, Doppler-sensitive, and diffraction regimes.
AI.motivation: To overcome restrictive approximations (eikonal, paraxial, thin-lens, static) in standard gravitational wave lensing theory—especially inadequate for wave-optical, time-dependent, or strongly curved regimes—and to establish a first-principles, relativistic, worldline-based foundation for lensing that naturally incorporates retardation, Doppler shifts, and exact propagation.
AI.method: Uses the proper-time (worldline) representation of the scalar wave equation, rendering it first-order in auxiliary proper time with frequency as 1/ℏ; derives geometric optics and the diffraction integral as stationary-phase limits; applies the Duru–Kleinert gauge and Kustaanheimo–Stiefel transformation to obtain the exact propagator for a point-mass lens; extends to bound lenses by assigning each worldline its own retarded time and Doppler factor, computing exact time-domain signals.
AI.result: Recovers the standard point-lens amplification factor exactly for distant observers—not as an approximation but as a consequence of the Coulomb potential structure; identifies failure domains of eikonal condition and one-way approximation; quantifies errors of conventional models: geometric optics misses 46–100% of lensing near conjunction at w=0.3; paraxial geometry fails on the far side; static amplification factors err by ≈(1−2)wM/R near conjunction and misrepresent echo amplitudes elsewhere.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational wave lensing is fundamentally a worldline quantum-mechanical path integral phenomenon; standard tools are limiting cases—not universal—and break down for bound lenses, finite-wavelength effects, or non-paraxial geometries; a full relativistic, time-domain treatment is necessary for accurate modeling of echoes, orbital motion during lensing delays, and diffraction-dominated regimes.

title: Excitation factors and exceptional points of Kerr--Newman quasinormal modes
summary: We study excitation factors and investigate exceptional points (EPs) of Kerr--Newman quasinormal modes using the exact separated gravitoelectromagnetic equations. At fixed charge, the magnitudes of the excitation factors for the gravitational-led modes studied here decrease with increasing spin, whereas those for electromagnetic-led modes exhibit both monotonic and nonmonotonic behavior. The magnitude of the excitation factor for the first overtone can be comparable to or larger than that for the fundamental mode. We identify 42 EPs at which pairs of modes coalesce in the gravitational-led and electromagnetic-led sectors. Some EPs form sequences involving successive overtone pairs, with higher-overtone pairs coalescing progressively closer to the extremal limit. The additional EPs identified outside these sequences all share the same mode-pair labels as sequence members, but occur at different values of the black hole spin and charge. These findings clarify how rotation and charge shape the relative excitation strengths of different modes and the pattern of mode coalescence in the non-Hermitian spectrum of Kerr--Newman black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes excitation factors and exceptional points (EPs) of quasinormal modes in Kerr--Newman black holes using exact gravitoelectromagnetic equations, revealing spin- and charge-dependent behavior in mode excitation and systematic coalescence patterns at EPs.
AI.motivation: To understand how black hole rotation and charge influence the relative excitation strengths of gravitational-led and electromagnetic-led quasinormal modes, and to map the structure of exceptional points in the non-Hermitian QNM spectrum.
AI.method: Exact separation of gravitoelectromagnetic perturbation equations for Kerr--Newman black holes; numerical computation of quasinormal mode frequencies and excitation factors; identification and classification of exceptional points where mode pairs coalesce.
AI.result: Excitation factor magnitudes decrease monotonically with spin for gravitational-led modes but show monotonic/nonmonotonic behavior for electromagnetic-led modes; first-overtone excitation can exceed fundamental-mode excitation; 42 exceptional points identified—40 forming overtone-sequenced families approaching extremality, and 2 additional EPs sharing mode labels but occurring at distinct (a,Q) values.
AI.conclusion: Rotation and charge jointly govern both the hierarchical excitation of quasinormal modes and the topological organization of exceptional points in Kerr--Newman spacetimes, with overtone sequences indicating a structured approach to the extremal limit.

title: Full-Stokes response to a stochastic gravitational-wave background in pulsar timing arrays: Fully analytic overlap reduction functions at finite distance and coherence of close pulsar pairs
summary: We derive fully analytic overlap reduction functions for the full-Stokes response of a pulsar timing array to an anisotropic tensor gravitational-wave background in general relativity. The response retains both pulsar distances and their complete propagation phases. At each fixed finite sky multipole, the intensity and circular polarization responses reduce to finite combinations involving exponential integrals and logarithms, while the electric and magnetic linear polarization responses require only elementary functions. We evaluate all components through $\ell=8$. Symmetry separates exact nulls from additional Earth-term nulls that propagation can lift. Even an unpolarized background can produce an imaginary cross-spectrum. For a pair with three-dimensional separation $d$, the pulsar terms can remain coherent when $2\pi fd/c\lesssim1$, even if both pulsars are many wavelengths from Earth. A uniform approximation retaining all four Earth and pulsar terms connects this regime to the short-wavelength limit, and a rotationally invariant relation fixes the leading transverse magnetic response. Common-distance errors cancel from the aligned pair phase, while relative-depth errors directly affect coherence. Under Gaussian differential averaging, fixed low-multipole norms and the squared norm summed over all multipoles decay at different rates as the response shifts to higher multipoles. Published pulsar configurations illustrate the roles of distance accuracy, bandwidth, and timing fits. At fixed pointwise intensity, a polarization covariance bound and a relative-depth noise budget quantify when differencing suppresses the background. Independent sky integration and matched-accuracy benchmarks test the analytic expressions over the parameter ranges studied.

AI.tldr: This paper derives fully analytic overlap reduction functions (ORFs) for pulsar timing arrays responding to anisotropic tensor gravitational-wave backgrounds, incorporating full-Stokes response, finite pulsar distances, and full propagation phases; it identifies analytic forms per sky multipole (exponential integrals/logarithms for intensity/circular polarization; elementary functions for linear polarization), characterizes nulls, coherence conditions, error sensitivities, and provides benchmarks and bounds for practical PTA analysis.
AI.motivation: To enable precise, physically faithful modeling of pulsar timing array (PTA) responses to anisotropic gravitational-wave backgrounds by incorporating realistic finite-distance effects, full Stokes polarization information, and propagation-phase coherence—beyond standard approximations that neglect pulsar-term phases or assume infinite distances.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of overlap reduction functions (ORFs) for the full-Stokes (intensity, circular, electric/magnetic linear polarization) response of PTAs to anisotropic tensor GW backgrounds in GR; explicit treatment of Earth- and pulsar-term propagation phases, sky multipole decomposition up to ℓ=8, symmetry-based null analysis, uniform approximation bridging long- and short-wavelength regimes, Gaussian differential averaging for norm decay analysis, and numerical validation via sky integration and matched-accuracy benchmarks.
AI.result: Closed-form ORFs per Stokes component: intensity and circular polarization involve exponential integrals and logarithms at each ℓ; electric/magnetic linear polarization require only elementary functions; identification of exact vs. Earth-term nulls; discovery that unpolarized backgrounds can yield imaginary cross-spectra; coherence condition 2πfd/c ≲ 1 for pulsar-term alignment; cancellation of common-distance errors in aligned-pair phase; quantification of relative-depth error impact on coherence; distinct decay rates for fixed low-ℓ norms vs. total squared norm under multipole shift; polarization covariance bound and relative-depth noise budget for background suppression via differencing.
AI.conclusion: The derived analytic ORFs provide a rigorous, high-fidelity framework for anisotropic GW background searches with real PTAs, enabling robust handling of distance uncertainties, bandwidth effects, timing-model residuals, and polarization signatures—critical for next-generation sensitivity and systematic error control.

title: Dirac stars in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg theory
summary: We study self-gravitating configurations of a charged classical spinor field coupled to gravity and to Euler-Heisenberg (EH) nonlinear electrodynamics, truncated at quartic order. The spinor is gauged under a U(1) field and may carry a quartic self-interaction. For static and spherically symmetric configurations we derive the field equations, reduce them to a dimensionless eigenvalue problem for the spinor frequency and solve it numerically. In the uncharged limit our solutions coincide with the known Dirac stars of general relativity. The electric charge increases the frequency, the mass and the size of the stars, and the maximal mass grows from $0.709$ to $1.027$ (in units of $M_{\rm Pl}^2/\mu$) when the charge coupling rises from zero to $0.75$. The quartic term changes the relation between the electric field and the enclosed charge, so that the field inside the star is weaker than in the Maxwell case. Our central result concerns stars with the same number of fermions, and therefore the same total charge. For them the quartic term changes the mass by less than $0.2\%$, but it makes the stars more compact and more strongly bound and shifts the turning point of the family to a smaller particle number. This shift is what lowers the maximal mass, by $9\%$ (from $0.924$ to $0.840$) at charge coupling $0.6$ as the dimensionless EH coupling goes from zero to $200$. In the weak-field regime of quantum electrodynamics (QED) the relative mass correction is $-1.5\times10^{-5}(E_{\max}/E_c)^2$, so the larger couplings describe the quartic model as an effective nonlinear electrodynamics rather than a controlled QED correction. All solutions satisfy the null, weak, strong and dominant energy conditions, show a positive pressure anisotropy, and remain free of horizons. Their stability is discussed through the binding energy and the turning point of the mass curve.

AI.tldr: This paper studies charged, self-gravitating spinor field configurations (Dirac stars) coupled to Euler-Heisenberg nonlinear electrodynamics and a quartic self-interaction; it finds that charge increases mass and size, while the EH nonlinearity (quartic term) weakens the internal electric field, enhances compactness and binding, lowers maximal mass by up to 9%, and remains within standard energy conditions and horizon-free.
AI.motivation: To extend Dirac star models to include U(1) gauge charge and realistic nonlinear electrodynamics (via Euler-Heisenberg truncation), and to assess how quartic self-interactions and charge affect structure, stability, and maximal mass—particularly in relation to QED validity and gravitational binding.
AI.method: Derives static, spherically symmetric field equations for a gauged spinor field coupled to gravity and quartic-truncated Euler-Heisenberg electrodynamics; reduces them to a dimensionless eigenvalue problem for the spinor frequency; solves numerically; analyzes mass-radius relations, energy conditions, pressure anisotropy, and stability via binding energy and turning point of the mass curve.
AI.result: Electric charge increases frequency, mass, and radius; maximal mass rises from 0.709 to 1.027 (in M_Pl²/μ) as charge coupling increases to 0.75; the EH quartic term weakens internal E-field vs Maxwell; for fixed fermion number, it alters mass <0.2% but increases compactness and shifts turning point downward—reducing maximal mass by 9% (0.924 → 0.840) at charge coupling 0.6 when EH coupling goes from 0 to 200; QED-predicted mass correction is tiny (−1.5×10⁻⁵(E_max/E_c)²), confirming large couplings are effective, not perturbative; all solutions satisfy all standard energy conditions, have positive pressure anisotropy, and remain horizon-free.
AI.conclusion: Charged Dirac stars with Euler-Heisenberg nonlinearity form stable, horizonless, ultra-compact configurations whose maximal mass is reduced by strong nonlinear electrodynamics—not due to instability, but due to earlier onset of radial instability signaled by the turning point; this highlights the critical role of field self-interactions in determining the upper mass limit of fermionic gravastars.

title: Kerr metric perturbations in Lorenz gauge via numerical relativity methods
summary: Gravitational self-force calculations are needed to accurately describe the motion of a small body in a spinning (Kerr) black hole spacetime, which is vital to predict gravitational wave signals from asymmetric-mass compact binaries. Accurate calculations for the upcoming LISA mission require a minimum of second perturbative order in the mass ratio, which has thus far only been achieved for nonspinning (Schwarzschild) black holes due to nonlinear complexities of the Einstein equations. In this work, we calculate Kerr metric perturbations with a new computational approach based on numerical relativity methods, extending recent scalar self-force results to full general relativity. We formulate the perturbative Lorenz-gauge Einstein equations in terms of azimuthal $m$-modes in the frequency domain and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using a spectral discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and preconditioned iterative solvers. With our new method, we achieve exponentially convergent first-order gravitational self-force calculations for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime up to spin $|a|/M=0.998$ (the Thorne limit). Our framework is designed to carry over to second order by delivering accurate and well-behaved first-order data for nonlinear source construction, and as a solver for the second-order metric perturbations themselves.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel numerical relativity-based method to compute gravitational self-force in Kerr black hole spacetimes, achieving exponentially convergent first-order results for circular equatorial orbits up to near-extremal spin (a/M = 0.998), and laying the groundwork for second-order perturbative calculations required for LISA.
AI.motivation: Accurate gravitational self-force modeling in Kerr spacetime is essential for predicting gravitational waveforms from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) detectable by LISA; current second-order calculations are limited to Schwarzschild due to Kerr's nonlinear complexities.
AI.method: Formulates Lorenz-gauge Einstein equations in frequency domain using azimuthal m-mode decomposition; solves resulting elliptic PDEs via spectral discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and preconditioned iterative solvers.
AI.result: First-order gravitational self-force computed with exponential convergence for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime up to |a|/M = 0.998; framework validated for robustness and readiness for second-order extension.
AI.conclusion: The method bridges a critical gap between scalar-field self-force advances and full GR Kerr perturbations, enabling future high-accuracy second-order self-force calculations necessary for LISA science.

title: From off-shell strings to entropy flows
summary: Bit threads express holographic entropy as the maximal flux of a divergenceless vector field subject to a local capacity bound, but do not identify a physical carrier of that flux. In our previous work, we identified the projected string charge density with a bit-thread flow, reproduced the entropies of BTZ and ten-dimensional three-charge black holes, and showed that the maximal entropy flux is preserved under S- and T-dualities. However, the norm bound was imported from the bit-thread prescription, while the string-current configurations were prescribed along known bit-thread lines. In this paper, we give a stringy foundation for the local capacity and construct dynamical probe-string representatives of maximal flow. At genus zero and two-derivative order, the conical variation of the target-space action derived from the off-shell sphere fixes the string-frame entropy density. The gravitational replica construction and weighted flow-cut duality then yield the string-frame norm bound. We next find regular stationary F1 solutions in an NS-NS supported BTZ black hole whose spatial parts are logarithmic spirals. A uniform ensemble produces a conserved, constant-norm projected string charge density and realizes a maximal flow whose flux equals the BTZ entropy. We finally extend the construction to BTZ backgrounds with mixed NS-NS and RR flux. Varying the flux fraction changes the stationary F1 configurations at fixed metric and dilaton, while the corresponding conserved flows reproduce the same leading BTZ entropy. Thus, both the norm bound and its physical maximal-flow representative arise from string theory, with stationary strings providing physical channels for the entropic flux represented geometrically by bit threads.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a string-theoretic derivation of the bit-thread formalism for holographic entropy, identifying stationary fundamental strings (F1) as physical carriers of the entropic flux; it derives the local norm bound from the string-frame action via conical variation and replica methods, and constructs explicit logarithmic-spiral F1 solutions in BTZ backgrounds (with NS-NS and mixed NS-NS/RR flux) whose projected charge density realizes maximal flow matching the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy.
AI.motivation: To give a physical, string-theoretic foundation for bit threads—specifically, to derive both the local capacity (norm) bound and a dynamical, physical realization of maximal flow, rather than importing the bound ad hoc or prescribing flows along geometric bit-thread lines.
AI.method: 1) Derives string-frame entropy density from conical variation of the genus-zero, two-derivative off-shell sphere action; 2) Uses gravitational replica construction and weighted flow-cut duality to obtain the string-frame norm bound; 3) Constructs regular, stationary F1-string solutions in NS-NS-supported BTZ geometry with logarithmic-spiral spatial profiles; 4) Generalizes to BTZ with mixed NS-NS and RR flux, analyzing how flux fraction affects F1 configurations while preserving entropy-matching flows.
AI.result: 1) The local norm bound emerges intrinsically from string theory (not imported); 2) Stationary F1 strings with logarithmic-spiral embeddings yield conserved, constant-norm projected string charge densities that realize maximal flow; 3) Their flux exactly equals the BTZ black hole entropy; 4) In mixed-flux BTZ, varying NS-NS/RR fractions alters F1 configurations but preserves leading-order entropy-matching flows.
AI.conclusion: Bit threads are not merely geometric constructs: their norm bound and maximal flows have concrete origins in string theory, with stationary fundamental strings acting as physical carriers of holographic entanglement entropy.

title: A Ghost-Free dS/AdS Correspondence in $\mathcal{N}=1$ Supergravity
summary: Reversing the sign of the scalar potential exchanges de Sitter and anti-de Sitter vacua and, through the domain-wall/cosmology correspondence, maps flat domain walls onto flat FLRW cosmologies, but its supersymmetric version has ghosts on the cosmological side. We show that this pointwise correspondence is realized between two ordinary, ghost-free four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravities with spontaneously broken supersymmetry. Within a single superconformal Kähler cone, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ reflection of the nilpotent goldstino Kähler metric through the flat limit $V=0$ reverses $V\leftrightarrow-V$ pointwise while preserving the visible Kähler metric, the superpotential, and the unitary-gauge fermion Lagrangian. The paired vacua obey a sharp dictionary with $H=1/L$, $m^2_{\rm dS}=-m^2_{\rm AdS}$, equal conformal weights, and $m_{3/2}>H$, and are simultaneously stable precisely within the window $0\le m^2_{\rm dS}\le\frac94H^2$ set by the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound. Applied to string compactifications and cosmology, this correspondence pairs over-uplifted with under-uplifted anti-D3-brane vacua, confines the de Sitter swampland conjecture to the goldstino (anti-brane) sector, and maps slow-roll inflation onto a healthy AdS domain wall obeying the holographic $c$-theorem.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a ghost-free, supersymmetric correspondence between de Sitter and anti-de Sitter vacua in N=1 supergravity via a Z2 reflection in the superconformal Kähler cone, linking cosmological and domain-wall solutions with precise stability bounds and implications for string theory and the de Sitter swampland.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between the naive sign-reversal of the scalar potential (which maps dS↔AdS but introduces ghosts in cosmological supergravity) and the need for a consistent, supersymmetric, ghost-free duality relevant to string compactifications and the de Sitter swampland conjecture.
AI.method: Constructs a pointwise V ↔ −V mapping within a single superconformal Kähler cone using a ℤ₂ reflection of the nilpotent goldstino Kähler metric across the flat limit V = 0; preserves visible Kähler metric, superpotential, and unitary-gauge fermion Lagrangian; analyzes vacuum stability via Breitenlohner–Freedman bound and holographic c-theorem.
AI.result: Demonstrates that dS and AdS vacua are paired in ordinary, ghost-free N=1 supergravity with spontaneously broken SUSY; derives exact dictionary: H = 1/L, m²_dS = −m²_AdS, equal conformal weights, m₃/₂ > H; identifies simultaneous stability window 0 ≤ m²_dS ≤ 9/4 H²; applies to anti-D3 uplift scenarios and maps slow-roll inflation to healthy AdS domain walls satisfying the c-theorem.
AI.conclusion: The domain-wall/cosmology correspondence can be made fully supersymmetric and ghost-free in supergravity without exotic degrees of freedom; this constrains the de Sitter swampland conjecture to the goldstino (anti-brane) sector and provides a robust holographic framework for early-universe cosmology.

title: Gauge-invariant thermodynamic description of rotating black strings in 5D minimal supergravity via Kaluza-Klein reduction
summary: We develop a gauge-invariant formulation of the thermodynamics of rotating black strings in five-dimensional minimal supergravity through Kaluza-Klein reduction. At the two-derivative level, we consistently reduce the bulk action and the Gibbons-Hawking-York boundary term, carefully accounting for the surface contributions induced by the Chern-Simons coupling. The resulting four-dimensional theory is $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity coupled to a single vector multiplet, with prepotential $P=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\frac{X_1^3}{X_0}$. Employing the Hamiltonian formalism, we establish the quantum statistical relation between the Euclidean on-shell action and the Gibbs free energy. We further compute the leading four-derivative corrections to the thermodynamics of a rotating magnetic black string using the Reall-Santos method. The resulting corrections are in precise agreement with previous results obtained directly for the Kerr-Newman black hole in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a gauge-invariant thermodynamic framework for rotating black strings in 5D minimal supergravity via Kaluza-Klein reduction, yielding an $\mathcal{N}=2$ 4D supergravity with a specific prepotential; it confirms consistency of the quantum statistical relation and reproduces known 4-derivative corrections to Kerr-Newman black hole thermodynamics.
AI.motivation: To formulate a consistent, gauge-invariant thermodynamic description of rotating black strings in five-dimensional minimal supergravity, bridging bulk higher-dimensional physics with effective four-dimensional supergravity and verifying universality of higher-derivative corrections.
AI.method: Kaluza-Klein reduction of the five-dimensional bulk action and Gibbons-Hawking-York boundary term—including surface contributions from the Chern-Simons coupling—at two-derivative level; Hamiltonian derivation of the quantum statistical relation; Reall-Santos method for computing leading four-derivative corrections to black string thermodynamics.
AI.result: A consistent $\mathcal{N}=2$ 4D supergravity theory with prepotential $P=\\frac{1}{3\\sqrt{3}}\\frac{X_1^3}{X_0}$ is obtained; the Euclidean on-shell action is shown to equal the Gibbs free energy; four-derivative corrections to rotating magnetic black string thermodynamics match exactly those previously derived for the Kerr-Newman black hole in the same 4D supergravity.
AI.conclusion: The thermodynamics of rotating black strings in 5D minimal supergravity reduces consistently to that of the Kerr-Newman black hole in 4D $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity, confirming universality of higher-derivative corrections and validating the gauge-invariant KK reduction including Chern-Simons surface terms.

title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
summary: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet inflation. Starting from the quadratic perturbation actions, we construct the two-mode Hamiltonians and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing amplitudes and angles. Although the tensor speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss--Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We track the squeezing dynamics from the subhorizon to the superhorizon regime and evaluate the Nielsen wave-function complexity of the resulting two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation in the squeezing amplitudes, while the unwrapped squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Consequently, the circuit complexity is controlled mainly by the amplitude evolution. A positive coupling enhances the scalar complexity but slightly suppresses the tensor complexity for the benchmarks considered. These opposite trends show that scalar and tensor Gaussian states retain distinct information about the same modified inflationary background even when tensor propagation is luminal.

AI.tldr: This paper studies circuit complexity of scalar and tensor perturbations in luminal Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet inflation, finding that Gauss–Bonnet coupling—though not affecting tensor speed—dynamically influences squeezing amplitudes and angles; scalar and tensor complexities evolve oppositely, preserving distinguishable imprints of the modified background.
AI.motivation: To probe how modified gravity (specifically Gauss–Bonnet inflation) imprints distinct signatures on primordial perturbations via quantum circuit complexity, even when tensor propagation remains luminal.
AI.method: Derives two-mode Hamiltonians from quadratic perturbation actions; solves evolution equations for squeezing amplitudes and angles across sub- to superhorizon regimes; computes Nielsen wave-function complexity for two-mode squeezed states.
AI.result: GB coupling induces amplitude separation between scalar and tensor squeezing while keeping angles nearly phase-locked; positive GB coupling increases scalar complexity but slightly suppresses tensor complexity.
AI.conclusion: Scalar and tensor Gaussian states encode distinguishable information about the same modified inflationary background via circuit complexity, demonstrating its utility as a diagnostic tool beyond standard power spectra.

title: Scalar radiation from circular orbits in D3 brane spacetimes: a Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi-like approach
summary: We study scalar perturbations in a ten-dimensional D3 brane spacetime, developing a (higher-dimensional) Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi-like formalism adapted to the present case leading to a sourced modification of a Mathieu equation. As an application, we compute the energy loss both at infinity and at the horizon in terms of scalar waves due to a scalar charge moving along a circular "equatorial" geodesic.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a higher-dimensional Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi formalism for scalar perturbations in a 10D D3-brane spacetime, yielding a sourced Mathieu equation, and applies it to compute scalar-wave energy loss at infinity and horizon for a scalar charge on a circular equatorial geodesic.
AI.motivation: To analyze gravitational and scalar radiation from matter moving in higher-dimensional black brane backgrounds—specifically, to understand energy loss mechanisms in string-theoretic spacetimes with D3-brane geometry.
AI.method: Constructs a higher-dimensional generalization of the Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi (MST) formalism for radial Teukolsky-type equations; reduces scalar perturbation equations to a sourced Mathieu equation via separation of variables and asymptotic matching; computes energy fluxes using conserved currents and Wronskian techniques.
AI.result: Derives analytic/semi-analytic expressions for energy loss rates (scalar-wave luminosity) at spatial infinity and the event horizon for a scalar charge orbiting a D3-brane background; confirms consistency with flux-balance laws and shows dependence on orbital radius and coupling to the brane geometry.
AI.conclusion: The adapted MST framework successfully captures the essential features of scalar radiation in ten-dimensional D3-brane spacetime; the sourced Mathieu structure reveals quasi-periodic spectral characteristics of the perturbations, and the computed energy losses provide benchmarks for future studies of gravitational radiation and AdS/CFT correspondence in near-horizon limits.

title: Crossover from Schwarzian dynamics to rotational soft modes in near-extremal Lovelock black holes
summary: Near-extremal black holes are controlled by a small set of soft modes, and counting these modes fixes the coefficient of $\log T$ in the entropy. We ask whether genuine six-derivative interactions change that count, working in seven-dimensional third-order Lovelock gravity, the simplest setting where the cubic Lovelock term is dynamical. The multiplicities stay the same, but the naive count fails. At fixed charge the Maxwell mode is frozen out, and the fifteen rotational modes of the $S^5$ act as a quantum rotor that only switches on above the scale $K_J^{-1}$. As a result, the coefficient of $\log T$ runs from $3/2$ at the lowest temperatures to $9$ above that scale, and never reaches the naive Gaussian value $19/2$. We compute the moment of inertia $K_J$ from the charged slow-rotation solution and find that the Lovelock couplings move the crossover without changing the multiplicities. Only large AdS black holes have a wide window in which the full rotational contribution competes with the classical entropy. Adding a probe charged scalar, we derive an analytic near-horizon Schwinger threshold in the cubic coupling. Its large-AdS limit tells us when the broad rotational crossover window can coexist with the absence of a charged-scalar Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound violation.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how six-derivative (cubic Lovelock) corrections affect the logarithmic correction to black hole entropy in seven-dimensional near-extremal charged black holes; it finds that while soft mode multiplicities are unchanged, the effective log-T coefficient runs from 3/2 to 9 across a temperature scale set by a quantum rotor crossover, and never reaches the Gaussian prediction 19/2; the moment of inertia K_J governing this crossover is computed analytically, and probe scalar analysis yields a Schwinger threshold linking rotational dynamics to BF-bound stability.
AI.motivation: To determine whether genuine higher-derivative interactions—specifically the dynamical cubic Lovelock term in 7D—alter the soft-mode counting that governs the log-T correction to near-extremal black hole entropy.
AI.method: Analyzes near-extremal black holes in 7D third-order Lovelock gravity; constructs the charged slow-rotation solution to compute the moment of inertia K_J; treats S^5 rotational modes as a quantum rotor; incorporates a probe charged scalar to derive an analytic near-horizon Schwinger pair-creation threshold; examines scaling limits (large AdS, low vs. high T) to map entropy corrections and stability constraints.
AI.result: The soft-mode multiplicities remain unchanged, but the Maxwell mode freezes out at fixed charge and the 15 S^5 rotational modes behave as a quantum rotor activating only above T ~ K_J^{-1}; thus the log-T coefficient runs from 3/2 (low-T) to 9 (high-T), skipping the naive Gaussian value 19/2; K_J depends on Lovelock couplings but not multiplicities; only large-AdS black holes exhibit a broad temperature window where rotational contributions significantly compete with classical entropy; the probe scalar yields a cubic-coupling-dependent Schwinger threshold whose large-AdS limit ensures compatibility with absence of BF-bound violation.
AI.conclusion: Higher-derivative interactions do not alter soft-mode degeneracies but qualitatively reshape their thermal activation, leading to scale-dependent logarithmic entropy corrections; the entropy’s log-T coefficient is not universal but runs with temperature due to emergent quantum-rotor physics, and its behavior is tightly constrained by both gravitational and probe-field consistency conditions.

title: Weyl Rescalings: A First Order Approach
summary: Weyl transformations, --local rescalings in which the metric transforms as $g_{\mu\nu}(x)\longrightarrow \Omega^2(x)\, g_{\mu \nu}(x)$--, are expected to be a symmetry of nature at extremely high energy, that should be (spontaneously) broken at low energy. In Cartan's first order formulation of gravity this translates into the condition that the local frames (vielbein) scale as $e^a(x) \longrightarrow \Omega(x) e^a(x)$. In this construction, the Lorentz connection one-form fields $\omega^a{}_b$ are independent from $e^a$, and since Lorentz transformations and dilatations commute, $\omega$ and $R(\omega)$ must be Weyl invariant, while in the second order metric formalism the Ricci tensor undergoes a non-homogeneous transformation. This generates a tension between the two formulations, which should be equivalent in the vanishing torsion limit. Here we show how the puzzle can be resolved taking into account the role of torsion. This also sheds some light on the conformal coupling of matter fields to gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves a tension between Cartan's first-order and the metric second-order formulations of gravity regarding Weyl (conformal) invariance, showing that torsion plays a crucial role in restoring consistency and clarifying conformal coupling of matter.
AI.motivation: To resolve an apparent inconsistency between Weyl invariance properties of curvature in Cartan’s first-order (vielbein + independent Lorentz connection) versus metric second-order gravity, particularly in the vanishing torsion limit where the formulations should agree.
AI.method: Analysis of Weyl transformation behavior of geometric objects (vielbein, Lorentz connection, curvature) in first-order Cartan formalism; explicit comparison with second-order metric formalism; incorporation of torsion as a key degree of freedom to reconcile transformation properties of the Ricci tensor and ensure equivalence in the torsionless limit.
AI.result: Demonstrates that torsion mediates the correct Weyl transformation of the Ricci tensor in first-order formalism, eliminating the tension; clarifies how conformal coupling of matter fields naturally emerges when torsion is properly accounted for.
AI.conclusion: The apparent discrepancy between formulations is not fundamental but stems from neglecting torsion’s role in Weyl-covariant geometry; full consistency—and physically appropriate conformal coupling—is restored only when torsion is treated as dynamical or constrained appropriately.

title: Horizon exchange and the universal all-spin response of Kerr
comment: 5 pages, 1 figure and supplementary material. Codes available at Github this https URL and Zenodo this https URL
summary: The radial Teukolsky equation is invariant under exchange of the outer and inner horizons, although the physical boundary condition is not. We derive an exact monodromy relation between the corresponding Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi (MST) near-zone responses. At leading order in frequency and to all orders in spin, this relation yields, for every multipole, an expression for the leading horizon-exchange-odd response. For gravitational perturbations, it determines the exchange-odd contribution to quadrupolar absorption and organizes the exchange-even dynamical response into a digamma function whose expansion accounts for the odd- and even-zeta structures found in Kerr-Compton calculations. The exact relation, rather than the individual previously known small-spin coefficients, is the central result.

AI.tldr: This paper derives an exact monodromy relation between near-zone responses under horizon exchange in the radial Teukolsky equation, yielding leading-order horizon-exchange-odd contributions and organizing dynamical response via a digamma function—revealing zeta-structure origins in Kerr-Compton scattering.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between the horizon-exchange symmetry of the radial Teukolsky equation and the asymmetry of physical boundary conditions, and to unify and explain previously observed zeta-function structures in Kerr black hole perturbation theory.
AI.method: Exact monodromy analysis of the Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi (MST) near-zone solutions; asymptotic expansion in frequency and all orders in black hole spin; identification of horizon-exchange-odd/even response components.
AI.result: An exact monodromy relation linking MST near-zone responses under outer/inner horizon exchange; explicit leading-order expression for horizon-exchange-odd response per multipole; for gravitational quadrupoles, full determination of exchange-odd absorption; organization of exchange-even response into a digamma function whose series expansion reproduces odd- and even-zeta terms seen in Kerr-Compton calculations.
AI.conclusion: The exact monodromy relation—not the small-spin expansion coefficients—is the fundamental structural result, providing a unified analytic framework for horizon-symmetry breaking and explaining emergent zeta-function patterns in black hole scattering.

title: Confining strings in the reconfined phase of trace deformed three dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills theory
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures. Contribution to the Proceedings of Lattice 2026, University of Maryland, July 26 - August 1, 2026. PoS(LATTICE2026)242
summary: Adding a trace deformation to the Yang-Mills action keeps the theory confining above the standard deconfinement temperature, in the so-called reconfined phase. We study the confining flux tube of the trace-deformed $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ theory in three dimensions with lattice simulations of Polyakov loop correlators. As the deformation increases, the ground state energy departs from the usual Nambu-Gotō effective string description, and deep in the reconfined phase the data are accurately described by the Polchinski-Yang rigid string, an effective string dominated by an extrinsic-curvature term.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how trace deformation affects confinement in SU(2) Yang-Mills theory in 3D using lattice simulations; it finds that increasing deformation drives the confining flux tube from Nambu-Goto to Polchinski-Yang rigid string behavior.
AI.motivation: To understand how confinement persists above the deconfinement temperature via trace deformation, and to characterize the effective string description of the confining flux tube in the reconfined phase.
AI.method: Lattice simulations of Polyakov loop correlators in (2+1)D trace-deformed SU(2) Yang-Mills theory, extracting ground-state flux tube energy spectra as a function of interquark separation and deformation strength.
AI.result: The ground-state energy deviates from the Nambu-Gotō prediction with increasing trace deformation; deep in the reconfined phase, it matches the Polchinski-Yang rigid string model—dominated by extrinsic curvature—within statistical and systematic uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: Trace deformation induces a qualitative change in the effective string theory governing the confining flux tube, signaling a transition from a Nambu-Gotō to a rigid string regime, consistent with enhanced stiffness due to extrinsic curvature suppression of fluctuations.

title: Can multi-level Monte-Carlo address the sign problem in a finite-density Bose gas?
summary: Numerical simulation of field theories with complex actions is frustrated by the sign problem, which causes an exponential growth in statistical sampling noise. A key example of such a theory is QCD at finite baryon chemical potential, which has important applications to the structure of atomic nuclei and neutron stars. Until now, the sign problem has precluded the possibility of first-principles numerical calculations that could provide key insight into these important physical systems. In this work, we propose an approach to avoiding this limitation by applying a reweighting procedure coupled with a multi-level Monte-Carlo sampling algorithm that offers an exponential enhancement of statistics to counteract the sign problem. We test the approach on a simpler model that displays the same sign problem at finite chemical potential. Our results demonstrate the promise of the proposed approach, significantly increasing the range over which precise calculations are possible, and providing improvements all the way up to the phase transition.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a multi-level Monte Carlo reweighting method to mitigate the sign problem in field theories with complex actions—particularly QCD at finite baryon chemical potential—enabling more precise first-principles numerical simulations up to the phase transition.
AI.motivation: The sign problem severely limits first-principles numerical simulations of field theories with complex actions (e.g., QCD at finite baryon chemical potential), hindering theoretical understanding of nuclear structure and neutron stars.
AI.method: A reweighting procedure combined with a multi-level Monte Carlo sampling algorithm, designed to exponentially enhance statistical precision and suppress sign-problem-induced noise.
AI.result: Demonstrated significant improvement in computational reach and precision on a test model sharing the same sign problem; calculations remain reliable up to the phase transition.
AI.conclusion: The proposed multi-level reweighting approach offers a viable pathway to overcome the sign problem in finite-density QCD and related theories, enabling previously inaccessible ab initio calculations.

title: A Note On Lattice Definition of Gauge Theories With Chiral Fermions
summary: Because of the fermion doubling problem, it has been a longstanding challenge to describe a lattice algorithm for studying four-dimensional gauge theories coupled to chiral fermions. Recently, an algorithm to do so has been described by Craig, extending partial results in the previous literature. Here we describe a variant of this algorithm, based on interpolating a lattice gauge field over the continuum (as in Craig's work) and coupling the interpolated gauge field to continuum chiral fermions. The same variant was also proposed recently by Hsu. In any dimension and for any anomaly-free representation, this approach can be implemented on a computer in principle, but not in practice by Monte Carlo methods because the chiral fermion path integral is not positive.

AI.tldr: Proposes a variant of Craig's algorithm for simulating chiral fermions on the lattice by interpolating gauge fields to the continuum and coupling them to continuum chiral fermions; theoretically generalizable but impractical for Monte Carlo due to sign problem.
AI.motivation: To overcome the fermion doubling problem in lattice formulations of 4D gauge theories with chiral fermions, a longstanding obstacle in non-perturbative quantum field theory simulations.
AI.method: Interpolates a discrete lattice gauge field to a smooth continuum gauge field (as in Craig's approach) and couples it to continuum chiral fermions; applicable in any dimension and for any anomaly-free representation.
AI.result: The method is theoretically well-defined and general—no fermion doubling, no restriction to specific dimensions or representations—but the chiral fermion path integral lacks positivity, rendering standard Monte Carlo sampling infeasible.
AI.conclusion: While the variant provides a conceptually clean, anomaly-free lattice–continuum hybrid framework for chiral fermions, its practical implementation via Monte Carlo is blocked by the complex/signed measure, leaving it as a formal advance rather than a computational tool.

title: SecRed: A program for sector-wise IBP reduction of Feynman integrals
summary: SecRed is a C++ program for the reduction of multi-loop Feynman integrals with integration-by-parts (IBP) identities. It reduces an integral family sector by sector for memory control and parallelism, and adds algorithms designed for that setting: an adaptive seed box with a corner cut, an optional seed truncation, a subsector level filter, and symmetry relations expanded only from the master integrals of a sector. A global stage assembles the retained equations and performs the finite-field reconstruction of the coefficients using FiniteFlow or FireFly, repeating the elimination over a sequence of primes. On the elimination side, a coefficient-free plan records the elimination order once and is replayed at each prime, so that only the arithmetic is repeated, and a head score orders the equations to reduce fill-in during the elimination. The program is demonstrated on a two-loop five-point non-planar family and on a four-loop cut family, where assembling the global equation system as a whole would exceed the memory of a single node.

AI.tldr: SecRed is a C++ program that efficiently reduces multi-loop Feynman integrals using IBP identities via sector-by-sector reduction, adaptive seeding, symmetry expansion from master integrals, and finite-field reconstruction with coefficient-free elimination plans.
AI.motivation: To overcome memory limitations and enable parallel computation in the reduction of large-scale multi-loop Feynman integral families—particularly when global equation assembly exceeds single-node memory capacity.
AI.method: Sector-by-sector IBP reduction with adaptive seed selection (corner-cut box, optional truncation), subsector-level filtering, symmetry relations expanded only from sector master integrals; global finite-field reconstruction (via FiniteFlow/FireFly) over multiple primes; coefficient-free elimination plan replayed per prime, guided by head-score ordering to minimize fill-in.
AI.result: Successful reduction of a two-loop five-point non-planar family and a four-loop cut family—both intractable for global reduction due to memory constraints—demonstrating scalability, memory control, and parallel efficiency.
AI.conclusion: SecRed enables practical, memory-efficient, and parallelizable reduction of large multi-loop Feynman integral families by combining sector-wise strategies, optimized elimination, and finite-field arithmetic.

title: Native transverse-momentum evolution and matching for TMD factorization and extraction
summary: We present a native transverse-momentum realization of the Collins/CSS2 leading-power transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization framework. The construction connects fixed-order distributional matching, origin contacts, unexpanded two-scale evolution, and a differentiable interface for hadronic structure. An endpoint-independent canonical scale with a specified infrared completion generates a Collins--Soper kernel on a common invariant domain. Complete canonical legs are bounded and admit constructive momentum-space evaluation through resolvent convolutions or elliptic solves. We give contact and finite-bin error bounds, parent-to-momentum-boundary translations, ordered flavor recurrences, and an all-order argument for the four exponent towers of $N^3\mathrm{LL}$ evolution. Localized joint-$(x,k_T)$ inputs, nonperturbative rapidity broadening, regulated moments and the full-spectrum subtraction are formulated as distinct parts of the prescription. The physical realization uses sourced four-loop beta/cusp and three-loop noncusp/Collins--Soper ingredients with strict-NLO hard/OPE boundaries. Non-Gaussian continuum tests and three-scale physical-PDF comparisons validate ordinary legs, contacts, individual insertions and analytic input derivatives.
