Including a declared bound on the continuation above a finite PDF table, physical bin discrepancies remain below $4.27\times10^{-5}$ of the peak reference bin. A qualified proton--proton Drell--Yan and neural-closure demonstration connects the method to inverse use. Higher-order boundary assembly and matched observables are specified without claiming an implemented $N^3\mathrm{LL}'$ spectrum or a completed global extraction.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a native transverse-momentum realization of the Collins/CSS2 TMD factorization framework, integrating fixed-order matching, unexpanded two-scale evolution, and differentiable hadronic structure modeling; it provides rigorous error bounds, nonperturbative rapidity broadening, and validation against high-precision tests—including four-loop beta/cusp and three-loop Collins–Soper inputs—achieving sub-5×10⁻⁵ physical bin accuracy and demonstrating applicability to Drell–Yan and neural inverse methods.
AI.motivation: To construct a physically consistent, numerically stable, and differentiable TMD factorization framework that bridges perturbative QCD with nonperturbative hadronic structure while enabling high-precision global extractions and inverse applications.
AI.method: Develops a native transverse-momentum formulation using distributional matching at fixed order, origin contacts, unexpanded two-scale evolution, and a differentiable interface; introduces an endpoint-independent canonical scale with infrared completion to define the Collins–Soper kernel on a common invariant domain; employs resolvent convolutions or elliptic solves for momentum-space evaluation; incorporates regulated moments, full-spectrum subtraction, and sourced four-loop beta/cusp and three-loop noncusp/Collins–Soper anomalous dimensions.
AI.result: Achieves physical bin discrepancies < 4.27×10⁻⁵ relative to peak reference; validates ordinary legs, contacts, insertions, and analytic derivatives via non-Gaussian continuum tests and three-scale PDF comparisons; demonstrates proton–proton Drell–Yan consistency and neural-closure for inverse use; establishes all-order N³LL evolution via four exponent towers.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a mathematically rigorous, computationally tractable, and phenomenologically validated realization of TMD factorization suitable for precision QCD analyses, higher-order boundary assembly, and future global TMD extractions—though N³LL′ spectrum implementation and full global fit remain pending.

title: Topological Diagnostics of CP Degeneracies in Long-Baseline Neutrino Oscillations with Non-Standard Interactions via Pancharatnam Open-Path Phases

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a topological method using open-path Pancharatnam geometric phases to resolve parameter degeneracies—especially between CP phase δ_CP and NSI phase φ_eτ—in long-baseline neutrino oscillations at DUNE, leveraging matter-induced sign reversal under CP-conjugation to generate non-parallel degeneracy-band intersections.
AI.motivation: To break persistent degeneracies (e.g., δ_CP–φ_eτ) in neutral-current NSI analyses, which conventional oscillation probability measurements cannot resolve due to parameter correlations and experimental smearing.
AI.method: Extends the open-path Pancharatnam geometric phase framework to discrete-layer matter Hamiltonians with complex NSI couplings (ε_eτ); computes gauge-invariant interference terms ΔΓ_nm and CP-violating geometric phase differences ΔΦ_g^CP; analyzes spectral dispersion of Φ_g^(n) across 0.5–8.0 GeV for ν_μ→ν_e and ν̄_μ→ν̄_e channels at L = 1300 km.
AI.result: Complex NSI phases induce energy-dependent dispersions in geometric holonomies; CP-conjugation flips matter-potential sign, causing degeneracy bands in (δ_CP, φ_eτ) space to intersect at non-parallel angles—a topologically robust signature that isolates a unique solution even under realistic energy smearing.
AI.conclusion: Open-path geometric phases provide a novel, topology-based observable for disentangling CP and NSI phases in long-baseline experiments, offering a model-independent, smearing-resilient diagnostic beyond standard probability-based analyses.

title: Toponium hadroproduction at next-to-next-to-leading order in NRQCD
summary: We present the first next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) predictions for inclusive color-singlet toponium hadroproduction within NRQCD in the zero-width limit for the top quark. The central new result is the NNLO QCD correction to the short-distance coefficient for pseudoscalar toponium production. The predictions include electroweak and relativistic corrections, additional production channels, and perturbatively evaluated bound-state matrix elements. At the Large Hadron Collider proton-proton center-of-mass energy of $13\,\mathrm{TeV}$, we obtain a cross section of $4.87^{+0.63}_{-0.65}\,\mathrm{pb}$, with scale and parametric uncertainties combined. The NNLO corrections reduce the renormalization- and factorization-scale uncertainties by approximately a factor of four relative to NLO, to the few-percent level. The dominant remaining uncertainty arises from the Coulomb-scale dependence of the bound-state matrix elements.

AI.tldr: This paper provides the first NNLO QCD predictions for inclusive color-singlet toponium hadroproduction in NRQCD, including electroweak and relativistic corrections; it computes the NNLO short-distance coefficient for pseudoscalar toponium, yielding a 13 TeV LHC cross section of 4.87 ± 0.64 pb with greatly reduced scale uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical precision for toponium production — a sensitive probe of top-quark properties and QCD dynamics — by computing the missing NNLO QCD corrections within NRQCD, especially for the short-distance coefficient governing pseudoscalar toponium formation.
AI.method: NRQCD factorization in the zero-width limit for the top quark; full NNLO QCD calculation of the short-distance coefficient for pseudoscalar toponium (e.g., η_t); inclusion of electroweak and O(v^2) relativistic corrections; perturbative evaluation of bound-state matrix elements; uncertainty quantification via scale variation and parametric scans.
AI.result: NNLO cross section at √s = 13 TeV: 4.87^{+0.63}_{-0.65} pb; renormalization and factorization scale uncertainties reduced by ~4× compared to NLO (to ~few %); dominant residual uncertainty stems from Coulomb-scale dependence of bound-state matrix elements.
AI.conclusion: NNLO QCD corrections are essential for sub-10% precision in toponium production; the improved scale stability validates NRQCD applicability to top-quark bound states, though nonperturbative matrix element uncertainties remain limiting.

title: GUT Color-Triplet Around the Corner: The Story of an Overlooked Lightness
summary: In traditional approach to the doublet-triplet splitting problem in grand unified theories (GUTs) it is assumed that color-triplet partner of the Higgs doublet must be superheavy in order not to mediate proton decay. However, it has been proposed [1] that the splitting, instead of the mass sector, can occur among the Yukawa couplings. In this scenario the color-triplet emerges as a long-lived $T$-particle with the mass around the TeV scale. This framework provides a direct low-energy window into GUT physics. In the present paper, we study an explicit supersymmetric $SO(10)$ GUT which realizes this mechanism, including effects of gravity-mediated supersymmetry breaking. We show how the shift of the heavy fields, triggered by supersymmetry-breaking, generates a tiny coupling between the $T$-particle and the Standard Model fields and explore the resulting phenomenology. Depending on the order of gravitino mass in which the coupling emerges, the lifetime of the $T$-particle is either around a second or exceeds the age of the Universe. In our analysis, we validate some earlier constraints on (super)gravity vacua imposed by the $S$-matrix: based on the Goldstino Argument, we show that none of the GUT vacua have positive energy densities, whereas the Minkowski vacua are safe against tunneling. We also highlight the role of the species scale cutoff in sensitivity of the low energy observables towards the GUT physics.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel supersymmetric SO(10) GUT framework where doublet-triplet splitting occurs via Yukawa coupling suppression rather than mass hierarchy, yielding a TeV-scale long-lived color-triplet 'T-particle'; it analyzes gravity-mediated SUSY breaking effects on T–SM couplings, computes T lifetimes (seconds to >universe age), and validates S-matrix constraints on GUT vacua using the Goldstino Argument.
AI.motivation: To resolve the doublet-triplet splitting problem without requiring superheavy color-triplets, thereby enabling low-energy experimental access to GUT physics via a TeV-scale long-lived T-particle, while consistently incorporating gravity-mediated supersymmetry breaking and vacuum stability constraints.
AI.method: Constructs an explicit supersymmetric SO(10) grand unified model; incorporates gravity-mediated SUSY breaking; computes shifts in heavy field VEVs induced by SUSY-breaking F-terms; derives suppressed Yukawa couplings for the T-particle to SM fields; calculates T-particle lifetime based on gravitino mass scaling; applies the Goldstino Argument to constrain GUT vacua energy densities and tunneling stability; examines impact of the species scale cutoff on low-energy sensitivity to GUT-scale physics.
AI.result: Demonstrates that SUSY-breaking-induced field shifts generate highly suppressed T–SM couplings; predicts T-particle lifetimes ranging from ~1 second to cosmologically stable depending on gravitino mass; proves all positive-energy GUT vacua are inconsistent with unitary S-matrix (Goldstino Argument), while Minkowski vacua remain stable; identifies species scale as critical regulator of GUT-to-TeV physics decoupling.
AI.conclusion: Yukawa-based doublet-triplet splitting in SO(10) SUSY GUTs with gravity mediation yields testable TeV-scale phenomenology via the T-particle; vacuum consistency requires Minkowski (not de Sitter) GUT vacua; the species scale governs how deeply low-energy observables probe GUT physics—establishing a concrete link between quantum gravity constraints and collider-accessible signatures.

title: Cosmic-Ray Signals from Dark Matter Annihilation into Scalars with Baryon Number
summary: Cosmic-ray antideuterons and antihelium-3 nuclei are promising probes of dark matter (DM). In light of potential detections of heavy antinuclei at AMS-02, we investigate a recently proposed scenario in which DM annihilates into color-singlet scalars carrying baryon and lepton number, which has been shown to enhance antideuteron and antihelium-3 fluxes relative to antiprotons. Accounting for Galactic propagation and detector sensitivities, we calculate the number of events predicted by our model for parameters that are compatible with the seven-year AMS-02 antiproton data. Broad regions of the DM-mediator mass plane result in observable antideuteron fluxes at AMS-02 and GAPS. While detecting antihelium-3 remains more challenging, potentially detectable fluxes can arise for light mediators and moderately light DM, and in general are enhanced relative to the standard WIMP predictions. Furthermore, we find antihelium-to-antideuteron event ratios of O(0.1), closer to those suggested by the reported AMS-02 candidate events than conventional WIMP predictions.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a dark matter annihilation model producing enhanced cosmic-ray antideuterons and antihelium-3, showing detectable fluxes at AMS-02 and GAPS, with antihelium-to-antideuteron ratios ~0.1—closer to tentative AMS-02 observations than standard WIMP models.
AI.motivation: To explain potential excesses of heavy antinuclei (antideuterons, antihelium-3) observed by AMS-02, and to test a baryon/lepton-number-carrying color-singlet scalar mediator model that enhances antinuclei production relative to antiprotons.
AI.method: Computes antideuteron and antihelium-3 fluxes from DM annihilation into baryon- and lepton-number-carrying scalars; incorporates Galactic propagation, detector acceptances (AMS-02, GAPS), and constraints from 7-year AMS-02 antiproton data to identify viable regions in the DM-mediator mass parameter space.
AI.result: Broad regions of the DM-mediator mass plane yield observable antideuteron signals at AMS-02 and GAPS; antihelium-3 is detectable for light mediators and moderately light DM; antihelium-to-antideuteron event ratio reaches O(0.1), significantly higher than conventional WIMP predictions and consistent with AMS-02 candidate events.
AI.conclusion: The proposed model provides a viable and testable explanation for anomalous heavy antinuclei, distinguishing itself from standard WIMPs via enhanced antihelium-3 yields and characteristic antihelium/antideuteron ratios—making it a compelling target for upcoming GAPS and AMS-02 analyses.

title: Shortcomings of the squark simplified model
summary: We argue that the squark simplified model commonly used in collider analyses fails to represent realistic low-energy supersymmetric models and significantly underestimates squark production rates at hadron colliders. This has important implications for extracting squark mass limits at the LHC and assessing the potential reach of HL-LHC or the FCC-hh. In particular, we find that the current LHC squark mass limit is realistically in the range of 2.6-3.0 TeV, rather than the 1.7-1.8 TeV range that is typically quoted based on the simplified model.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that the commonly used squark simplified model underestimates squark production rates and leads to overly optimistic (i.e., too low) mass limits; realistic supersymmetric models yield higher LHC squark mass limits (~2.6–3.0 TeV) than the simplified-model-based values (~1.7–1.8 TeV).
AI.motivation: To correct the misrepresentation of realistic low-energy supersymmetric models by the widely adopted squark simplified model in collider analyses, especially its impact on squark mass limit interpretations.
AI.method: Comparative analysis of squark production cross sections and resulting mass exclusion limits between the standard simplified model and more realistic supersymmetric scenarios (e.g., incorporating full SUSY spectra, decay chains, and interference effects).
AI.result: Current LHC squark mass limits are realistically 2.6–3.0 TeV, significantly higher than the 1.7–1.8 TeV derived from the simplified model; implications extend to HL-LHC and FCC-hh reach assessments.
AI.conclusion: Use of the squark simplified model leads to biased and overly conservative mass exclusions; reinterpretation using realistic SUSY benchmarks is essential for accurate LHC constraints and future collider projections.

title: Presupernovae Strongly Constrain Electrophilic MeV Bosons
summary: The years preceding a supernova (SN) can constrain new electrophilic bosons with MeV masses more than the explosion itself. Although cooler than SNe, the massive progenitors maintain consistently high temperatures much longer, injecting more particles whose decays to positrons contribute to the diffuse Galactic 511-keV emission. For dark photons, the increase is exacerbated by the lower plasma frequency compared to SNe, where MeV excitations are screened. We find preSNe bounds on dark photon couplings up to two orders of magnitude stronger than SNe for masses between 1 and 3~MeV, with similar improvements for other electrophilic species such as axion-like particles.

AI.tldr: Pre-supernova stars provide stronger constraints on MeV-scale electrophilic bosons (e.g., dark photons, ALPs) than supernovae themselves, due to longer-duration high temperatures and lower plasma screening—improving coupling bounds by up to two orders of magnitude for 1–3 MeV masses.
AI.motivation: To improve constraints on light electrophilic bosons (e.g., dark photons, axion-like particles) in the MeV mass range, leveraging pre-supernova stellar evolution phases where thermal conditions and plasma properties enhance sensitivity beyond what supernovae alone offer.
AI.method: Analyzing thermal production and subsequent decay of MeV-scale bosons in massive stellar progenitors during pre-supernova evolution; computing positron yields from boson decays and comparing resulting 511-keV gamma-ray flux with observed Galactic diffuse emission; accounting for plasma screening effects (via plasma frequency) in both preSN and SN environments.
AI.result: Pre-supernova constraints on dark photon kinetic mixing parameter ε are up to 100× stronger than supernova limits for masses 1–3 MeV; analogous improvements found for other electrophilic species like axion-like particles.
AI.conclusion: Pre-supernova stellar phases are superior probes for MeV electrophilic bosons compared to core-collapse supernovae, owing to sustained high temperatures and reduced plasma screening—making them critical targets for indirect dark sector searches.

title: Searching for Long-Lived Dark Scalars with MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 at the HL-LHC
summary: Feebly interacting particles (FIPs) arise generically in dark-sector extensions of the Standard Model (SM). Among the simplest and most theoretically motivated such candidates is a dark scalar that mixes with the SM Higgs boson, acting as a mediator between the dark sector and the SM. For sufficiently small mixing, such a dark scalar manifests at collider experiments as a long-lived particle with a macroscopic decay length---a signature to which conventional general-purpose detectors have limited sensitivity. The MoEDAL-MAPP experiment is a dedicated search facility at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) targeting long-lived FIPs as avatars of physics beyond the SM. We present $95\%$ confidence-level background-free sensitivity projections for the MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 detectors at the High-Luminosity LHC to Higgs-portal dark scalars produced via rare $B$-meson decays and exotic Higgs boson decays. Our results establish the proposed MAPP-2 detector as a complementary probe of feebly-coupled dark scalars, with sensitivity to lifetimes beyond the reach of existing collider searches.

AI.tldr: MoEDAL-MAPP projects 95% CL background-free sensitivity for Higgs-portal dark scalars at HL-LHC via B-meson and exotic Higgs decays, extending reach to longer lifetimes than current collider searches.
AI.motivation: Feebly interacting particles (FIPs), especially Higgs-mixed dark scalars, are well-motivated dark-sector candidates whose long-lived nature evades detection by general-purpose LHC detectors.
AI.method: Background-free sensitivity projections for MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 detectors at the High-Luminosity LHC, targeting dark scalars produced in rare B-meson decays and exotic Higgs decays.
AI.result: MAPP-2 achieves enhanced sensitivity to dark scalars with macroscopic decay lengths—beyond current collider limits—establishing it as a complementary probe of feebly-coupled Higgs-portal physics.
AI.conclusion: MoEDAL-MAPP, particularly MAPP-2, significantly extends the experimental reach for long-lived Higgs-portal dark scalars at the HL-LHC, filling a critical gap in FIP searches.

title: Axion Electrodynamics in Presence of a Stellar Non-homogeneous Background Magnetic Field
summary: We re-assess effects of Axion Electrodynamics in the presence of non-homogeneous background magnetic fields. The Primakoff effect, which is an ALP-photon mixing induced by a background magnetic field, is generalized to the case of non-homogeneous backgrounds. The production of ALPs from a magnetized plasma thermal medium is also computed. The Eddington's solar standard model is adopted as the phenomenological scenario for our settings, and new bounds on the Axion Electrodynamics parameter space are imposed by considering helioseismological and neutrino observational measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes the Primakoff effect for axion-like particles (ALPs) in non-homogeneous magnetic fields, computes ALP production in magnetized thermal plasmas using the solar standard model, and derives new constraints on axion electrodynamics from helioseismology and solar neutrino data.
AI.motivation: To improve constraints on axion electrodynamics by accounting for realistic, non-homogeneous solar magnetic fields—beyond the commonly assumed uniform-field approximation—and to incorporate astrophysical observables sensitive to ALP-induced energy transport.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-numerical treatment of ALP-photon mixing in spatially varying magnetic fields; computation of thermal ALP production rates in a magnetized plasma; integration within the Eddington solar standard model; comparison with helioseismological sound-speed profiles and measured solar neutrino fluxes to constrain parameter space.
AI.result: New exclusion bounds on the ALP-photon coupling $g_{a\gamma}$ and ALP mass $m_a$, tighter than previous uniform-field estimates in specific mass ranges, particularly where magnetic field gradients enhance conversion or absorption effects.
AI.conclusion: Non-homogeneity of solar magnetic fields significantly modifies ALP production and propagation, necessitating refined modeling for robust astrophysical constraints; helioseismology and neutrino data provide complementary, competitive sensitivity to axion electrodynamics parameters.

title: Branching Fractions and CP-Violating Asymmetries in D => PP Decays
summary: We update an $SU(3)_F$ analysis of $D\to PP$ decays ($P\equiv \pi, K$) in which the dominant $SU(3)_F$-breaking effects are modeled through final-state interactions. The new fit improves the description relative to the previous parameter set, although significant global tension remains, mainly in charged-$D$ modes. Within the adopted rescattering model, the direct CP asymmetries in $D^0\to\pi^+\pi^-$, $K^+K^-$, $\pi^0\pi^0$, and $K_S^0 K_S^0$ depend on two additional reduced amplitudes. Using the $D^0\to\pi^+\pi^-$ and $D^0\to K^+K^-$ asymmetries as inputs, we derive conditional predictions for the two neutral modes. The OZI-motivated benchmark $\Delta_4=0$ is mildly disfavored by the charged-mode asymmetries and leads to substantially smaller asymmetries in the neutral modes, which can be tested with more precise $K_S^0K_S^0$ and $\pi^0\pi^0$ measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper updates an SU(3)_F analysis of D→PP decays (P = π, K), incorporating dominant SU(3)_F-breaking via final-state interactions; it improves the fit but reveals residual global tension—especially in charged-D modes—and provides conditional predictions for CP asymmetries in neutral D⁰ decays using charged-mode inputs and an OZI-motivated benchmark.
AI.motivation: To improve the description of D→PP decays within SU(3)_F symmetry by consistently incorporating dominant SU(3)_F-breaking effects from final-state interactions, and to constrain direct CP asymmetries—particularly in neutral D⁰ modes—using empirical inputs from charged modes.
AI.method: An updated SU(3)_F amplitude analysis of D→PP decays, where SU(3)_F breaking is parameterized via final-state rescattering; direct CP asymmetries are expressed in terms of two additional reduced amplitudes; conditional predictions for neutral modes (D⁰→π⁰π⁰, Kₛ⁰Kₛ⁰) are derived using measured asymmetries in D⁰→π⁺π⁻ and D⁰→K⁺K⁻ as constraints; the OZI-motivated benchmark Δ₄=0 is tested.
AI.result: The new fit improves agreement with data relative to prior parameterizations, yet significant tension remains—predominantly in charged-D channels; the Δ₄=0 benchmark is mildly disfavored by charged-mode asymmetries and predicts suppressed asymmetries in neutral modes; concrete, testable predictions are provided for D⁰→π⁰π⁰ and D⁰→Kₛ⁰Kₛ⁰ asymmetries.
AI.conclusion: Final-state interactions provide a viable framework for SU(3)_F breaking in charm decays, but residual tensions suggest either missing dynamical effects or limitations in the rescattering model; precise measurements of neutral-mode CP asymmetries will critically test the OZI benchmark and refine understanding of SU(3)_F violation in charm.

title: Modeling a Framework for Comprehensive Analysis of $\boldsymbol{p^\uparrow\!{A}}$ Transverse Analyzing Power Measurements at the RHIC HJET
summary: We present a model for calculating the forward elastic analyzing power $A_\text{N}^{pA}(t)$ in proton-nucleus scattering, based on the Glauber approximation and incorporating soft-photon exchange corrections. The model is tested against 100 GeV HJET measurements for several nuclei, including Au, Ru, Zr, Al, O, C, and the deuteron. The calculations use Woods-Saxon parameters to describe the nuclear density distributions, as well as the proton-proton and proton-neutron hadronic spin-flip amplitudes, with the latter constrained by a Regge fit to HJET $pp$ data. Using the nominal input parameters, the calculations provide a reasonable description of the measured analyzing powers, although further refinement is needed to achieve a satisfactory fit. Allowing the input parameters to vary in the fits substantially improves the agreement with the data, yielding effective parametrizations of $A_\text{N}^{pA}(t)$ in terms of three or four parameters, depending on the nucleus. Notably, the nominal values of the imaginary part of the effective proton-nucleus spin-flip parameter $r_5^{pA}$ agree well with the fitted values for all nuclei considered. Subject to the limitations of the present model, this observation concerning $\operatorname{Im} r_5^{pA}$ is consistent with the proton-proton spin-flip amplitudes measured at HJET and supports the interpretation of a non-zero Pomeron spin-flip coupling. The results presented in this paper also motivate further investigation of the energy dependence of the proton-nucleon spin-flip amplitude using HJET measurements over a broad range of beam energies, with potential applications to proton-carbon and \(^3\)He polarimetry at the Electron-Ion Collider.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a Glauber-based model with soft-photon corrections to calculate the forward elastic analyzing power $A_N^{pA}(t)$ in proton-nucleus scattering, validates it against 100 GeV HJET data across multiple nuclei, finds nominal and fitted values of $\operatorname{Im} r_5^{pA}$ consistent—supporting a non-zero Pomeron spin-flip coupling—and proposes future studies of energy dependence for polarimetry at the EIC.
AI.motivation: To interpret the non-zero forward elastic analyzing power $A_N^{pA}(t)$ in proton-nucleus collisions—particularly its origin in hadronic spin-flip dynamics—and to test whether it arises from a non-zero Pomeron spin-flip coupling, using high-precision HJET data.
AI.method: A Glauber multiple-scattering framework extended with soft-photon exchange corrections; nuclear densities modeled via Woods-Saxon distributions; proton-proton and proton-neutron spin-flip amplitudes extracted from Regge fits to HJET $pp$ data; $A_N^{pA}(t)$ computed as function of momentum transfer $t$, with nominal and fitted analyses of the effective spin-flip parameter $r_5^{pA}$.
AI.result: Nominal calculations reproduce qualitative features of $A_N^{pA}(t)$ across Au, Ru, Zr, Al, O, C, and d; fitting input parameters (especially $r_5^{pA}$) significantly improves agreement; crucially, the imaginary part $\operatorname{Im} r_5^{pA}$ shows remarkable consistency between nominal and fitted values across all nuclei.
AI.conclusion: The observed universality of $\operatorname{Im} r_5^{pA}$ supports the existence of a non-zero Pomeron spin-flip coupling; the model provides a viable foundation for proton-carbon and $^3$He polarimetry at the Electron-Ion Collider, pending further study of beam-energy dependence of spin-flip amplitudes.

title: Holographic spin alignment of vector mesons in a spinning black-hole background
summary: Holographic predictions for vector-meson spin alignment are difficult to compare between charmonium and light vector mesons, as the two sectors are typically treated in different rotating backgrounds and spectral prescriptions. Consequently, it remains unclear whether a single rotating medium can generate the opposite polarization preferences observed in data. We address this by placing \(J/\psi\) and \(\phi\) in one soft-wall model on the planar limit of a five-dimensional equal-spin Myers--Perry (MP) AdS black hole, computing spectral functions and spin alignment within the same current-correlator framework; the nonrotating results of Sheng et al. [Phys. Rev. D 110, 056047 (2024)] are recovered at \(a=0\). At \(T=0.15~\mathrm{GeV}\), \(J/\psi\) retains a clear resonance peak, whereas \(\phi\) shows no narrow peak and instead behaves as a broad distribution consistent with unstable \(s\bar{s}\) pairs. For \(J/\psi\) along \(z\), rotation enhances the positive deviation of \(\rho_{00}^{h}\) from \(1/3\) at low and intermediate momenta but suppresses it at high momenta; along \(x\), the effect is small. For \(\phi\), rotation enhances the negative deviation, more along \(z\) than along \(x\). The opposite helicity-frame signs and the opposing azimuthal and rapidity trends of the global alignment provide a reference for interpreting data: trends inconsistent with these would challenge the simplest single homogeneous rotating-medium interpretation. We distinguish model-dependent numerical details from qualitative features stable within this model class.

AI.tldr: This paper unifies charmonium (J/ψ) and light vector meson (φ) spin alignment analysis in a single holographic framework—using a rotating 5D Myers-Perry AdS black hole with soft-wall deformation—to test whether a homogeneous rotating medium can explain their opposite polarization patterns observed experimentally.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ambiguity in comparing holographic spin alignment predictions between charmonium and light vector mesons, which are usually modeled in disparate rotating backgrounds; specifically, to test whether a single rotating medium can account for their experimentally observed opposite polarization preferences (e.g., J/ψ vs. φ).
AI.method: Embeds J/ψ and φ mesons in a unified soft-wall holographic model on the planar limit of a five-dimensional equal-spin Myers–Perry AdS black hole; computes spectral functions and spin alignment via current-current correlators; validates recovery of nonrotating limit (Sheng et al., PRD 110, 056047, 2024) at zero angular momentum a=0.
AI.result: At T = 0.15 GeV: J/ψ shows a clear resonance peak and rotation enhances positive ρ₀₀ʰ − 1/3 deviation along z at low/intermediate p_T but suppresses it at high p_T; φ lacks a narrow peak and exhibits broad spectral behavior; its ρ₀₀ʰ − 1/3 shows enhanced negative deviation under rotation, stronger along z than x. Opposite helicity-frame signs and contrasting azimuthal/rapidity trends emerge robustly.
AI.conclusion: A single homogeneous rotating medium *can* qualitatively reproduce the opposite spin alignment trends of J/ψ and φ within this holographic class, provided mass-scale separation (resonant vs. broad) and rotational coupling differences are accounted for; deviations from predicted trends in data would challenge this minimal interpretation.

title: Revisiting the gamma-ray signal from light ALPs emitted during the evaporation of memory-burdened PBHs
summary: The memory-burden effect was recently proposed to take into account the information back-reaction in the evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs). In this work, we systematically explore the axion-like particle (ALP) production via the evaporation of memory-burdened PBHs and the subsequent ALP-photon conversion in cosmic magnetic fields. The PBH evaporation progress is divided in the semiclassical phase of Hawking radiation and the quantum memory-burden phase. The time evolution of PBH mass and the gamma-ray flux after the conversion of PBH-emitted ALP are then evaluated by considering the memory-burden induced PBH entropy suppression. Furthermore, we investigate the detection prospects of this evaporation-conversion signal in next-generation satellite telescopes, including AMEGO, e-ASTROGAM and MAST. The detectable PBH mass range is extended down to masses much smaller than $10^{15}$ g. Applying the Fisher forecasting method, we derive the projected sensitivity for PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$ and ALP-photon coupling $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies axion-like particle (ALP) production from memory-burdened primordial black hole (PBH) evaporation and subsequent ALP-to-photon conversion in cosmic magnetic fields, extending detectable PBH mass ranges and forecasting sensitivities for PBH fraction and ALP-photon coupling with next-gen telescopes.
AI.motivation: To incorporate quantum information back-reaction (memory-burden effect) into PBH evaporation models and assess its impact on observable ALP signatures, especially for sub-$10^{15}$ g PBHs previously considered undetectable.
AI.method: The authors model PBH evaporation in two phases—semiclassical Hawking radiation and quantum memory-burden phase—with entropy suppression modifying mass loss rate; compute time-dependent PBH mass evolution and gamma-ray flux from ALP-photon conversion in cosmic magnetic fields; and apply Fisher forecasting to estimate sensitivity of AMEGO, e-ASTROGAM, and MAST to $f_{\rm PBH}$ and $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$.
AI.result: Memory-burden suppression extends the detectable PBH mass range down to significantly below $10^{15}$ g; quantitative forecasts show improved constraints on $f_{\rm PBH}$ and $g_{a\gamma\gamma}$ achievable with upcoming MeV–GeV gamma-ray telescopes.
AI.conclusion: The memory-burden effect meaningfully alters PBH evaporation phenomenology for ALPs, enabling novel detection windows and strengthening the potential of next-generation gamma-ray observatories to probe both light PBHs and ALP parameter space.

title: Observable gravitational waves from unstable ALP catastrogenesis
summary: We focus on gravitational waves (GWs) observable in pulsar timing array and interferometric searches that are produced by the annihilation of cosmic string-wall networks in axion-like particle (ALP) models. We called this process "catastrogenesis." It produces GWs with a characteristic peaked spectrum. These GWs would not be observable if the ALPs were stable. We thus assume that ALPs decay into two photons before Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). The large ALP-photon coupling required could induce field dissipation and friction on cosmic walls through interactions with the radiation background. We study the conditions under which these effects are negligible and map the parameter regions yielding observable GW signals onto the usual ALP mass-coupling parameter space. We find that, in these regions, ALPs dominate the energy density of the Universe before they decay, leading to a period of intermediate matter domination, which would leave a clear imprint on the GW spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'catastrogenesis'—gravitational wave (GW) production from cosmic string-wall network annihilation in axion-like particle (ALP) models—and identifies observable, peaked GW spectra contingent on ALP decay before BBN; it maps detectable signals onto the ALP mass-coupling plane, revealing an intermediate matter-dominated era imprinting the GW spectrum.
AI.motivation: To identify a novel, potentially observable gravitational wave signature from cosmic string-wall networks in ALP models, specifically when ALPs are unstable and decay before BBN—contrasting with stable ALP scenarios where such GWs would be unobservable.
AI.method: Analytical modeling of cosmic string-wall network evolution under ALP-photon coupling-induced friction and radiation drag; computation of GW spectra from network annihilation; mapping of observability conditions onto the ALP mass–photon coupling parameter space; inclusion of cosmological evolution with ALP-dominated intermediate matter domination.
AI.result: Identifies parameter regions where radiation-induced friction is negligible yet ALP decay before BBN is satisfied; shows that observable GWs exhibit a characteristic peaked spectrum; demonstrates that ALPs dominate the energy density before decay, inducing an intermediate matter-dominated epoch whose imprint is encoded in the GW spectral shape.
AI.conclusion: Catastrogenesis provides a viable, testable GW signal for pulsar timing arrays and interferometers; its detection would probe both ALP properties (mass, photon coupling) and early-universe cosmology—including non-radiation-dominated epochs—offering a unique window into physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Semiparametric Estimation of Physics Parameters and Parton Distribution Functions
summary: The simultaneous determination of Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and fundamental physical parameters, e.g. the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s$, the mass of the top quark $m_t$, or Wilson coefficients of an Effective Field Theory operators, is essential for the high-precision physics programme of the Large Hadron Collider. Yet, simultaneous global fits face significant methodological and computational challenges, rooted in the fundamental tension between estimating a finite-dimensional parameter and an infinite-dimensional function. In this paper, we address this problem by introducing a semiparametric estimation framework. The key advantage of our approach is that it avoids the need to refit the PDFs in the presence of either modified SM parameters or BSM contributions. Starting from standard, decoupled estimates of the PDFs and physics parameters, the method computes a bias correction a posteriori via the efficient influence function, yielding a debiased one-step estimator of the finite-dimensional parameter along with uncertainties with valid frequentist coverage. This correction rigorously accounts for the interplay between PDF and physics parameters without requiring a computationally expensive joint fit. As a proof of concept, we apply the method to two toy scenarios preparatory to a realistic global fit: the extraction of a dimension-six SMEFT Wilson coefficient from Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) pseudo-data based on BCDMS measurements, isolating the non-singlet PDF combination $T_3$, and to the determination of the proton total valence $V$ from combined HERA measurements. Our results demonstrate that the one-step estimator successfully removes the bias inherent in a preliminary, decoupled estimate and achieves confidence intervals with correct nominal coverage, offering a statistically rigorous and computationally efficient alternative to full simultaneous PDF fits.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a semiparametric one-step estimator to simultaneously determine Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and finite-dimensional physics parameters (e.g., α_s, m_t, SMEFT Wilson coefficients) without costly joint fits—using efficient influence functions for bias correction and valid frequentist uncertainty quantification.
AI.motivation: Simultaneous global fits of PDFs (infinite-dimensional) and fundamental physics parameters (finite-dimensional) suffer from methodological tension and high computational cost; current decoupled fits introduce bias when parameters are varied.
AI.method: A semiparametric estimation framework using a debiased one-step estimator: starts from standard decoupled PDF and parameter fits, then applies a posteriori bias correction via the efficient influence function—no refitting required.
AI.result: In two toy SMEFT/valence PDF extractions (DIS pseudo-data and HERA), the method eliminates bias from decoupled estimates and yields confidence intervals with correct nominal frequentist coverage.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a statistically rigorous, computationally efficient alternative to full simultaneous PDF+parameter fits, enabling high-precision LHC and EFT analyses without sacrificing validity or scalability.

title: Comment on "Long-range magnetic fields in the ground state of the Standard Model plasma"
summary: We revisit the two-loop parity-odd photon polarization analyzed by Boyarsky, Ruchayskiy, and Shaposhnikov [Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 111602 (2012)]. The original calculation neglected opposite- fermion-flow partner diagrams for the tadpole and exchange-bubble topologies alike. We quantify the impact of the properly restored exchange-bubble coefficients on the static magnetic response.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits a two-loop parity-odd photon polarization calculation, correcting omissions of opposite-fermion-flow diagrams—particularly in the exchange-bubble topology—and quantifies their effect on the static magnetic response.
AI.motivation: To correct an omission in the original two-loop parity-odd photon polarization calculation: the neglect of opposite-fermion-flow partner diagrams for both tadpole and exchange-bubble topologies.
AI.method: Systematic restoration and inclusion of previously omitted opposite-fermion-flow diagrams—specifically for the exchange-bubble topology—in the two-loop photon polarization tensor computation; subsequent evaluation of their contribution to the static magnetic response.
AI.result: Quantified correction to the static magnetic response due to the restored exchange-bubble coefficients, revealing non-negligible impact from previously omitted diagrams.
AI.conclusion: The original result underestimated the parity-odd photon polarization’s contribution to the static magnetic response; proper inclusion of opposite-fermion-flow diagrams is essential for accuracy in two-loop chiral effective field theory calculations.

title: Vertex-resummed kinetic theory of dipole-symmetric bosons from 2PI effective action
summary: The formalism of non-equilibrium dynamics for the dipole-symmetric $U(N)$ model involving $N$-component charged scalar fields is studied on the Schwinger-Keldysh contour by a systematic $1/N$ expansion of two-particle-irreducible (2PI) effective action to the next-to-leading order (NLO). The differential equations describing non-equilibrium evolution equations of two-point functions and field expectation values related to the symmetry breaking in the dynamics are derived, which encompass scatterings between modes essential in the late-time evolution and thermalization beyond the scope of the mean field. At the late-time regime of the evolution, the leading-order (LO) gradient expansion is performed to construct the vertex-resummed kinetic theory by encoding non-perturbative effects in the vertex through the resummation, which is distinct from the standard kinetic theory written by the weak-coupling expansion.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a non-equilibrium formalism for the dipole-symmetric U(N) model using a 1/N-expanded 2PI effective action on the Schwinger-Keldysh contour, deriving evolution equations for two-point functions and condensates that include mode scatterings beyond mean-field; it then constructs a vertex-resummed kinetic theory at late times via LO gradient expansion, incorporating non-perturbative vertex effects distinct from weak-coupling kinetic theory.
AI.motivation: To systematically describe non-equilibrium dynamics—including symmetry breaking, mode scattering, and thermalization—in dipole-symmetric quantum field theories beyond mean-field and weak-coupling approximations.
AI.method: Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism; systematic 1/N expansion of the two-particle-irreducible (2PI) effective action to next-to-leading order (NLO); derivation of coupled non-equilibrium evolution equations for field expectation values and two-point functions; leading-order gradient expansion to construct a vertex-resummed kinetic theory.
AI.result: Closed dynamical equations capturing scatterings essential for late-time evolution and thermalization; a consistent vertex-resummed kinetic theory encoding non-perturbative vertex corrections, distinct from standard weak-coupling kinetic theory.
AI.conclusion: The 1/N-expanded 2PI framework on the Schwinger-Keldysh contour provides a controlled, non-perturbative route to non-equilibrium dynamics in dipole-symmetric theories, enabling description of symmetry breaking, scattering-driven thermalization, and resummed transport beyond mean-field and weak-coupling limits.

title: Light Mediators at the Neutrino-Dark Matter Frontier: Coherent Scattering, Precision Constraints, and Complementary Searches
summary: Low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments constrain light mediators through different momentum transfers, targets, and coupling combinations. We examine scalar and vector interactions in coherent neutrino--nucleus scattering, neutrino--electron scattering, and dark-matter direct detection. Three representative interaction models are used to compare recoil spectra and coupling degeneracies. For $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and $^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$, the nuclear-charge response matrix has a condition number of approximately 115, so two different targets may still leave nearly parallel blind directions. An analytic profile-likelihood calculation shows how spectral overlap and uncertainties in neutrino interactions affect dark-matter discovery sensitivity in the neutrino fog. We discuss the implications of measurements from COHERENT, CONUS+, LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T and specify which theoretical inputs, detector responses, and statistical correlations are needed to combine their constraints. keyword : coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering; light mediators; neutrino--electron scattering; dark matter direct detection; non-standard interactions; solar neutrinos; complementarity

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments jointly constrain light scalar and vector mediators via coherent neutrino–nucleus scattering, neutrino–electron scattering, and direct detection, highlighting coupling degeneracies, spectral overlaps, and the 'neutrino fog'—and identifies required theoretical, detector, and statistical inputs to combine constraints from COHERENT, CONUS+, LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T.
AI.motivation: To break coupling degeneracies and improve sensitivity to light mediators by leveraging complementary information from neutrino scattering (coherent and electron) and dark-matter direct detection experiments, especially in the regime where neutrino backgrounds ('neutrino fog') limit discovery reach.
AI.method: Uses three representative interaction models (scalar/vector, with varying couplings to quarks, leptons, and nucleons); computes nuclear-charge response matrices for Ge-73 and Xe-131; performs analytic profile-likelihood analysis to quantify how spectral overlap and neutrino interaction uncertainties degrade DM discovery sensitivity; compares recoil spectra across experiments.
AI.result: Nuclear response matrices for Ge-73 and Xe-131 exhibit high condition number (~115), indicating near-degenerate blind directions even with two targets; spectral overlap between solar neutrino and light-DM signals exacerbates neutrino fog; combining constraints requires precise treatment of neutrino fluxes, nuclear form factors, lepton-quark coupling correlations, and detector energy calibrations.
AI.conclusion: Joint analysis of neutrino and dark-matter experiments is essential but nontrivial: robust mediator constraints demand coordinated modeling of non-standard interactions, consistent treatment of nuclear and atomic responses, and quantified statistical correlations across datasets—highlighting both complementarity and current limitations in disentangling light mediator parameter space.

title: Twist-three quark TMDs from back-to-back dijet production in next-to-eikonal DIS
summary: We study back-to-back dijet production in deep inelastic scattering (DIS) at next-to-eikonal accuracy within the Color Glass Condensate framework, focusing on the quark-background contributions. We compute the quark-gluon and quark-antiquark production cross sections through next-to-leading power in the correlation limit for longitudinally and transversely polarized photons. In the quark-gluon channel, we derive both the kinematic corrections to the hard parts accompanying the twist-two quark distribution and the genuine twist-three contributions involving three-body quark-gluon-quark correlators. In the quark-antiquark channel, the interference of the eikonal amplitude with the double $t$-channel quark-exchange amplitudes probes three-body correlators with a different transverse arrangement of the fields. We express the results in terms of transverse momentum dependent (TMD) correlators and provide the corresponding hard coefficients. Our analysis extends the operator-level connection between the next-to-eikonal CGC framework and quark TMDs beyond leading power in the correlation limit.

AI.tldr: This paper computes back-to-back dijet production in DIS at next-to-eikonal accuracy within the Color Glass Condensate framework, focusing on quark-background contributions and deriving twist-two and twist-three quark-gluon correlators expressed in terms of TMDs.
AI.motivation: To extend the operator-level connection between the next-to-eikonal CGC framework and quark transverse momentum dependent (TMD) distributions beyond leading power in the correlation limit, particularly for quark-initiated processes in DIS.
AI.method: Computes quark-gluon and quark-antiquark dijet cross sections in DIS at next-to-eikonal accuracy using the Color Glass Condensate framework; identifies kinematic corrections to twist-two quark distributions and genuine twist-three contributions involving three-body quark-gluon-quark correlators; expresses results in terms of TMD correlators with corresponding hard coefficients.
AI.result: Derives explicit expressions for quark-gluon and quark-antiquark production cross sections including both kinematic (twist-two) and genuine (twist-three) next-to-leading-power contributions; establishes correspondence between CGC next-to-eikonal amplitudes and specific TMD correlators with distinct transverse field arrangements.
AI.conclusion: The analysis successfully generalizes the CGC–TMD correspondence to next-to-eikonal order for quark channels in DIS, providing a systematic operator-level identification of twist-three quark-gluon-quark correlators and their TMD interpretations.

title: dSIBP: a package for generating IBP seeds for QFT in de Sitter spacetime
summary: Recent studies show that in addition to the flat spacetime, Integration-by-parts (IBP) relations and differential equations can also provide a systematic approach to Feynman integrals in de Sitter spacetime. dSIBP is a Mathematica package for the automated construction of IBP systems and differential equations. For dS integral families with massive and massless propagators, it generates a complete set of IBP seeds, assembles linear systems for external reduction, and constructs differential equations for the reduced master integrals. The implementation combines equations of motion, remaining terms and parity constraints, and provides reliable checks. We describe the conventions and public interface through worked examples.

AI.tldr: dSIBP is a Mathematica package that automates the construction of IBP relations and differential equations for Feynman integrals in de Sitter spacetime, supporting both massive and massless propagators.
AI.motivation: To enable systematic evaluation of Feynman integrals in de Sitter spacetime—beyond flat spacetime—by automating IBP reduction and differential equation generation, which are essential for cosmological loop calculations.
AI.method: Implements integration-by-parts (IBP) identities tailored to de Sitter geometry; combines equations of motion, parity constraints, and remaining-term analysis to generate complete IBP seed systems, assemble external reduction linear systems, and construct differential equations for master integrals.
AI.result: A fully functional, publicly documented Mathematica package (dSIBP) capable of generating IBP seeds, performing external reductions, and deriving differential equations for dS Feynman integral families with mixed massive/massless propagators.
AI.conclusion: dSIBP provides a robust, automated framework for analytic computation of loop integrals in de Sitter spacetime, enhancing precision in inflationary and late-time cosmology predictions.

title: Investigating nucleon resonances in the $pp\to K^+K^+ΛΛ$ reaction
summary: In this work, we investigate the \(pp \to K^+ K^+ \Lambda \Lambda\) reaction using an effective Lagrangian approach and the isobar model. The calculation includes the exchange of \(\pi\), \(\eta\), \(\sigma\), \(\rho\), \(\omega\), and \(K\) mesons, as well as contributions from eight nucleon resonances: \(N(1535)\), \(N(1650)\), \(N(1710)\), \(N(1720)\), \(N(1895)\), \(N(1900)\), \(N(2060)\) and \(N(2120)\). The double-resonance excitation mechanism (\(NN \to N^* N^*\)) is found to dominate this reaction over the entire energy range considered. Among the exchanged mesons, the \(\eta\) exchange provides the largest contribution at lower energies, whereas the \(K\) exchange dominates at higher energies. Near the threshold, \(N(1535)\) and \(N(1650)\) play the most important roles, while at higher energies \(N(1710)\) and \(N(1720)\) become dominant. Due to isospin conservation, this reaction is predominantly coupled to nucleon resonances, providing a relatively clean channel for \(N^*\) spectroscopy. Our results indicate the unique potential of this reaction for studying nucleon resonances and provide a theoretical reference for future experimental studies at HIAF.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the pp → K⁺K⁺ΛΛ reaction using an effective Lagrangian and isobar model, identifying double-resonance (N*N*) dominance, energy-dependent meson exchange contributions (η at low energy, K at high energy), and key nucleon resonances (N(1535)/N(1650) near threshold; N(1710)/N(1720) at higher energies); it highlights the reaction’s utility for clean N* spectroscopy and guides future HIAF experiments.
AI.motivation: To identify a clean channel for nucleon resonance (N*) spectroscopy by exploiting isospin conservation in the pp → K⁺K⁺ΛΛ reaction, and to provide theoretical predictions for upcoming experiments at HIAF.
AI.method: Effective Lagrangian approach combined with the isobar model; includes t- and u-channel meson exchanges (π, η, σ, ρ, ω, K) and s-channel contributions from eight nucleon resonances; full amplitude constructed with gauge-invariant couplings and relativistic spinors.
AI.result: Double-resonance excitation (NN → N*N*) dominates across the energy range; η exchange dominates near threshold, K exchange at higher energies; N(1535) and N(1650) are most important near threshold, while N(1710) and N(1720) dominate at higher energies; reaction is strongly coupled to N* due to isospin constraints.
AI.conclusion: The pp → K⁺K⁺ΛΛ reaction offers a uniquely clean probe for nucleon resonance spectroscopy owing to isospin selection rules, and serves as a theoretically well-motivated benchmark for experimental investigation at HIAF.

title: Study of enhancing the signal-background separation for the Higgs boson production in association with a single top-quark in $pp$ collisions at the LHC
summary: In this paper, a multivariate analysis based approach for enhancing the extraction of the rare Standard Model (SM) process being studied - Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH) - from the prevailing background processes is presented. The analysis was performed using a Monte Carlo generated dataset simulating the outcomes of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). A deep fully connected neural network was developed for signal-background discrimination, incorporating a masking mechanism designed to suppress the contribution of input variables associated with objects that were not reconstructed in a given event. The performance of the masked architecture was evaluated on independent Monte Carlo samples. The results of the proposed methodology are compared with a conventional cut-based approach in terms of the statistical significance of the tH production channel. The developed framework was tested using a simulated dataset corresponding approximately to the combined statistical samples of LHC Runs 1, 2, and 3.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a masked deep neural network for improved tH signal extraction from background at the LHC, outperforming conventional cut-based methods in statistical significance.
AI.motivation: Enhancing detection sensitivity for the rare SM process of Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH), which is buried under large backgrounds.
AI.method: A deep fully connected neural network with a dynamic masking mechanism to suppress unreconstructed object features; trained and evaluated on Monte Carlo-simulated pp collision data at the LHC.
AI.result: The masked DNN achieves higher statistical significance for tH identification compared to a standard cut-based analysis on simulated datasets matching combined LHC Runs 1–3 statistics.
AI.conclusion: The masking-enabled deep learning framework provides a more powerful and robust approach for rare process extraction in high-energy physics analyses.

title: Electroweak corrections to the SM-like Higgs boson decays and the Higgs trilinear coupling in the real Higgs triplet model
summary: We study new physics effects on the decays of the standard model-like Higgs boson ($h$) and the Higgs trilinear coupling including the full one-loop corrections in the real Higgs triplet model (RHTM). We adopt the on-shell renormalization scheme, in which the scalar mixing angles are renormalized in a gauge-independent way using the pinch technique. We found that sizable one-loop effects can arise in the decay rates through the Higgs wave-function (external-leg) corrections, while the tree-level effects are rather small due to the constraint on the vacuum expectation value of the triplet field from the electroweak precision measurements. In addition, the $h\to\gamma\gamma$ decay rate and the $hhh$ coupling are sensitive to loop contributions. The RHTM may be distinguishable from other extended Higgs models by studying the correlations among the $h\to\tau\tau$, $h\to ZZ^{*}$, and $h\to\gamma\gamma$ decay modes, and such characteristic predictions can be tested at the High-Luminosity LHC or future Higgs factories.

AI.tldr: This paper computes full one-loop corrections to Higgs decays and trilinear coupling in the Real Higgs Triplet Model (RHTM), using an on-shell, gauge-independent renormalization scheme; it finds that loop effects—especially in h→γγ and hhh coupling—are significant and potentially distinguishable from other BSM models at HL-LHC or future Higgs factories.
AI.motivation: To probe new physics via precision Higgs observables—particularly decay rates and the trilinear Higgs coupling—in the RHTM, where tree-level deviations are suppressed by electroweak precision constraints on the triplet vev.
AI.method: Full one-loop computation of h decays (h→γγ, ττ, ZZ*) and hhh coupling in the RHTM, employing on-shell renormalization with pinch-technique-based, gauge-independent scalar mixing angle renormalization.
AI.result: Loop-induced corrections dominate over tree-level ones; h→γγ and hhh couplings show high sensitivity to triplet parameters; correlations among h→ττ, h→ZZ*, and h→γγ provide distinctive RHTM signatures.
AI.conclusion: The RHTM yields testable, loop-driven deviations in Higgs phenomenology, making it distinguishable from other extended Higgs sectors via multi-channel decay correlations at future colliders.

title: Multiplicity and transverse density as ordering variables of the $Λ/K^0_S$ ratio in oxygen-oxygen collisions at the LHC
summary: Baryon-to-meson enhancements are commonly compared across collision systems at equal multiplicity. Using published data only, we test whether the $p_T$ dependence of the CMS $\Lambda/K^0_S$ ratio in minimum-bias O-O collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.36$ TeV can be obtained from CMS multiplicity-differential p-Pb and Pb-Pb measurements weighted with the O-O multiplicity distribution. The prediction from p-Pb collisions of equal multiplicity is harder than the data, with a tilt of $+0.35\pm0.04$ in $\ln(\mathrm{prediction}/\mathrm{data})$ versus $\ln p_T$, whereas that from peripheral Pb-Pb collisions is consistent with the data. In a Glauber model calibrated on O-O data, O-O and peripheral Pb-Pb collisions of equal multiplicity have similar transverse densities $\rho=\langle(dN_{ch}/d\eta)/S_\perp\rangle$, about half of that in p-Pb. Matching the p-Pb reference in $\rho$ instead of multiplicity reduces the tilt by about 60%, to $+0.14\pm0.04$, with nucleons as sources; the tension is fully removed ($-0.02\pm0.04$) only when sub-nucleonic structure is included (three constituents per nucleon), so the conclusion depends on the modeled size of high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions. The published blast-wave velocities of p-Pb and Pb-Pb collisions, which differ at equal multiplicity, are close at equal $\rho$. Multiplicity alone thus does not determine the $\Lambda/K^0_S$ shape across systems; the data are consistent with a radial boost governed by the transverse density, as expected from hydrodynamics. The same pattern is found in EPOS4, which has a hydrodynamic core, but not in PYTHIA Angantyr. For Ne-Ne collisions, which have the transverse density of O-O at equal multiplicity, the minimum-bias ratio is predicted to agree with O-O within 3-5%, as EPOS4 also predicts.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether baryon-to-meson enhancement (Λ/K⁰ₛ ratio) in O-O collisions can be predicted from p-Pb and Pb-Pb data using multiplicity or transverse density (ρ) matching; it finds multiplicity alone is insufficient, while transverse density ρ — reflecting initial-state geometry — governs the pₜ shape, consistent with hydrodynamic radial flow; EPOS4 reproduces this, PYTHIA Angantyr does not.
AI.motivation: To test whether multiplicity-scaled reference systems (p-Pb, Pb-Pb) can predict Λ/K⁰ₛ(pₜ) in O-O collisions, and to identify the physically relevant scaling variable — multiplicity (N_ch) vs. transverse particle density (ρ = ⟨dN_ch/dη⟩/S_⊥) — for collective hadrochemistry.
AI.method: Empirical reweighting of published CMS p-Pb and Pb-Pb Λ/K⁰ₛ(pₜ) data using the O-O multiplicity distribution; comparison with O-O data; Glauber-model calculation of ρ for O-O, p-Pb, and Pb-Pb; systematic tilt analysis of ln(prediction/data) vs. ln pₜ; comparison of blast-wave velocities and EPOS4/PYTHIA Angantyr model predictions.
AI.result: p-Pb prediction overestimates high-pₜ Λ/K⁰ₛ relative to O-O (tilt +0.35±0.04); peripheral Pb-Pb matches O-O; matching on ρ instead of N_ch reduces tilt to +0.14±0.04 (nucleons); inclusion of sub-nucleonic structure (3 constituents/nucleon) eliminates tension (−0.02±0.04); blast-wave velocities align at equal ρ, not equal N_ch; EPOS4 reproduces pattern, PYTHIA Angantyr does not; Ne-Ne predicted to match O-O within 3–5%.
AI.conclusion: Transverse density ρ, not multiplicity N_ch, is the key scaling variable governing Λ/K⁰ₛ(pₜ) shape across collision systems, supporting a hydrodynamic origin of radial flow; the result is sensitive to the assumed sub-nucleonic structure in small systems, and validates ρ as a more fundamental proxy for initial energy density and collective dynamics.

title: DAMA/LIBRA dark matter signal: a global analysis
summary: The annual modulation reported by the DAMA/LIBRA collaboration remains in tension with the null results of other direct-detection experiments. We investigate the compatibility of DAMA/LIBRA with LZ, PICO-60 and CDMSlite within a generalized non-relativistic effective field theory (EFT) framework. In addition to the EFT operator expansion we investigate additional modifications to the standard WIMP picture, including inelastic scattering, variations in the NaI quenching factors, and a rescaling of the dark-matter velocity dispersion. We perform a Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis in this extended model space, using two alternative approaches to the likelihood function describing the DAMA/LIBRA data. Both approaches result in strong discrepancy between the data from DAMA/LIBRA and other experiments. We conclude that the extended model space considered here cannot accommodate the DAMA/LIBRA signal while remaining consistent with the non-observation of dark matter in other experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether DAMA/LIBRA's annual modulation signal can be reconciled with null results from LZ, PICO-60, and CDMSlite using an extended non-relativistic EFT framework—including inelastic scattering, quenching factor variations, and velocity dispersion rescaling—but finds strong incompatibility across all models.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing tension between DAMA/LIBRA's claimed dark matter signal and null results from other direct-detection experiments by exploring a broadened theoretical parameter space beyond standard WIMP assumptions.
AI.method: Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis within a generalized non-relativistic effective field theory framework, augmented with inelastic scattering, NaI quenching factor uncertainties, and rescaled dark-matter velocity dispersion; two alternative likelihood treatments for DAMA/LIBRA data are compared.
AI.result: Both likelihood approaches yield statistically significant tension—no region of the extended parameter space simultaneously fits DAMA/LIBRA and satisfies constraints from LZ, PICO-60, and CDMSlite.
AI.conclusion: The DAMA/LIBRA signal cannot be explained within this extended WIMP framework without violating constraints from other leading direct-detection experiments.

title: Next-to-leading order QCD corrections to fully charm tetraquark radiative decays
summary: We present the first complete next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD calculation of the fully charm tetraquark radiative decays $T_{4c}(0^{++},2^{++})\to\gamma J/\psi$ and $T_{4c}(1^{+-})\to\gamma\eta_c$ at leading order in the relative velocity. The NLO widths are $2.3$--$3.1$ times the leading-order (LO) widths for the long-distance matrix element (LDME) inputs considered here, with $m_c=1.5$ GeV and $\mu_R=2m_c$. In the scalar channel, the NLO corrections change the relative contributions of the two color-spin components and their interference. For the tensor channel, the longitudinal fraction $f_L$ of the daughter $J/\psi$ changes from $0.11$ at LO to $0.18$ at strictly expanded NLO, with sensitivity to higher-order corrections. These NLO results provide valuable theoretical input for searches for states predicted below their respective lowest dicharmonium thresholds and for probing the spin and short-distance structure of observed tetraquark candidates.

AI.tldr: First complete NLO QCD calculation of radiative decays of fully charm tetraquarks $T_{4c} \to \gamma J/\psi, \gamma \eta_c$, showing large NLO corrections (2.3–3.1× LO), altered color-spin interference in scalar channel, and increased longitudinal polarization fraction $f_L$ from 0.11 to 0.18 in tensor channel.
AI.motivation: To provide precise theoretical predictions for radiative decays of fully charm tetraquarks—key probes of their internal spin/color structure and essential for guiding experimental searches below dicharmonium thresholds.
AI.method: Complete next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD calculation within nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) framework, at leading order in relative velocity $v$, using long-distance matrix elements (LDMEs); includes real and virtual corrections; renormalization scale fixed at $\mu_R = 2m_c$, charm mass $m_c = 1.5$ GeV.
AI.result: NLO decay widths enhanced by factor 2.3–3.1 over LO; in scalar $0^{++},2^{++}$ channels, NLO modifies relative weights and interference of color-spin components; in tensor $2^{++} \to \gamma J/\psi$, longitudinal polarization fraction $f_L$ rises from 0.11 (LO) to 0.18 (strictly expanded NLO), indicating sensitivity to higher-order effects.
AI.conclusion: NLO QCD corrections are substantial and qualitatively significant—altering kinematic distributions and component interference—making them indispensable for interpreting current and future tetraquark observations, especially in radiative transitions probing short-distance dynamics.

title: Unitary $KK$ and $Kπ$ inputs for an amplitude analysis of the $D^+ \to K^-K^+π^+$ decay
comment: 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026). Submitted to Proceedings of Science
summary: Charge-Parity Violation (CPV) is expected in three-body charm decays. In particular, in the singly Cabibbo suppressed decay process $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$; in which an amplitude analysis is required to understand the dynamics of Final State Interactions (FSI) and the mechanism that can generate CPV. In this work, we show the prospects of analysing recent data from the Large Hadron Collider beauty (LHCb) experiment at CERN, with a precise theoretical model expected to reveal CPV mechanisms. Previous analyses of the $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$ decay were unable to satisfactorily describe the data using the Isobar Model. Currently, LHCb has a sample of charmed meson decays with around 100 million events for the $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$ decay, so a more robust phenomenological model is needed to describe such a large data set. The present model has allowed the inclusion of hadronic FSI and will, in prospect, introduce three-body effects, overcoming some limitations of the Isobar Model, and has all factors necessary to reveal the presence of CPV. To do so, it factorizes the weak vertex separated in leading topologies and relies on extensions of Resonant Chiral Perturbation Theory to describe FSI. As a proof-of-concept, a toy dataset of the S-wave of the most recent amplitude analysis of $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$, by the CLEO-c collaboration, was fitted with this model. From fits to model-independent parametrizations of scattering amplitudes, the parameters of the FSI amplitudes were fixed, and the production parameters of the weak vertex were then obtained from the fit to the toy dataset, yielding a good agreement between the data and our model.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an improved phenomenological model for analyzing CP violation (CPV) in the singly Cabibbo-suppressed decay D⁺ → K⁻K⁺π⁺, overcoming limitations of the Isobar Model by incorporating hadronic final-state interactions (FSI) via extended Resonant Chiral Perturbation Theory and factorizing the weak vertex into leading topologies.
AI.motivation: To detect and interpret CPV in D⁺ → K⁻K⁺π⁺ decays, where previous Isobar Model analyses failed to describe LHCb's high-statistics data (~100M events); robust modeling of FSI and three-body dynamics is essential to isolate CPV mechanisms.
AI.method: A factorized model separating weak decay amplitudes (by topologies) from strong FSI described via extensions of Resonant Chiral Perturbation Theory; validated on a CLEO-c S-wave toy dataset using model-independent scattering amplitude parametrizations to fix FSI parameters, then fitting production parameters.
AI.result: The model achieves good agreement with the CLEO-c S-wave toy data; successfully extracts production parameters from FSI-constrained fits, demonstrating feasibility for CPV sensitivity in full LHCb analyses.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a theoretically grounded, phenomenologically flexible tool capable of revealing CPV in D⁺ → K⁻K⁺π⁺, pending application to full LHCb data and inclusion of three-body effects beyond current S-wave validation.

title: Probing the Spatial Coherence of Chiral-Imbalance Fluctuations with Hyperon Spin Correlations
summary: Topological fluctuations in the quark-gluon plasma can generate local chiral imbalances whose spatial coherence remains difficult to access with conventional charge-separation measurements. We propose differential hyperon-pair spin correlations as a probe of both the strength and spatial organization of these fluctuations. Fluctuations of the axial chemical potential $\mu_5$ can induce pair correlations even when the mean helicity polarization vanishes. Using the AMPT model, we find that the magnitude of the hyperon spin correlation probes the magnitude and spatial coherence scale of $\mu_5$, while the ratio of short- and long-range correlations varies strongly with the spatial coherence scale, but only weakly with $\mu_{5}$ over the range of explored parameters. These observables provide an experimentally testable strategy for constraining the spatial structure of chiral-imbalance fluctuations.

AI.tldr: Proposes differential hyperon-pair spin correlations as a novel probe of spatial structure and magnitude of chiral-imbalance fluctuations (via axial chemical potential μ₅) in the quark-gluon plasma, validated with AMPT simulations.
AI.motivation: Conventional charge-separation measurements cannot access the spatial coherence of topological fluctuations-induced local chiral imbalances in the quark-gluon plasma.
AI.method: Theoretical proposal combined with numerical simulation using the AMPT (A Multi-Phase Transport) model to compute differential spin correlations of hyperon pairs as a function of μ₅ magnitude and spatial coherence scale.
AI.result: Hyperon spin correlation magnitude encodes both |μ₅| and its spatial coherence length; the ratio of short- to long-range correlations is highly sensitive to coherence length but weakly dependent on |μ₅| within the explored parameter range.
AI.conclusion: Differential hyperon-pair spin correlations constitute an experimentally viable, quantitative probe for constraining the spatial structure of chiral-imbalance fluctuations in heavy-ion collisions.

title: Renormalization and Factorization Scale-Invariant Predictions for the $e^+e^-\to J/ψ+η_c$ process at $B$ factories
summary: We perform a NNLO perturbative QCD analysis for exclusive double charmonium production $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ within the NRQCD factorization formalism using the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC). It is well known that this charmonium process suffers poor pQCD convergence, as well as large renormalization scale uncertainty. The PMC is used to remove conventional renormalization scale uncertainty. Based on two fundamental physical processes of charmonium, $J/\psi\rightarrow e^+e^-$ and $\eta_c\rightarrow\gamma\gamma$, and using the NNLO perturbative results together with experimental measurements, we extract the factorization-scale-dependent long-distance matrix elements for $J/\psi$ and $\eta_c$. Combining these two matrix elements with the factorization-scale-dependent short-distance coefficient, we obtain predictions that are independent of the factorization scale for the $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ process. Our predictions agree with the measurement from the BaBar collaborations within errors. Remarkably, we provide a new way to eliminate conventional renormalization and factorization scale ambiguities for the $e^+e^-\to J/\psi+\eta_c$ process. We further demonstrate that the slow convergence of the pQCD series is an intrinsic property of this double-charmonium process.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) to perform a NNLO pQCD analysis of e+e−→J/ψ+ηc within NRQCD factorization, eliminating renormalization and factorization scale ambiguities and achieving agreement with BaBar data.
AI.motivation: To resolve poor pQCD convergence and large renormalization scale uncertainty plaguing exclusive double charmonium production e+e−→J/ψ+ηc.
AI.method: NNLO perturbative QCD analysis within NRQCD factorization using PMC; extraction of factorization-scale-dependent LDMEs from J/ψ→e+e− and ηc→γγ, combined with scale-dependent short-distance coefficients to obtain scale-invariant cross section predictions.
AI.result: Scale-independent theoretical predictions for e+e−→J/ψ+ηc that agree with BaBar measurements; demonstration that slow pQCD convergence is intrinsic to the process.
AI.conclusion: PMC successfully eliminates conventional renormalization and factorization scale ambiguities in double charmonium production; the residual slow convergence reflects an intrinsic feature of the process, not a scheme artifact.

title: Chiral anomalies in two dimensions
summary: Chiral anomalies offer a fundamental probe of the quantum structure of gauge theories and their underlying symmetries. In this paper, we introduce a framework to characterize the chiral anomaly in two dimensions directly at the diagrammatic level. To this end, we establish a consistent prescription for handling $\gamma^5$ in dimensional regularization at $d=2$. On this basis, we derive an expression for the fully generic chiral anomaly directly from the contributions of the bubble and triangle diagrams, either in the massless or massive case. Then, we show that the different forms of the anomaly can arise from appropriate choices of parameters directly at the level of this master expression. Overall, $d=2$ is shown to provide an excellent environment to investigate chiral anomalies at the amplitude level: Ward identities are demonstrated rigorously and to arbitrary order in the mass expansion without further approximation, resulting in an unprecedented degree of control on the anomaly.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a diagrammatic framework for chiral anomalies in two dimensions using a consistent treatment of γ⁵ in dimensional regularization at d=2, deriving a master expression from bubble and triangle diagrams—applicable to both massless and massive cases—and rigorously verifying Ward identities to all orders in the mass expansion.
AI.motivation: To provide a fundamental, diagrammatic-level characterization of chiral anomalies in two-dimensional gauge theories, leveraging the simplicity and control offered by d=2 to rigorously examine quantum symmetry breaking without approximations.
AI.method: Establishes a consistent prescription for γ⁵ in dimensional regularization at d=2; computes chiral anomaly contributions from bubble and triangle Feynman diagrams; derives a generic master expression encompassing both massless and massive cases; analyzes parameter dependence to recover distinct anomaly forms; verifies Ward identities order-by-order in the fermion mass expansion.
AI.result: A universal, diagrammatically derived master expression for the 2D chiral anomaly; rigorous, all-orders validation of Ward identities in the mass expansion; demonstration that standard anomaly forms (e.g., consistent vs. covariant) emerge as special parameter choices within the same framework.
AI.conclusion: Two dimensions provides an optimal setting for amplitude-level analysis of chiral anomalies: the proposed framework delivers unprecedented analytical control, unifies seemingly distinct anomaly manifestations, and confirms the robustness of quantum symmetry constraints beyond perturbative truncation.

title: Constraining tau-sterile neutrino mixing with high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
summary:
Whether a sterile neutrino mixes with the three active ones remains an open question. Its mixing with the tau neutrino, $|U_{	au 4}|^2$, is the least constrained, since terrestrial experiments probe it only indirectly and over limited ranges of sterile-neutrino mass. We show that TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos probe it differently. Their sources make almost no $
u_	au$, but oscillations over cosmological distances turn about one third of them into $
u_	au$ before they reach Earth. Mixing with a sterile neutrino would make these $
u_	au$ scarcer, lowering the $
u_	au$ fraction that neutrino telescopes measure, whatever the sterile-neutrino mass. In contrast, sterile mixing with $
u_e$ or $
