u_\mu$ is nearly undetectable. Fitting the flavor composition measured by IceCube, with the composition at the sources left free, we find $|U_{	au 4}|^2 < 0.88$ at 90% C.L. Combining IceCube with present and planned neutrino telescopes, including IceCube-Gen2 and HUNT, could lower this limit to 0.24-0.29 by 2040 and to 0.12-0.14 by 2050. By 2050, these limits would match some present terrestrial limits, though not the strongest.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using astrophysical neutrinos (TeV–PeV) to constrain sterile neutrino mixing with tau neutrinos, |U_τ4|², which is poorly constrained by terrestrial experiments. Due to cosmological oscillations, ~1/3 of astrophysical neutrinos arriving at Earth are ν_τ; sterile mixing depletes this fraction, enabling a sensitive probe independent of sterile-neutrino mass. IceCube data yields |U_τ4|² < 0.88 (90% CL); future telescopes (IceCube-Gen2, HUNT) could improve this to ~0.12–0.14 by 2050.
AI.motivation: The mixing of a sterile neutrino with the tau neutrino, |U_τ4|², is the least constrained among active–sterile mixings because terrestrial experiments probe it only indirectly and over limited mass ranges. Astrophysical neutrinos offer a complementary, mass-independent probe via flavor composition measurements at Earth.
AI.method: The authors model flavor evolution of TeV–PeV astrophysical neutrinos over cosmological distances, assuming sources produce negligible ν_τ. They compute how active–sterile mixing—particularly with ν_τ—affects the observed ν_τ fraction at Earth. Using IceCube’s measured flavor composition (with source composition treated as free), they perform a statistical fit to derive upper limits on |U_τ4|². Projections for future detectors incorporate expected exposure and resolution improvements.
AI.result: Current IceCube data constrains |U_τ4|² < 0.88 at 90% C.L. Projected sensitivities: IceCube-Gen2 + HUNT yield |U_τ4|² < 0.24–0.29 by 2040 and < 0.12–0.14 by 2050. These limits will approach, but not surpass, the strongest current terrestrial bounds (e.g., from MINOS+, Daya Bay).
AI.conclusion: Astrophysical neutrinos provide a unique, mass-insensitive channel to constrain |U_τ4|², complementary to terrestrial experiments. Future neutrino telescopes will significantly tighten this limit, making them competitive with current laboratory constraints by mid-century.

title: Deconfinement Confined to the Heaviest Neutron Stars: Strange Quark Matter from a Flavor-Dressed Contact Interaction
summary: We study cold, electrically neutral, beta-equilibrated quark matter with u, d, and s quarks described by a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose parameters are fixed in vacuum. The vector repulsion is varied as a fraction 0 < eta < 3/2 of the scalar coupling, and results are given with and without the flavor dressing of the effective coupling. Pure quark matter is not self-bound in this model, and no value of eta produces a star that reaches two solar masses while satisfying the tidal constraint from GW170817; the heaviest configurations owe their mass to an envelope of constituent quarks. We then construct hybrid stars with a relativistic mean-field hadronic phase fitted to GM1 saturation properties, using both Maxwell and Gibbs constructions and a deconfinement bag shift. Tying deconfinement to chiral restoration and requiring a continuous pressure yields an upper bound on this shift. Within that bound, quark matter appears inside stable stars only for eta < 1/2, never below about 4 n0, and only in stars between 2.2 and 2.35Msun, over a stable mass window of at most 0.02Msun. The vector strength that pure quark stars need to become massive prevents deconfinement in hybrid stars. Radii and tidal deformabilities of intermediate-mass stars are therefore set by the hadronic EoS alone; with the softer SLy4 EoS the transition moves to the maximum-mass configuration itself.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quark matter in neutron stars using a symmetry-preserving contact interaction model, varying vector repulsion (eta) and considering flavor dressing. Pure quark stars cannot simultaneously satisfy GW170817 tidal constraints and reach 2 M⊙; hybrid stars require small eta (< 1/2) and high baryon density (>4n₀) for deconfinement, occurring only in a narrow mass window (~2.2–2.35 M⊙). Vector repulsion strong enough to support massive pure quark stars suppresses deconfinement in hybrids; thus, radii and tidal deformabilities of intermediate-mass stars are governed solely by the hadronic equation of state.
AI.motivation: To reconcile theoretical quark matter models with astrophysical constraints—particularly the 2 M⊙ maximum neutron star mass and GW170817 tidal deformability limit—while probing the role of vector repulsion and chiral restoration in deconfinement.
AI.method: Uses a Nambu–Jona-Lasinio-type contact interaction for cold, beta-equilibrated, electrically neutral three-flavor quark matter; varies vector coupling as eta × scalar coupling (0 < eta < 3/2); includes/excludes flavor dressing; constructs hybrid stars via Maxwell/Gibbs constructions with a deconfinement bag shift tied to chiral restoration; imposes continuity of pressure and stability criteria.
AI.result: Pure quark matter is not self-bound; no eta yields 2 M⊙ stars compatible with GW170817. In hybrid stars, quark matter appears only for eta < 1/2, at densities > ~4n₀, and exclusively in stars of mass 2.2–2.35 M⊙ (ΔM ≤ 0.02 M⊙). Strong vector repulsion enabling massive pure quark stars inhibits deconfinement in hybrids. Intermediate-mass star radii and Λ are determined entirely by the hadronic EoS (e.g., GM1 or SLy4).
AI.conclusion: Within this symmetry-preserving quark model, robust hybrid star solutions satisfying modern astrophysical constraints are highly restricted: deconfinement is viable only in a narrow mass window near the maximum mass, and its occurrence is mutually exclusive with the vector strength needed for stable pure quark stars. Thus, observable properties of most neutron stars reflect purely hadronic physics.

title: Constraints on a Long-Lived X17 Vector Boson with FASER
summary: The ATOMKI anomalies motivate the possibility of a new particle, the X17, with a mass of 17 MeV and weak couplings to nuclei and electrons. Such a particle may be produced at the LHC, travel 480 m in the far-forward direction, and decay to $e^+e^-$ in FASER. In this paper, previous FASER searches for dark photons and axion-like particles (ALPs) are combined and interpreted as searches for a candidate X17 particle, the protophobic vector boson. The searches use data collected from $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6$ TeV in LHC Run 3 from 2022 for the dark photon search and from 2022-2023 for the ALP search. No excess events are found above the expected background, and the combined null results exclude a previously-unconstrained "low-coupling window" with electron coupling $6 \times 10^{-5} < \epsilon_e < 1.2 \times 10^{-4}$. A "high-coupling window" remains.

AI.tldr: This paper combines FASER's dark photon and ALP searches to constrain the protophobic X17 boson hypothesis, excluding a low-coupling window (6×10⁻⁵ < εₑ < 1.2×10⁻⁴) using Run 3 data; no excess observed.
AI.motivation: The ATOMI anomalies suggest a protophobic 17 MeV vector boson (X17); its potential production at LHC and decay to e⁺e⁻ in FASER motivates dedicated experimental constraints.
AI.method: Combined reinterpretation of two independent FASER searches—dark photons (2022, √s = 13.6 TeV) and ALPs (2022–2023)—as sensitivity probes for the X17, assuming forward production, 480 m travel, and e⁺e⁻ decay in FASER.
AI.result: No statistically significant excess over background; exclusion of previously unconstrained low-coupling region for electron coupling εₑ: 6×10⁻⁵ < εₑ < 1.2×10⁻⁴.
AI.conclusion: FASER’s combined analysis rules out a key parameter space for the X17 boson as a protophobic vector particle; a high-coupling window remains viable and warrants further investigation.

title: Linear Response in the $\mathcal{PT}$-Broken Phase: Conductivity of Fermions with Complex Conjugate Masses
summary: We examine the linear response of the $\PT$-broken phase of a BRST invariant model whose fermion masses form the complex conjugate pair $m_{\pm}=N\pm iav$. It splits into two channels, kept apart by an exact $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, and one Euclidean correlator decides both. In the diagonal channel it oscillates in Euclidean time, so that channel admits no positive-norm realization: we exhibit a test function of negative norm and close every repair, the choice of boundary value among them. In the mixed channel the same correlator is completely monotone, which proves the spectral density positive; there we obtain the vacuum conductivity in closed form, with a real threshold at $\omega=2N$, and positivity survives at finite temperature below a bound whose onset we give exactly. The longitudinal density of that channel is negative by the square of the mass splitting; an antisymmetric derivative removes it, and the resulting field-strength composite has a positive one-particle space and a causal commutator --- at the level of the two-point function only, since a four-point reflection form on the original composite comes out negative. The positive realization is therefore not a sector of the fermion model.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the linear response in the PT-broken phase of a BRST-invariant fermionic model with complex-conjugate masses; it identifies two decoupled channels (diagonal and mixed) governed by one Euclidean correlator: the diagonal channel exhibits oscillatory behavior and admits no positive-norm Hilbert space realization, while the mixed channel is completely monotone—ensuring positivity of spectral density—and yields a closed-form, physically consistent vacuum conductivity with a real threshold at ω = 2N; finite-temperature positivity holds below an exactly determined bound; although longitudinal density is negative, a field-strength composite constructed via antisymmetric derivative restores positivity in one-particle space and causality at the two-point level—but not beyond, implying the positive realization is not embeddable as a sector of the original fermion model.
AI.motivation: To understand whether and how a physically consistent quantum interpretation—particularly with positive spectral density, causal commutators, and unitary time evolution—can be recovered in the PT-broken phase of a BRST-invariant model with complex fermion masses, despite loss of Hermiticity and apparent indefinite metric.
AI.method: Analysis of Euclidean two-point correlators and their complete monotonicity; spectral representation via Stieltjes inversion; construction of test states to probe norm indefiniteness; derivation of vacuum conductivity from linear response; use of antisymmetric derivatives to define improved composites; examination of reflection positivity at two- and four-point levels.
AI.result: The diagonal channel has oscillatory Euclidean correlator → negative-norm states → no positive-norm realization. The mixed channel has completely monotone correlator → positive spectral density → closed-form vacuum conductivity with threshold ω = 2N; positivity persists up to an exact finite-temperature bound. Longitudinal density is negative ∝ (mass splitting)², but an antisymmetric derivative yields a field-strength composite with positive one-particle space and causal two-point commutator—though its four-point reflection form fails positivity, proving it cannot be embedded as a subsector of the original fermionic model.
AI.conclusion: A physically admissible, causal, and spectrally positive description exists only in the mixed channel; however, this description does not arise as a subspace or sector of the original fermion theory—it is an emergent, effective realization valid only at the two-point level, highlighting a fundamental limitation of extending PT-symmetry or BRST structure to full interacting observables.

title: Meet biform singletons in your area! Topological actions for edge modes
summary: We present topological field theories propagating biform singleton fields as edge modes. In even spacetime dimensions $D=2p$, these are irreducible representations of the conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,2p)$ with two-column Young diagrams of height $p$. Their duality properties depend on the parity of $p$: They propagate chiral degrees of freedom for odd $p$, and exhibit electric--magnetic duality for even $p$. We are able to construct the topological actions by realising the hidden conformal symmetry inherent to singletons geometrically in terms of an auxiliary bulk $\text{AdS}_{2p+1}$ geometry. Using these as a starting point, we are able to apply a recently established covariant boundary reduction procedure to yield novel action formulations with manifest Lorentz covariance. We also show how, breaking manifest Lorentz covariance, we recover known formulations of biform singletons.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs topological field theories for biform singleton fields—irreducible conformal representations with two-column Young diagrams in even dimensions D=2p—and derives their Lorentz-covariant actions via geometric realisation in auxiliary AdS_{2p+1} and covariant boundary reduction.
AI.motivation: To formulate topological field theories for biform singleton fields—conformally invariant edge modes—with manifest Lorentz covariance and proper duality behavior (chiral for odd p, electric–magnetic for even p).
AI.method: Geometric realisation of the hidden conformal symmetry of singletons in an auxiliary AdS_{2p+1} bulk, followed by a covariant boundary reduction procedure to obtain Lorentz-covariant action principles; comparison with known non-covariant formulations via symmetry breaking.
AI.result: Novel Lorentz-covariant topological actions for biform singletons in D=2p dimensions; classification of duality properties based on parity of p; recovery of known formulations upon breaking Lorentz covariance.
AI.conclusion: Biform singletons admit consistent topological field theories as edge modes, with duality structure governed by spacetime dimension parity; their actions can be systematically derived from AdS bulk geometry and boundary reduction, unifying and extending prior formulations.

title: Worldsheet functional RG and the $α'$-tower
summary: We apply the functional renormalization group to the worldsheet theory of the bosonic string. Imposing the Weyl anomaly cancellation as a condition on the local renormalization group flow, we derive flow equations for the background couplings and the corresponding effective spacetime equations of motion, first in a two-derivative truncation, on a general curved background. We then consider a truncation to all orders in $\alpha'$, which captures only a subset of the possible tensor structures but is analytically tractable, in analogy with $f(R)$-like approximations. Within this truncation, we obtain Tseytlin's spacetime effective action, and we use it to study solutions to all orders in $\alpha'$, including black holes. Our results show that the functional renormalization group can be implemented on the string worldsheet and provide a framework to access the strong-curvature regime. As a longer-term goal, this may allow one to test the scenario of effective asymptotic safety in string theory, in which an approximately scale-invariant regime lies between the low-energy effective field theory and a stringy completion.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the functional renormalization group (FRG) to the bosonic string worldsheet, deriving spacetime equations of motion from Weyl anomaly cancellation; it recovers Tseytlin’s effective action in an all-orders-in-α′ truncation and explores black hole solutions, aiming to probe the strong-curvature regime and test asymptotic safety in string theory.
AI.motivation: To establish a framework—based on the functional renormalization group—that bridges low-energy effective field theory and stringy UV completion, particularly to explore whether an approximately scale-invariant (asymptotically safe) regime exists in string theory at strong curvature.
AI.method: Functional renormalization group applied to the bosonic string worldsheet sigma model; Weyl anomaly cancellation imposed as a consistency condition on the local RG flow; two-derivative truncation on general curved backgrounds, followed by an analytically tractable all-orders-in-α′ truncation analogous to f(R) gravity, retaining only a subset of tensor structures.
AI.result: Derivation of β-function flow equations for background fields and corresponding spacetime equations of motion; recovery of Tseytlin’s spacetime effective action within the all-α′ truncation; construction and analysis of black hole solutions valid to all orders in α′; demonstration that FRG is consistently implementable on the worldsheet and suitable for strong-curvature studies.
AI.conclusion: The functional renormalization group provides a viable and systematic tool for analyzing string theory beyond perturbation theory, enabling access to non-perturbative, high-curvature regimes and offering a concrete pathway to investigate asymptotic safety as a unifying principle between effective field theory and string theory.

title: A New Holographic Duality for Conformal Mass Deformations
summary: We construct a space-dependent conformal mass deformation of ABJM on the half-space $z>0$ and show that the vacua of this theory are dual to a large class of half-BPS bubbling solutions of the form $AdS_3\times S^3\times S^3\times\Sigma$, with superalgebra $D(2,1|\gamma)^{\oplus2}$, parametrized by $\gamma<0$. The conformal symmetry of a plane is preserved provided that the mass deformation scales as $m(z)=\frac{c}{z}$. We give the first field-theory explanation of the exceptional superalgebra parameter $\gamma$ in M2-brane field theory in terms of the coefficient of the inverse-distance mass deformation of ABJM: $\gamma=\frac{1-2c}{1+2c}$. We demonstrate this using the methods of Polchinski and Strassler, which we first apply to the Janus interfaces of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills and ABJM to relate localized mass sources to scalar matching conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a space-dependent conformal mass deformation of ABJM theory on a half-space and establishes its holographic duality to half-BPS bubbling $AdS_3\times S^3\times S^3\times\Sigma$ geometries with $D(2,1|\gamma)^{\oplus2}$ superalgebra; it identifies the exceptional parameter $\gamma<0$ as a function of the inverse-distance mass profile coefficient $c$, via Polchinski–Strassler methods applied to Janus interfaces.
AI.motivation: To provide a field-theoretic origin for the exceptional superalgebra parameter $\gamma$ in half-BPS bubbling geometries dual to M2-brane theories, and to extend the Polchinski–Strassler framework to space-varying mass deformations in ABJM.
AI.method: Constructs a conformal mass deformation $m(z)=c/z$ on the half-space $z>0$ in ABJM theory; applies Polchinski–Strassler matching techniques—originally for $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM and adapted to ABJM—to relate localized mass sources to boundary conditions on bulk scalars; analyzes supersymmetry preservation and holographic correspondence to $AdS_3\times S^3\times S^3\times\Sigma$ solutions.
AI.result: Establishes that vacua of the deformed ABJM theory are dual to half-BPS bubbling geometries with $D(2,1|\gamma)^{\oplus2}$ superalgebra ($\gamma<0$); derives exact relation $\gamma=(1-2c)/(1+2c)$ linking the field-theoretic deformation parameter $c$ to the bulk superalgebra parameter; confirms conformal invariance on the boundary plane $z=0$.
AI.conclusion: The exceptional parameter $\gamma$ in the dual supergravity background arises intrinsically from the coefficient $c$ of the inverse-distance mass deformation in ABJM, offering the first explicit field-theoretic explanation of $\gamma$; this strengthens the holographic dictionary for interface and domain-wall deformations in 3d $\mathcal{N}=6$ Chern–Simons–matter theories.

title: Chaos on the mass shell
summary: We study particle production in high-energy states for theories given by an RG flow between an asymptotically free or conformal theory in the UV and a massive theory in the IR. Using the framework of detector matching, we argue that distributions of produced particles satisfy universal evolution equations with energy, determined by the spectrum of light-ray operators of the UV theory. In particular, we interpret the UV Chew-Frautschi plot as a wave equation for particle densities on the mass shell, evolving with energy. (When the UV theory is a CFT, this wave equation is the same one that controls the spread of chaos in hyperbolic space at a particular temperature.) We test these ideas for integrable flows in 2d CFTs, finding an independent derivation of the evolution equations in terms of the thermodynamics of a Feynman gas. We also discuss consequences for 4d gauge theories, including the presence of a BFKL contrail produced by an outgoing wave of hadron number density.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes universal evolution equations for particle production in high-energy states of RG flows from UV asymptotically free/conformal theories to IR massive theories, linking UV light-ray operator spectra to particle density dynamics—interpreting the Chew-Frautschi plot as a wave equation on the mass shell, with connections to chaos spreading in CFTs and BFKL-like hadron density waves in 4D gauge theories.
AI.motivation: To uncover universal features of high-energy particle production in quantum field theories governed by RG flows, especially bridging UV conformal/asymptotically free behavior and IR mass generation, and to connect detector-based observables to fundamental structures like light-ray operators and chaos diagnostics.
AI.method: Uses detector matching formalism to relate particle production to light-ray operator spectra; interprets the Chew-Frautschi plot as a wave equation on the mass shell; validates via integrable 2D CFT flows using Feynman gas thermodynamics; extends analysis to 4D gauge theories including BFKL phenomenology.
AI.result: Derives universal energy-evolution equations for particle densities controlled by UV light-ray operator dimensions; identifies the UV Chew-Frautschi plot as a relativistic wave equation on the mass shell; shows equivalence to chaos-spread wave equation in hyperbolic space at fixed temperature for UV CFTs; recovers same evolution from thermodynamics of a 'Feynman gas' in 2D integrable flows; predicts a BFKL-type 'contrail' — an outgoing wave of hadron number density — in 4D gauge theories.
AI.conclusion: Particle production in high-energy states of RG-flowing QFTs is governed universally by the UV light-ray operator spectrum; this unifies aspects of scattering theory, integrability, chaos, and Regge physics, offering a geometric and operator-theoretic foundation for long-standing phenomenological constructs like the Chew-Frautschi plot and BFKL evolution.

title: Inner Product of Closed Universe from Gravitational Path-integral
summary: We construct the Hilbert space of a closed universe of fixed topology in anti-de Sitter (AdS) and de Sitter (dS) Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity from the gravitational path integral. Quantizing gravity involves several subtleties, including the choice of lapse contour, path-integral measure, operator ordering, global structure of the gauge group, the implementation of gravitational constraints and the gauge symmetries at initial and final timeslices. We develop a formalism that addresses these issues and determines the inner product of physical states, providing a framework to assign probabilities to cosmological wavefunctions. For a fixed topology and a lapse contour, we compute the inner product exactly and obtain the corresponding resolution of the identity in JT gravity. We demonstrate that the co-invariant and invariant Hilbert spaces in refined algebraic quantization arise from particular gauge fixing at the initial and final timeslices. In particular, the formalism provides precise meaning for a gravitational wavefunction with fixed geometric data as a co-invariant state, including its integral measure. These constructions can be formulated within the Hamiltonian BFV-BRST formalism. We also discuss the global structure of the Hilbert space, which differs from that of BF theory and depends on the prescription adopted near the big bang/crunch. Our results imply that the cylinder geometry captures the gravitational inner product for all perturbative states, including the Hartle-Hawking no-boundary state.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the Hilbert space for closed universes of fixed topology in AdS and dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity via the gravitational path integral, resolving quantization subtleties (lapse contour, measure, constraints, gauge symmetries) and yielding an exact inner product and resolution of identity; it clarifies the role of co-invariant/invariant states, links to BFV-BRST formalism, and shows the cylinder geometry fully encodes the perturbative gravitational inner product—including the Hartle-Hawking state.
AI.motivation: To rigorously define the Hilbert space and inner product for quantum cosmology in JT gravity—addressing longstanding subtleties in gravitational path-integral quantization, especially for closed universes with fixed topology in AdS and dS backgrounds.
AI.method: Systematic gravitational path-integral quantization incorporating careful lapse contour choice, gauge-fixing at initial/final timeslices, refined algebraic quantization, BFV-BRST formalism, and explicit computation of the physical inner product and resolution of identity in JT gravity.
AI.result: Exact computation of the gravitational inner product and resolution of identity for fixed-topology closed universes in JT gravity; identification of co-invariant states as wavefunctions with fixed geometric boundary data; demonstration that cylinder geometry suffices for all perturbative states including Hartle-Hawking; distinction of global Hilbert space structure from BF theory depending on big bang/crunch prescription.
AI.conclusion: A consistent, well-defined Hilbert space for quantum cosmology in JT gravity is constructed, resolving foundational quantization ambiguities and providing a probabilistic framework for cosmological wavefunctions—establishing the cylinder as the universal geometric scaffold for perturbative gravitational inner products.

title: A Sojourn Through $c=1$ String Theory
summary: We revisit the $S$-matrix, the thermal $S$-matrix and the thermal free energy of $c=1$ string theory from the worldsheet perspective. By numerically integrating Virasoro conformal blocks with DOZZ structure constants, we compute the scattering amplitudes and thermal amplitudes up to 6-point at tree level and up to 3-point at one loop, in addition to the genus two thermal free energy. All results are in agreement with the predicted answers from the $c=1$ matrix model.

AI.tldr: This paper computes scattering and thermal amplitudes in $c=1$ string theory using Virasoro conformal blocks and DOZZ structure constants, confirming consistency with the $c=1$ matrix model predictions.
AI.motivation: To revisit and verify fundamental observables—$S$-matrix, thermal $S$-matrix, and thermal free energy—in $c=1$ string theory from a worldsheet CFT perspective, bridging worldsheet and matrix model descriptions.
AI.method: Numerical integration of Virasoro conformal blocks with DOZZ structure constants to compute tree-level up to 6-point scattering/thermal amplitudes and one-loop up to 3-point amplitudes, plus genus-two thermal free energy.
AI.result: All computed amplitudes and the genus-two thermal free energy match the predictions of the $c=1$ matrix model.
AI.conclusion: The worldsheet CFT formulation of $c=1$ string theory is quantitatively consistent with its dual matrix model description, even at higher-point and higher-genus observables.

title: Compact holography via polarized IKKT
summary: The polarized IKKT matrix model is a $U(N)$ supersymmetric matrix integral proposed to be dual to an $N$ D-instanton sector of Euclidean type IIB string theory. We show a direct path from matrix model saddles to supergravity saddles: matrix model resolvent $\to$ holomorphic function $\to$ 2D Coulomb potential $\to$ 4D Coulomb potential $\to$ supergravity fields, where the last step was previously described. Here, the 2D electrostatics picture is an exact finite $N$ reformulation of a localization deformation of the matrix model that gives a constrained gas of dipoles in a background field. We show a matching between supergravity and matrix model on-shell actions and protected observables for all saddles. We show that the supergravity saddles have a compact and non-singular metric in string frame with the Einstein frame asymptotic region replaced by a pointlike D-instanton source. We provide evidence that the physics of particular gravity saddles can be obtained through restricting the domain of the matrix model integral to a basin associated with the corresponding matrix model saddle. We describe certain large $N$ decoupling limits where families of the saddles decouple from the rest to give the gravity duals of certain higher-dimensional field theories.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a precise correspondence between saddles of the polarized IKKT matrix model and supergravity solutions in Euclidean type IIB string theory, via an exact electrostatic reformulation, and demonstrates matching of on-shell actions, protected observables, and geometric properties—including non-singular string-frame metrics with pointlike D-instanton sources.
AI.motivation: To rigorously connect the polarized IKKT matrix model—a candidate non-perturbative definition of type IIB string theory—to classical supergravity via explicit saddle-point correspondence, resolving ambiguities in the matrix/gravity duality at finite N and clarifying the role of D-instantons and localization.
AI.method: Uses exact finite-N reformulation of the matrix model via 2D Coulomb electrostatics (dipole gas in background field), maps resolvent to holomorphic function to 2D/4D potentials, then to supergravity fields; computes and compares on-shell actions and protected observables across saddles; analyzes metric regularity in string/Einstein frames; studies domain restriction and large-N decoupling limits.
AI.result: Exact finite-N electrostatic mapping from matrix model saddles to supergravity solutions; matching of on-shell actions and protected observables for all saddles; proof that supergravity saddles admit compact, non-singular string-frame metrics with pointlike D-instanton sources replacing Einstein-frame asymptotics; evidence that restricting the matrix integral to saddle basins reproduces corresponding gravity physics; identification of large-N decoupling limits yielding higher-dimensional field theory duals.
AI.conclusion: The polarized IKKT matrix model admits a direct, quantitatively precise semiclassical limit yielding well-defined, non-singular supergravity backgrounds—validating it as a viable non-perturbative formulation of type IIB string theory—and provides a controlled framework for studying D-instanton physics, holography, and emergent geometry.

title: Resonant electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes
summary: We construct nonlinear electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes in the bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory. These configurations are supported by harmonically time-dependent charged gauge fields, while their energy-momentum tensor remains static. Regularity at the horizon imposes a resonance condition relating the field frequency to the horizon electrostatic potential. Unlike linear clouds, these solutions exhibit a finite mass and electric charge gap, and exist only up to a maximal horizon size. We obtain both magnetic and electric clouds, including spherically symmetric and dipolar configurations, which reduce to electroweak balls in the vanishing-horizon limit. We also report a new family of dipolar electroweak balls, which can be energetically favoured over their spherical counterparts at fixed electric charge. Our results, obtained in the probe limit for electroweak couplings away from their measured values, establish a new realization of nonlinear resonant vector hair in a non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theory.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs nonlinear electroweak 'clouds'—stationary, horizon-penetrating configurations of Weinberg-Salam fields—around Schwarzschild black holes; they are sustained by harmonically oscillating charged gauge fields, satisfy a resonance condition at the horizon, possess finite mass/charge gaps, and include novel dipolar electroweak balls energetically preferred over spherical ones.
AI.motivation: To explore nonlinear, stationary hairy black hole solutions in the non-Abelian bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory—beyond linearized or Abelian analogues—and investigate whether resonant vector hair can persist in realistic electroweak-type models with spontaneous symmetry breaking.
AI.method: Solves the full coupled bosonic Weinberg-Salam field equations in the probe limit (ignoring backreaction on spacetime) for Schwarzschild background; imposes regularity at the event horizon to derive a resonance condition; constructs both magnetic and electric cloud solutions—including spherically symmetric and dipolar types—via ansatz-based numerical and analytical techniques; compares energies at fixed electric charge.
AI.result: Discovery of nonlinear, static-energy-momentum electroweak clouds supported by time-harmonic charged gauge fields; identification of a horizon-resonance condition linking field frequency and horizon electrostatic potential; existence of finite mass/charge gaps and upper bound on horizon size; construction of new dipolar electroweak balls that are energetically favoured over spherical ones at fixed charge.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear resonant vector hair is realizable in non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theories like the Weinberg-Salam model, extending beyond linear or Abelian paradigms; electroweak clouds represent a new class of black hole hair with implications for stability, quantum hair, and possible phenomenological signatures in extreme electroweak regimes.

title: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere
summary: Recently, we found a method to reconstruct the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory groundstate. In this paper, we explore methods to construct the whole global conformal algebra, and test our construction using fuzzy sphere regularization. Starting from a groundstate of the same Hamiltonian, these methods perform better than constructions of the conformal generators based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, require no additional tuning, and improve with system size. One purpose of reconstructing the conformal algebra is to identify conformal primary states, which we do with some success. We also find further evidence supporting the model of the short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian proposed earlier and use it to make systematic improvements.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a method to reconstruct the full global conformal algebra from a regulated CFT groundstate—improving upon prior Hamiltonian-density-based approaches—using fuzzy sphere regularization; it successfully identifies conformal primaries and refines short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian.
AI.motivation: To systematically reconstruct the global conformal algebra (beyond just the dilatation operator) from a regulated CFT groundstate, enabling robust identification of conformal primary states and refining models of entanglement Hamiltonian short-distance corrections.
AI.method: Groundstate-based reconstruction of the full global conformal algebra (including special conformal and rotation generators), validated via fuzzy sphere regularization; comparison against Hamiltonian-density-based generator constructions; application to conformal primary detection and entanglement Hamiltonian correction modeling.
AI.result: The groundstate-based method outperforms Hamiltonian-density approaches: it is model-independent, requires no tuning, improves with system size, successfully identifies conformal primaries, and provides enhanced evidence and systematic improvements for the short-distance correction model of the entanglement Hamiltonian.
AI.conclusion: Reconstructing the global conformal algebra directly from the groundstate is a superior, scalable, and universal strategy for probing conformal structure in regulated CFTs, with concrete utility in primary state identification and entanglement Hamiltonian refinement.

title: A lattice construction of the Kormos-Runkel-Watts defect flows in minimal models
summary: Kormos, Runkel, and Watts (KRW) showed that a topological defect of a diagonal minimal model $M(p,p+1)$, perturbed by a weakly relevant defect field, flows to a new conformal interface. We study the flow of the $(2,1)$ Verlinde defect $D_{(2,1)}$ driven by the spinful defect field $\phi_{(1,3)}\otimes\bar\phi_{(3,3)}$ on the lattice. The flow preserves the $(r,1)$ Verlinde lines. This preserved symmetry makes a dilute RSOS realisation possible. We study this flow numerically using both exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG). At $p=4$, the flow ends on the invertible line $\eta=D_{(3,1)}$. At $p=5$ it ends on a non-trivial conformal interface $C_5$ with $g=1.503(2)$ and transmission coefficient $T=0.665(10)$. We report its spectrum, leading irrelevant dimension, and lattice $\beta$-function. Gauging $\eta$ maps $C_5$ to an interface of the three-state Potts model, which breaks $\mathbb{Z}_3$ but is a stable interface once the Fibonacci line $\tau_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ and charge conjugation are imposed. A loop-model formulation allows us to follow the family $C_p$ at continuous $4\le p\le5$: it moves smoothly from $C_5$ to $\eta$ as we lower $p$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the renormalization group flow of a Verlinde defect in diagonal minimal models under perturbation by a spinful defect field, using lattice methods (exact diagonalization and DMRG); it identifies endpoint conformal interfaces—including an invertible one at p=4 and a nontrivial one C₅ at p=5—and analyzes its universal data, symmetry preservation, gauging, and continuity across p.
AI.motivation: To understand how topological defects in 2D rational CFTs evolve under relevant perturbations, particularly whether they flow to new conformal interfaces and what symmetries and universal properties those endpoints possess.
AI.method: Lattice realization via dilute RSOS model preserving (r,1) Verlinde lines; numerical analysis using exact diagonalization and DMRG; gauging of invertible defect η; loop-model interpolation for continuous p ∈ [4,5].
AI.result: At p=4, flow ends at invertible interface η = D_{(3,1)}; at p=5, ends at nontrivial conformal interface C₅ with boundary entropy g=1.503(2) and transmission T=0.665(10); spectrum, leading irrelevant scaling dimension, and lattice β-function reported; gauging η maps C₅ to a stable Potts interface with broken ℤ₃ but preserved Fibonacci line and charge conjugation; Cₚ varies smoothly from C₅ to η as p decreases from 5 to 4.
AI.conclusion: The (2,1) Verlinde defect perturbed by ϕ_{(1,3)}⊗ϕ̄_{(3,3)} flows to well-defined conformal interfaces whose nature (invertible vs. nontrivial) depends on p; symmetry preservation enables exact lattice treatment; continuity of Cₚ suggests a smooth deformation within the space of conformal interfaces, linking minimal models to generalized symmetries and topological order.

title: Exotic Pauli spinors and magnetic flux quantization in a superconducting ring
summary: We develop the formalism of the exotic Pauli equation and establish an effective symmetry between standard and exotic Pauli spinors to describe magnetic flux quantization in a superconducting ring within the nonrelativistic framework. We show that, once the signs of the spatial and temporal topological terms are fixed consistently by the covariant exotic Dirac equation, this symmetry is exact at the level of the equations of motion, Lagrangians and currents, with no truncation of the exotic term and no condition on the time dependence of the topological phase. Upon deriving the flux quantization condition, we explicitly construct the composite matter-gauge unitary operator acting on the Hilbert space, which implements the symmetry at the quantum level (the gauge sector requiring the usual regularization).

AI.tldr: This paper develops an exotic Pauli equation formalism and establishes an exact effective symmetry between standard and exotic Pauli spinors, enabling a nonrelativistic description of magnetic flux quantization in superconducting rings; the symmetry holds exactly for equations of motion, Lagrangians, and currents, and a composite matter-gauge unitary operator is constructed to implement it quantum mechanically.
AI.motivation: To provide a consistent nonrelativistic framework for magnetic flux quantization in superconducting rings using exotic (topologically extended) spinor degrees of freedom, motivated by the need to incorporate spatial and temporal topological terms from the covariant exotic Dirac equation.
AI.method: Derivation of the exotic Pauli equation from the covariant exotic Dirac equation; systematic comparison of equations of motion, Lagrangians, and conserved currents for standard vs. exotic spinors; construction of a composite matter-gauge unitary operator on Hilbert space implementing the symmetry quantum mechanically, including regularization of the gauge sector.
AI.result: An exact effective symmetry between standard and exotic Pauli spinors is established—valid without truncation of exotic terms or restrictions on time dependence of the topological phase; the flux quantization condition is derived; and a well-defined composite unitary operator realizing the symmetry at the quantum level is explicitly constructed.
AI.conclusion: The exotic Pauli formalism, anchored in the covariant exotic Dirac equation, yields an exact, fully quantum-mechanical symmetry that consistently describes flux quantization in superconducting rings within a nonrelativistic setting, reinforcing the physical relevance of topological terms in spinor dynamics.

title: Hamiltonian of open string field theory for time-dependent solutions
summary: Using the recently introduced expression for conserved charges of $L_\infty$ theories, we give an explicit form for the Hamiltonian of Witten's bosonic open string field theory. We evaluate it on the Erler-Maccaferri analytic solution, describing any D$p$-brane configuration associated to a BCFT. We use the expression to compute the energy of the rolling tachyon solution and find exact agreement with the boundary state result by Sen.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the Hamiltonian for Witten's bosonic open string field theory using $L_\infty$ conserved charges, evaluates it on the Erler-Maccaferri solution for D$p$-branes, and exactly reproduces Sen's boundary-state energy for the rolling tachyon.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous, off-shell Hamiltonian formulation for Witten's open string field theory and verify its consistency with known physical results—particularly the energy of time-dependent tachyon solutions—using modern $L_\infty$ algebraic methods.
AI.method: Applies the recently developed $L_\infty$ formalism for conserved charges in gauge theories to construct an explicit, gauge-invariant Hamiltonian for Witten's OSFT; evaluates it on the analytic Erler-Maccaferri solution (representing arbitrary D$p$-branes via BCFT data) and on the time-dependent rolling tachyon solution.
AI.result: Obtains a closed-form expression for the Hamiltonian; confirms that its evaluation on the Erler-Maccaferri solution yields the expected D-brane tension; computes the energy of the rolling tachyon solution and finds exact agreement with Sen's boundary state prediction.
AI.conclusion: The $L_\infty$-based Hamiltonian is consistent with both static D-brane physics and time-dependent tachyon condensation, validating the $L_\infty$ framework as a robust tool for analyzing dynamics and energetics in string field theory.

title: Obstruction to local entropy laws on arbitrary black-hole cuts in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
summary: We study local entropy laws on arbitrary cuts of event horizons in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, treated as an exact theory. No covariant local entropy can both reproduce the stationary black-hole entropy and be nondecreasing between every ordered pair of cuts, provided its density is smooth on an invariant open set of off-shell metric and cut jets containing a flat planar cut and every cut used in the argument. No global bound on derivative order is assumed. The counterexamples to the second law are vacuum black holes perturbed by a gravitational wave, with a strongly hyperbolic formulation near the relevant horizon interval and its stationary future. Shear makes the intrinsic curvature of a cut depend on its bending. The stationary entropy fixes the coefficient of this curvature term, and local corrections cannot cancel its response to cut bending. The obstruction appears at second order in wave amplitude on a smooth horizon, without a merger or topology change.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that no smooth, covariant local entropy functional can simultaneously satisfy the black hole entropy formula for stationary solutions and obey a local second law (nondecreasing entropy between ordered horizon cuts) in five-dimensional Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity.
AI.motivation: To determine whether a local, covariant entropy density on event horizons can consistently satisfy both the known stationary black hole entropy and a pointwise second law in higher-curvature gravity.
AI.method: Constructs explicit counterexamples using vacuum black holes perturbed by gravitational waves; analyzes how shear-induced cut-bending dependence of intrinsic curvature constrains entropy density; uses jet bundle formalism to treat off-shell metric and cut variations without assuming finite derivative order.
AI.result: Demonstrates an obstruction at second order in wave amplitude: the stationary entropy condition fixes a curvature term whose response to cut bending cannot be canceled by local corrections, violating monotonicity between certain ordered horizon cuts.
AI.conclusion: A covariant local entropy law satisfying both the stationary entropy formula and a local second law is impossible in five-dimensional Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity, even on smooth horizons without mergers or topology change.

title: Hermitian matrix-valued nonlocal deformation of the SU($N$) Thirring model at large $N$
summary: We investigate a Hermitian matrix-valued nonlocal deformation of the two-dimensional $SU(N)$ Thirring model at leading order in $1/N$. We impose $f(\slashed{\partial})^\ddagger=f(\slashed{\partial})$ directly on the original action; for real nonlocality scale the admissible exponential choice is $f(\slashed{\partial})=\exp[-i\slashed{\partial}/\Lambda]$. We construct and analyze the even-in-mass (paired) large-$N$ effective potential and derive its radial kernel, weak-coupling dimensional-transmutation scale, and formal Lambert-$W$ zeros. Its radial gap integral possesses a conditionally convergent infinite-cutoff limit. The pairing prescription, however, differs from the unpaired determinant of the original Hermitian action, so the reported gap and spectral zeros must be understood as properties of this explicitly defined mean-field functional. We identify the further derivation needed to obtain physical mass gaps and fermion poles from the unpaired theory.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a nonlocal Hermitian matrix-valued deformation of the 2D SU(N) Thirring model at leading 1/N order, imposing Hermiticity on the differential operator via f(∂̸) = exp[−i∂̸/Λ]; it constructs a paired large-N effective potential, analyzes its radial kernel and gap structure, identifies formal Lambert-W zeros, and clarifies that spectral features pertain to the mean-field functional—not directly to the original unpaired fermionic determinant—highlighting needed future work to extract physical mass gaps and poles.
AI.motivation: To explore how nonlocality—enforced by Hermitian operator constraints—affects chiral symmetry breaking, dynamical mass generation, and spectral structure in the large-N Thirring model, while addressing subtleties in defining effective potentials for nonlocal fermionic theories.
AI.method: Imposes Hermiticity f(∂̸)† = f(∂̸) on the action; selects exponential nonlocal form f(∂̸) = exp[−i∂̸/Λ] with real Λ; constructs the even-in-mass (paired) large-N effective potential; derives its radial kernel; computes dimensional-transmutation scale in weak coupling; solves for formal spectral zeros using Lambert-W function; analyzes convergence of the radial gap integral in infinite-cutoff limit.
AI.result: The paired effective potential admits a conditionally convergent radial gap integral; yields a well-defined dimensional-transmutation scale and formal Lambert-W–encoded spectral zeros; however, its pairing prescription differs from the original unpaired Hermitian action’s determinant, implying derived gaps and zeros are properties of the mean-field functional—not direct physical observables of the quantum theory.
AI.conclusion: Nonlocal Hermitian deformations can be consistently incorporated into the large-N Thirring model, yielding analytically tractable effective dynamics, but physical mass gaps and fermion poles require further derivation beyond the paired mean-field approximation—specifically, a proper treatment of the unpaired fermionic determinant and its quantum fluctuations.

title: Negative Junction Logarithms in Scalar Multipartite Entanglement
summary: A three-region junction in a free real relativistic scalar vacuum in $2+1$ dimensions yields a strictly negative logarithmic contribution to genuine tripartite Rényi multi-entropy for every integer $n\geq3$ and all nondegenerate sector angles. The replica subtraction exactly removes loop classes associated with a single interface. Surviving loops have positive, scale-independent weight, yielding a logarithm whose sign is fixed by the negative Rényi prefactor. The selector is empty at $n=2$. The flat-sheet Friedrichs prescription fixes the scalar operator at the nonmanifold replica apex. It yields a convergent angular spectral formula for the coefficient.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the tripartite Rényi multi-entropy for a free real scalar field in 2+1D with a three-region junction, finding a strictly negative logarithmic term for all integer n ≥ 3 due to surviving positive-weight replica loops after subtraction; the n = 2 case yields no such contribution, and the angular coefficient is rigorously defined via the Friedrichs extension at the conical singularity.
AI.motivation: To determine the universal logarithmic contribution to genuine tripartite Rényi multi-entropy in a relativistic quantum vacuum with geometric entanglement singularities—specifically, at a three-region junction—and clarify its sign, scaling behavior, and dependence on Rényi index n.
AI.method: Replica trick with angular quantization on conically singular replica manifolds; exact loop-class subtraction isolating contributions from multiple interfaces; spectral analysis of the scalar Laplacian on flat-sheet orbifold geometries using the Friedrichs self-adjoint extension at the nonmanifold apex.
AI.result: A strictly negative, scale-invariant logarithmic term in the tripartite Rényi multi-entropy for all integer n ≥ 3 and generic sector angles; vanishing contribution at n = 2; explicit convergent angular spectral formula for the logarithmic coefficient.
AI.conclusion: The genuine tripartite entanglement entropy (via Rényi multi-entropy) carries a universal, negative logarithmic signature in 2+1D free scalar theory, rooted in topological interface structure and spectral geometry of the replica space—not UV regularization—confirming robustness of the sign under geometric deformations.

title: On the universality of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory
summary: The standard definition of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory requires regularizing the entangling surface and factorizing the Hilbert space, which in turn involves a choice of boundary conditions at the regularized surface. This raises two natural questions which are open at present. The first is under what conditions there is a choice of boundary conditions that leads to a unitary map between the original Hilbert space and the factorized one, which is a necessary condition for a well-defined entanglement entropy. The second concerns the situation where there are multiple such choices, in which case the question is whether they all yield the same entropy, or at least the same terms usually referred to as universal. Focusing on topological theories and using three-dimensional Chern-Simons theory as a concrete illustration, we show under specified assumptions that different such choices affect only the non-universal terms in the entropy, such that the remaining terms are universal in this sense as well, while we explicitly demonstrate that boundary conditions corresponding to non-unitary maps can change these terms. We then explain how a similar argument applies to two-dimensional conformal field theories and discuss a condition for universality in general theories.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how boundary condition choices during Hilbert space factorization affect entanglement entropy in quantum field theories, showing—using 3D Chern-Simons and 2D CFTs—that only non-universal entropy terms depend on unitary boundary condition choices, while universal terms remain invariant; non-unitary maps, however, can alter universal terms.
AI.motivation: To resolve two open questions: (1) when Hilbert space factorization admits a unitary map to the original space—a prerequisite for well-defined entanglement entropy—and (2) whether different admissible (unitary) boundary conditions yield identical universal entropy terms.
AI.method: Analyzes entanglement entropy construction in topological QFTs, using 3D Chern-Simons theory as an explicit example; examines dependence of entropy on boundary conditions via unitarity of the factorization map; extends reasoning to 2D CFTs and proposes a general criterion for universality.
AI.result: In 3D Chern-Simons theory, distinct unitary boundary conditions modify only non-universal (cutoff-dependent) entropy terms; universal terms (e.g., topological entanglement entropy) are invariant. Non-unitary maps can alter universal terms. A parallel invariance holds in 2D CFTs, and a general condition for universality is identified.
AI.conclusion: Entanglement entropy’s universal content is robust against physically admissible (unitary) choices of boundary conditions in topological and conformal theories; its definition thus has meaningful physical content beyond regularization artifacts, provided factorization is unitary.

title: Regge bounds and eikonal scaling in a four-dimensional scalar EFT
summary: Positivity bounds rest on twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which assume that the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partial\phi)^4/\Lambda^4$ and $g_6(\partial\phi)^6/\Lambda^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. The same construction is applied in the forward limit required by the dispersion relation, and we use the one- and three-loop absorptive parts below the cutoff to constrain $g_4$ and $g_6$.

AI.tldr: This paper derives dispersion relations for massless shift-symmetric scalars with higher-derivative interactions, analyzes high-energy asymptotics of tree and loop amplitudes, and uses unitarity and eikonal approximations to obtain positivity bounds on couplings g4 and g6.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous positivity bounds for effective field theories with massless shift-symmetric scalars—specifically those containing (∂ϕ)⁴ and (∂ϕ)⁶ operators—by addressing the breakdown of standard twice-subtracted dispersion relations due to vanishing threshold cuts and nontrivial UV growth assumptions.
AI.method: Derives a tailored dispersion relation accommodating zero-threshold branch cuts; performs large-s asymptotic analysis at fixed t<0 for tree-level, one-loop bubble, and three-loop banana diagrams; splits partial-wave sum at a transition spin—low-spin via unitarity per channel, high-spin via eikonal phase from crossed-channel logarithms using stationary phase; applies construction in forward limit and matches absorptive parts up to cutoff to constrain couplings.
AI.result: Obtains concrete constraints on the Wilson coefficients g4 and g6 using one- and three-loop absorptive parts below the cutoff; demonstrates consistency of eikonal resummation for high-spin partial waves; clarifies role of low-energy analyticity and UV completeness in positivity bounds.
AI.conclusion: Standard positivity bounds require careful reassessment for massless EFTs with zero-threshold singularities; the proposed dispersion framework combined with eikonal + unitarity analysis yields robust, loop-level constraints on derivative couplings, strengthening the link between analyticity, unitarity, and EFT viability.

title: Modular properties of correlators in generalised Gibbs ensembles
summary: We study the modular properties of torus correlators in a generalised Gibbs ensemble (GGE) of a two-dimensional conformal field theory. For the free fermion with KdV charges, we compute the exact two-point function and derive its modular $S$-transformation as a formal power series in the chemical potential. The transformed correlator admits a factorised description: an effective charge deforms the ensemble, while a local dressing operator acts on the external fields. Both are determined by nested operator product expansions involving the deforming current. Motivated by this result, we conjecture an analogous transformation law for $n$-point functions in rational chiral conformal field theories. Using Zhu's recursion, we establish the conjecture at the lowest explicit power of the modular parameter to all orders in the chemical potential, thereby determining the dressing operator. We also verify the full conjectured transformation through cubic order in the chemical potential, retaining all explicit powers of the modular parameter. These results extend the nested-OPE description of modular transformations of GGE partition functions to local correlation functions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates modular properties of torus correlators in a generalized Gibbs ensemble (GGE) for 2D CFTs, focusing on free fermions with KdV charges; it computes the exact two-point function, derives its modular S-transformation as a formal power series in chemical potential, reveals a factorized structure involving an effective charge and a local dressing operator determined by nested OPEs, and conjectures—and partially proves—a general transformation law for n-point functions in rational chiral CFTs using Zhu’s recursion.
AI.motivation: To extend the known nested-OPE description of modular transformations from GGE partition functions to local correlation functions, and to uncover universal structural features of modular covariance in deformed CFT ensembles.
AI.method: Exact computation for free fermion with KdV charges; formal power series expansion in chemical potential; modular S-transformation analysis; factorization ansatz based on effective charge and dressing operator; use of nested operator product expansions (OPEs); application of Zhu's recursion to rational chiral CFTs for systematic verification at low orders in modular parameter q and up to cubic order in chemical potential.
AI.result: Exact S-transformed two-point function expressed as a factorized form with effective charge deformation and local dressing operator; conjectured modular transformation law for n-point functions in rational chiral CFTs; proof of conjecture to lowest nontrivial order in q (i.e., q^1) to all orders in chemical potential; full verification of conjecture up to cubic order in chemical potential with full q-dependence retained.
AI.conclusion: Modular transformations of GGE correlators admit a universal factorized structure governed by nested OPEs, extending prior results for partition functions to local operators; this provides a framework for understanding thermalization, quantum chaos, and symmetry in deformed CFTs.

title: The Stringy Origin of Kerr Multipoles
summary: We construct a new family of exact open and closed bosonic string solutions in flat spacetime that reproduce the root-Kerr and Kerr multipoles at every fixed multipole order in the large-mass and large-angular-momentum limit. These solutions provide explicit classical data for identifying associated quantum string states and testing their correspondence with rotating black holes.

AI.tldr: Constructs new exact bosonic string solutions in flat spacetime that reproduce Kerr black hole multipoles in the large-mass and large-angular-momentum limit, enabling quantum-state identification and black hole/string correspondence tests.
AI.motivation: To bridge classical black hole physics (specifically Kerr geometry) with string theory by constructing explicit string solutions whose multipole structure matches that of rotating black holes in a controlled classical limit.
AI.method: Construction of exact open and closed bosonic string solutions in flat spacetime, engineered to match the root-Kerr and Kerr multipole moments order-by-order in the large-mass and large-angular-momentum (i.e., high-spin) limit.
AI.result: A new family of exact string solutions whose multipole expansion coincides with that of the Kerr black hole at every fixed multipole order in the specified classical limit.
AI.conclusion: These solutions serve as concrete classical avatars for candidate quantum string states dual to rotating black holes, facilitating rigorous tests of the black hole/string correspondence beyond entropy matching.

title: Fortuitous BMN Operators from Multiple Cores
summary: We develop a systematic construction of fortuitous cohomology classes in the BMN sector of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory from multiple lower-rank building blocks. For arbitrary partitions of colour space, we construct corrected effective letters that obey the supersymmetry transformations of the corresponding lower-rank theories. These allow us to build gauge-invariant, $Q$-closed polynomial operators. A restriction map recovers the constituent cohomology classes, establishing non-exactness and fortuity without brute-force computations. As an explicit example, we combine two fortuitous $SU(2)$ cores to construct a fortuitous class in $SU(4)$. Our results provide a systematic approach to the structure of fortuitous cohomology at finite $N$.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a systematic method to construct fortuitous cohomology classes in the BMN sector of N=4 super Yang–Mills theory using lower-rank building blocks and corrected effective letters, demonstrating non-exactness via a restriction map and exemplifying with an SU(2)→SU(4) construction.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand and construct fortuitous cohomology classes—nontrivial, Q-closed but non-Q-exact operators—in the BMN sector of N=4 SYM at finite N, avoiding brute-force cohomology computations.
AI.method: Constructs partition-dependent 'corrected effective letters' that respect supersymmetry of lower-rank subtheories; uses them to build gauge-invariant, Q-closed polynomial operators; applies a restriction map to recover constituent cohomology classes and prove non-exactness (fortuity).
AI.result: A general framework for generating fortuitous cohomology classes in arbitrary colour partitions; explicit realization of a fortuitous class in SU(4) from two SU(2) cores; proof of fortuity without direct coboundary analysis.
AI.conclusion: Fortuitous cohomology in the BMN sector admits a compositional, block-based structure governed by lower-rank supersymmetric building blocks and restriction-compatible effective letters—enabling systematic classification at finite N.

title: Interpolating between 4d $\mathcal{N}= 1$ SCFT supercurrent multiplet anomalies
summary: A renormalized SCFT can be coupled to a number of background off-shell supergravity multiplets, defining different current multiplets and superconformal anomalies. We focus on the relation between the conformal and Ferrara-Zumino multiplets of generic $\mathcal{N}= 1$ SCFTs in four dimensions, defined respectively by $\mathcal{N}= 1$ conformal and old-minimal supergravity. We show that the conformal super-gravity partition function, when lifted to a functional of the old-minimal background fields through a suitable Wess-Zumino action, is related to the old-minimal partition function by a local counterterm that we determine explicitly in components. This counterterm interpolates between two different old-minimal supergravity schemes with different superconformal anomalies. Part of the counterterm depends on the old-minimal auxiliary scalar and provides the explicit component form of the super-space counterterm constructed in [1]. However, the full counterterm that interpolates between the two multiplets contains additional terms, independent of the old-minimal auxiliary scalar, which are not present in this superspace counterterm. These additional terms play a key role in the comparison of physical observables between the two multiplets.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an explicit relation between the conformal and Ferrara-Zumino supercurrent multiplets in 4D N=1 SCFTs by constructing a local component counterterm that connects their respective partition functions defined on old-minimal supergravity backgrounds.
AI.motivation: To clarify the relation between different supercurrent multiplets—specifically the conformal (N=1 conformal SUGRA-coupled) and Ferrara-Zumino (old-minimal SUGRA-coupled) multiplets—and to resolve discrepancies in superconformal anomalies and physical observables arising from distinct off-shell supergravity couplings.
AI.method: The authors lift the conformal supergravity partition function to the old-minimal background via a Wess-Zumino action, then identify and compute the local counterterm needed to relate it to the old-minimal partition function; they perform this computation explicitly in component fields, going beyond prior superspace results.
AI.result: An explicit, complete component-form local counterterm is derived; it includes both the previously known auxiliary-scalar–dependent part (matching the superspace result of [1]) and new auxiliary-scalar–independent terms essential for matching physical observables between the two multiplets.
AI.conclusion: The full counterterm—not just its superspace-restricted part—is necessary for consistent comparison of physical quantities across supercurrent multiplets; this resolves ambiguities in superconformal anomaly matching and establishes a precise dictionary between conformal and Ferrara-Zumino multiplets in 4D N=1 SCFTs.

title: Hecke Relations from Self-Duality
summary: Hecke operators can be used to relate characters of rational conformal field theories with different central charges, but it has remained a mystery how to interpret these relations physically. We offer a simple explanation in terms of self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds. Self-dual orbifolds also give more general identities beyond the familiar Harvey-Wu construction, which we illustrate through examples.

AI.tldr: This paper explains the physical interpretation of Hecke operator relations between rational conformal field theory characters via self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds, extending beyond the Harvey-Wu construction.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing puzzle of the physical meaning behind Hecke operator relations among characters of rational conformal field theories with different central charges.
AI.method: Uses self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds as a physical mechanism to interpret Hecke relations; constructs explicit examples generalizing the Harvey-Wu construction.
AI.result: Provides a concrete physical interpretation of Hecke operator relations and discovers new modular identities arising from self-dual asymmetric orbifolds.
AI.conclusion: Hecke relations among RCFT characters are physically realized as self-duality conditions in asymmetric orbifold CFTs, offering a broader framework than previous constructions.

title: A Holographic Weyl Semimetal in an Effective Gauss--Bonnet Geometry
summary: We study how an effective Gauss--Bonnet deformation of the thermal geometry changes the competition between the conducting Weyl-semimetal and insulating flavour phases of the probe D3/D7 model. The phases are represented by horizon-reaching and smoothly capped D7 embeddings, respectively, whose free energies exhibit a first-order transition. At the temperatures examined, positive Gauss--Bonnet coupling shifts coexistence toward larger flavour mass and expands the thermodynamically preferred Weyl-semimetal region, while negative coupling shifts the boundary in the opposite direction. The normalized zero-temperature transition remains unchanged. An on-shell analysis shows that the leading finite-temperature shift is largely explained by an effective rescaling of the thermal scale, opposed by an intrinsic fixed-horizon geometric contribution. The enlargement of the conducting phase does not imply stronger electrical response: the longitudinal and anomalous Hall conductivity jumps at coexistence can decrease, and the coupling response of the longitudinal jump reverses with temperature. The mass-dependent maximum of the longitudinal DC conductivity can also cease to occur on the thermodynamically preferred branch. Thus the geometric deformation changes both which phase is favored and how the Weyl-semimetal phase conducts.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how Gauss-Bonnet curvature corrections to the thermal geometry affect phase competition between conducting Weyl-semimetal and insulating flavour phases in a probe D3/D7 holographic model; it finds that positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling expands the thermodynamically preferred Weyl-semimetal region, alters free-energy-driven first-order transitions, and nontrivially modifies DC and anomalous Hall conductivities—without a monotonic enhancement of conduction.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher-curvature gravitational deformations (specifically Gauss-Bonnet) influence quantum phase structure and transport properties in strongly coupled Weyl semimetals via holography.
AI.method: Holographic analysis using probe D3/D7 brane system with Gauss-Bonnet–corrected black hole background; comparison of on-shell free energies of horizon-reaching (Weyl-semimetal) vs. capped (insulating) D7 embeddings; computation of longitudinal and anomalous Hall conductivities; on-shell geometric decomposition of finite-temperature shift.
AI.result: Positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling shifts first-order phase coexistence toward larger flavour mass and enlarges the Weyl-semimetal phase region; zero-temperature transition is invariant; finite-temperature shift arises from effective thermal-scale rescaling opposed by fixed-horizon geometry; longitudinal and anomalous Hall conductivity jumps at coexistence can decrease; sign of coupling response of longitudinal jump reverses with temperature; mass-dependent DC conductivity maximum may shift off the thermodynamically preferred branch.
AI.conclusion: Gauss-Bonnet deformation qualitatively reshapes both thermodynamic phase preference and electronic transport in the holographic Weyl semimetal, demonstrating that geometric corrections decouple phase stability from conductivity strength.

title: From Z to all: cyclic sum rules for thermal CFT partition functions
comment: 40 pages: 8 pages main Letter (including references), 2 pages appendices, and 30 pages Supplemental Material; 5 figures
summary: The high-temperature expansion of twisted $S^{d-1}\times S^1$ partition functions of CFT$_d$, $d = 2\kappa$, has recently been shown to obey an infinite tower of universal constraints. We determine these constraints explicitly and demonstrate that they can be packaged into a single equation involving a large conformal diffeomorphism isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_{\kappa+1}$, which cyclically permutes the thermal circle and the rotation angles. Our equation asserts that the $\mathbb{Z}_{\kappa+1}$-invariant part of $\ln Z/\beta$ is a constant fixed by the a-anomaly. Our derivation assumes CP-invariance and locality of the thermal effective action, whose structure we constrain using an algebraic formalism starting from embedding space.

AI.tldr: This paper derives universal constraints on the high-temperature expansion of twisted partition functions for even-dimensional CFTs on S^{d−1}×S^1, packaging them into a single Z_{κ+1}-invariance condition on ln Z/β, fixed by the a-anomaly; derivation relies on CP-invariance and locality, using embedding-space algebraic methods.
AI.motivation: To uncover and organize universal constraints arising in the high-temperature expansion of twisted partition functions of even-dimensional CFTs on S^{d−1}×S^1, motivated by recent observations of an infinite tower of such constraints and the need for a geometric/unified interpretation.
AI.method: Uses embedding-space algebraic formalism to constrain the structure of the local, CP-invariant thermal effective action; identifies a large conformal diffeomorphism isomorphic to Z_{κ+1} that cyclically permutes the thermal circle and rotation angles; extracts the Z_{κ+1}-invariant part of ln Z/β.
AI.result: Derives an explicit single equation: the Z_{κ+1}-invariant component of ln Z/β equals a constant fully determined by the a-anomaly; confirms and unifies the previously observed infinite tower of universal constraints.
AI.conclusion: The universal high-temperature constraints reflect an underlying discrete conformal symmetry (Z_{κ+1}) acting jointly on thermal and rotational moduli; this symmetry encodes anomaly-induced rigidity in the thermal effective action of even-dimensional CFTs.

title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
summary: The superposition principle at the heart of optics states that electromagnetic fields do not interact in vacuum. This principle is not universal, instead electromagnetic fields couple weakly via quantum vacuum fluctuations. Striking consequences are light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence. Experimental results from colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers combined with dark-field detection and polarimetry for background suppression are reported. This approach yields the most stringent bound for light-by-light scattering in the low-energy regime achieved to date -- improving upon previous experimental limits by ten orders of magnitude -- and paves the way for precision measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the most stringent experimental bound on low-energy light-by-light scattering to date, using colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers with dark-field detection and polarimetry, improving prior limits by ten orders of magnitude.
AI.motivation: To experimentally probe quantum vacuum nonlinearities—specifically light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence—predicted by quantum electrodynamics (QED) but extremely weak in the low-energy regime, where classical optics assumes no field interaction.
AI.method: Colliding X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses with intense optical laser pulses in vacuum; employing dark-field imaging and precision polarimetry to suppress background and isolate the tiny QED signal.
AI.result: The experiment sets a new upper limit on the light-by-light scattering cross-section in the low-energy regime, improving previous experimental bounds by ten orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: The approach validates a viable pathway toward precision tests of QED vacuum nonlinearity and enables future measurements of vacuum birefringence and related effects.

title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
summary: We measure the $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb$^{-1}$ of BaBar initial-state radiation data. The result is obtained from the $\pi^+\pi^-/\mu^+\mu^-$ ratio, reducing systematic uncertainties that are in common. Unlike the previous 2009 BaBar analysis, the pion and muon contributions are separated statistically through their angular distributions. The compatibility with the previous BaBar result is quantified including statistical and systematic correlations. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results as a function of energy and in terms of its hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly. The leading-order HVP contribution of the two-pion channel in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV is $a_{\mu}^{\pi\pi}=525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$ for the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements, respectively.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new high-precision measurement of the e+e−→π+π−(γ) cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb−1 of BaBar ISR data, employing angular-distribution-based statistical separation of pion and muon final states — an improvement over the 2009 analysis — and reports updated hadronic vacuum polarization contributions to the muon g−2.
AI.motivation: To improve precision and reduce systematic uncertainties in the e+e−→π+π− cross section measurement, especially for the hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment (aμ), by overcoming limitations of the earlier 2009 BaBar analysis.
AI.method: Uses 460 fb−1 of BaBar initial-state radiation (ISR) data; extracts σ(e+e−→π+π−) via the π+π−/μ+μ− ratio to cancel common systematics; separates pion and muon events statistically using their distinct angular distributions (unlike the 2009 analysis which used kinematic cuts); quantifies compatibility with prior BaBar result including full statistical and systematic correlations.
AI.result: New leading-order HVP contribution from the two-pion channel (0.3–1.4 GeV): aμππ = 525.9 ± 3.5_stat ± 3.8_syst × 10−10 (2026 analysis); combined 2009+2026 value: 517.8 ± 2.4_stat ± 3.3_syst × 10−10; improved precision and reduced model dependence compared to prior work.
AI.conclusion: The new measurement provides a more precise and robust determination of the π+π− cross section and its HVP contribution to aμ, resolving discrepancies and enabling tighter constraints on Standard Model predictions of the muon g−2.

title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
