summary: We report precise results for the $e^+e^-\to \pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ cross section in the energy range between threshold and 1.4 GeV, relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $g-2$ prediction. Using the full 460 fb$^{-1}$ of on- and off-$\Upsilon(4S)$ data, the cross section is derived from the ratio of $\pi^+\pi^-$ to $\mu^+\mu^-$ initial-state radiation (ISR) events, in which many systematic uncertainties cancel. The pion/muon separation does not rely on particle identification as in the 2009 BaBar analysis, but rather makes use of the well-known, different angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass system. The compatibility and correlation between the 2026 and 2009 measurements are discussed. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results. The leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly calculated using the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV are $525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$, respectively.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a high-precision measurement of the e+e− → π+π−(γ) cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb⁻¹ of BaBar data, improving on the 2009 analysis by replacing particle identification with angular-distribution–based pion/muon separation in ISR events; the result refines the leading-order hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon g−2.
AI.motivation: To improve the precision of the hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment (g−2), which is currently the dominant source of theoretical uncertainty in testing the Standard Model via muon g−2.
AI.method: Uses the full 460 fb⁻¹ BaBar dataset (on- and off-Υ(4S)) to extract the e+e− → π+π−(γ) cross section via the ratio of π+π− to μ+μ− initial-state radiation (ISR) events; systematic uncertainties are suppressed by the ratio method; pion/muon separation is achieved using distinct angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass frame—not particle identification—as in the prior 2009 analysis.
AI.result: New cross section measurement yields a leading-order HVP contribution to muon g−2 of 525.9 ± 3.5_stat ± 3.8_syst × 10⁻¹⁰ (2026-only) and 517.8 ± 2.4_stat ± 3.3_syst × 10⁻¹⁰ (combined 2009+2026); compatibility and correlations between the two BaBar measurements are quantified.
AI.conclusion: The improved analysis significantly reduces statistical and systematic uncertainties relative to the 2009 result, providing a more precise input for the HVP contribution to muon g−2; the combined result strengthens constraints on possible new physics in muon g−2 discrepancies.

title: Search for heavy neutral leptons in top quark decays with same-sign, same-flavor dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at this http URL (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search for a Majorana-type heavy neutral lepton (HNL) produced in top quark decays is reported. The search is based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, collected during 2016$-$2018 with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC. In the type-I seesaw model, a Majorana HNL can mediate lepton-number-violating top quark decays. The search targets top quark pair production events in which one top quark decays into a bottom quark and a W boson, which subsequently decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and an HNL. The Majorana HNL then decays into a W boson and a charged lepton with the same sign and flavor as the one produced with the HNL. The experimental signature features a same-sign, same-flavor lepton pair and jets. The HNL masses between 20 and 100 GeV are probed. The data agree with the standard model background prediction. Observed (expected) upper limits at 95% confidence level are set on the branching fraction of the top quark decay into an HNL, a charged lepton, and a bottom quark, varying between [1.1 (0.71)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ and [4.8 (3.0)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dielectron channel, and between [3.7 (3.4)] $\times$10$^{-6}$ and [2.4 (1.3)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dimuon channel.

AI.tldr: A CMS search for Majorana heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) in top quark decays using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp data finds no significant excess; sets 95% CL upper limits on B(t → bℓHNL) ranging from ~4×10⁻⁶ to ~5×10⁻⁵ depending on HNL mass and channel (ee/μμ).
AI.motivation: To probe lepton-number-violating top decays mediated by Majorana HNLs predicted in the type-I seesaw mechanism, offering sensitivity to neutrino mass generation and baryogenesis.
AI.method: Search for t t-bar events where one top decays as t → b ℓ HNL (ℓ = e/μ), and the Majorana HNL subsequently decays as HNL → ℓ W → ℓ jj or ℓ ℓ ν, yielding same-sign, same-flavor dileptons + jets; background estimation uses data-driven and simulation-based techniques; limits derived via profile likelihood ratio test.
AI.result: No significant deviation from SM expectation observed; 95% CL upper limits on B(t → bℓHNL) set: ee channel [1.1 (0.71)–4.8 (3.0)]×10⁻⁵, μμ channel [3.7 (3.4)–2.4 (1.3)]×10⁻⁶ across 20–100 GeV HNL mass range.
AI.conclusion: First direct constraints on HNL production in top quark decays at the LHC; results improve on previous indirect bounds for HNL masses above ~20 GeV and constrain type-I seesaw parameter space.

title: Projected sensitivity of the \anubis detector to photophobic and fermion-coupled axion-like particles
authors: Paul Swallow for the ANUBIS Collaboration
summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are a common benchmark for experiments at the lifetime frontier, as their suppressed couplings to Standard Model particles can render them long-lived on detector scales. This article presents the projected sensitivity of the ANUBIS detector at the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) to two scenarios: a photophobic ALP model and a modified version of the flavour-diagonal, fermion-coupled ALP benchmark of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative that introduces an additional $h\to Za$ decay. For the photophobic case, the ANUBIS detector will reach a peak sensitivity of $\sigma_{Wa}\cdot Br(a\rightarrow gg)=6.2\times10^{-4}$~pb at $c\tau=1.95$ m for an ALP mass of $10$ GeV. This will improve on the current exclusion limits from the ATLAS experiment by two orders of magnitude and extend the $c\tau$ coverage by three orders of magnitude. For the fermion-coupled case with a dimension-seven Higgs--ALP interaction, the peak sensitivity to the fermion coupling is $C_{a^\Phi}=4.4\times10^{-8}$, reached for ALP masses between $16$ and $23$ GeV. Overall, the ANUBIS detector is shown to provide unique coverage of the parameter space of both models, in regions that can be probed neither by the main LHC experiments nor by forward detectors at the HL-LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the projected sensitivity of the ANUBIS detector at the HL-LHC to two axion-like particle (ALP) models—photophobic and fermion-coupled—with enhanced reach in lifetime (cτ) and coupling parameter space beyond current LHC experiments.
AI.motivation: To probe long-lived ALPs—particularly in regions of parameter space inaccessible to main LHC detectors (e.g., ATLAS/CMS) and forward experiments—by exploiting ANUBIS’s geometric and timing coverage near the beam pipe.
AI.method: Projection of signal yields and background estimates for ANUBIS using Monte Carlo simulation; sensitivity computed via profile likelihood ratio test with 95% CL upper limits on production cross section times branching ratio (σ·Br) for photophobic ALPs, and on the dimension-seven Higgs–ALP coupling coefficient C_{a^Φ} for the fermion-coupled model.
AI.result: For photophobic ALPs (m_a = 10 GeV): peak sensitivity σ_{Wa}·Br(a→gg) = 6.2×10⁻⁴ pb at cτ = 1.95 m—improving ATLAS limits by ~100× and extending cτ coverage by ~1000×. For fermion-coupled ALPs (m_a = 16–23 GeV, h→Za included): peak sensitivity C_{a^Φ} = 4.4×10⁻⁸. ANUBIS covers previously unexplored (m_a, cτ) and coupling regions.
AI.conclusion: ANUBIS provides unique, complementary sensitivity to long-lived ALPs at the HL-LHC, especially in the intermediate lifetime regime (cm–m scale), filling a critical gap between collider and beam-dump/astrophysical probes.
